title: Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source
full_text:
Meta is back with Muse Glimmer: local, agentic, multimodal, and open source!
To celebrate, we are shipping with Meta day-0 support in transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, Inference Endpoints, and other libraries. We built a few cool things and explain our findings in this blog. Check out the demos below for inspiration.
You can find Muse Glimmer on the Hugging Face Hub.
Benchmarks
Benchmark results
Scores are reported as published. Bold indicates the best result among the compared models; ↓ indicates lower is better.
Architecture
Muse Glimmer is a dense 30B parameter model consisting of:
- 2B ViT-style encoder for vision (Perception Encoder)
- 28B parameter text decoder
In addition to the main VLM, there’s also a speculative decoding drafter implemented on DFlash. Usage of this module is optional, and it can provide much faster generation in exchange for some memory cost. We found this drafter to be particularly well suited to structured content generation such as coding.
Text Decoder
The language model uses the following architecture components:
- Hybrid attention: Alternating between three sliding window layers (of 2,048 tokens) using rotary position embedding, followed by a fourth layer that uses full attention and NoPE (no positional embedding). The pattern is therefore (SWA, SWA, SWA, Full), repeated 13 times to a total of 52 layers. This allows the model to retain relative order and distance information with RoPE and preserve information globally with NoPE.
- Gated Grouped-Query Attention: Each key-value head is shared by 16 query heads, which reduces KV-cache memory by 16x and makes generation faster and cheaper.
- Q-K normalization with extra query scaling: Before computing attention, Muse Glimmer applies RMS normalization to every query and key head to keep attention logits stable. After this, queries are multiplied by a scale factor to set the target logit scale after normalization. The extra query scaling behaves like an inverse temperature at the softmax level.
Perception Encoder
Muse Glimmer uses one image encoder to handle both images and videos. Unlike the relatively small vision encoders used in other VLMs, this is a sizable 2B ViT-like model designed after the Perception Encoder architecture. Perception Encoder was previously introduced by Meta as a backbone for various downstream spatial and multimodal tasks.
The encoder patchifies images to a shape of 2 frames x 3 channels x 14 x 14, and passes them through a linear layer for projection. An interpolated absolute position embedding from a learned position table is then added to these embeddings. These are then sent to the vision tower which consist of 50 layers and GELU MLPs. Similar to the language model, the attention pattern consists of three window attention layers followed by one full attention layer. Inside the attention layers, 2D RoPE is applied to the queries and keys.
After transformer, pixel shuffle concatenates 2x2 groups of neighboring spatial tokens which reduces the number of image tokens 4x without discarding their channels. The merged features are then projected to the shared embedding space of the text decoder.
Videos go through the same encoder frame by frame, where each frame is converted into patches (of shape [batch, temporal groups, grid height, grid width, 2 frames, 3 channels, 14, 14]). The processor targets 2 frames per second and caps the clip at 96 frames sampled evenly across video. The processor creates timestamped video placeholders, interleaving text with frame e.g. “Time: 0.0s <|video|> x N” in which the final video embeddings are replaced before the final projection layer.
Transformers
Upgrade transformers to the latest version to be able to use Muse Glimmer.
pip install --upgrade transformers accelerate
Muse Glimmer comes with day-0 support in transformers, both for the main model and the speculative decoding drafter. You can use AutoModelForMultimodalLM and AutoProcessor classes to load the model and the processor.
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM
MODEL_ID = "meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B"
# Load model
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)
model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    dtype="auto",
    device_map="auto"
)
The same snippet runs unchanged on NVIDIA (CUDA), AMD (ROCm) and Intel (XPU) GPUs, device_map="auto" places the model on whichever accelerator is available.
Text-only Inference
After loading the model, you can do text-only inference with it as follows.
# Prompt
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Write a short joke about saving RAM."},
]
# Process input
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=True,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    reasoning_strength="low"
).to(model.device)
input_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]
# Generate output
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024)
response = processor.decode(outputs[0][input_len:], skip_special_tokens=False)
print(response)
Prompting the model with images and text
We would need torchvision to be able to use images and text.
pip install torchvision
Muse Glimmer accepts images as input, as demonstrated here:
messages = [
    {
        "role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "image", "image": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/merve/vl-test-suite/resolve/main/SF.png"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "What is shown in this image?"}
        ]
    }
]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=True,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    reasoning_strength="low"
).to(model.device)
input_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]
# Generate output
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
response = processor.decode(outputs[0][input_len:], skip_special_tokens=False)
print(response)
Multimodal tool calling
Muse Glimmer can do multimodal tool calling, here’s how you can do it. In the example below, we ask the model to call the weather tool based on the city in the image.
import json
import re
tools = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "weather.get",
            "description": "Get the current weather for a city.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "city": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["city"],
            },
        },
    }
]
messages = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image", "image": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/merve/vl-test-suite/resolve/main/SF.png"},
            {"type": "text", "text": "I'm going to the city in this picture. What clothes should I wear?"},
        ],
    },
]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tools=tools,
    tokenize=True,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    reasoning_strength="low"
).to(model.device)
input_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=128)
response = processor.decode(outputs[0][input_len:], skip_special_tokens=False)
parsed = processor.tokenizer.parse_response(response)
Object Detection
You can use Muse Glimmer to do open ended object detection in images as follows.
import json
messages = [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
        {"type": "image", "image": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/merve/vl-test-suite/resolve/main/SF.png"},
        {
            "type": "text",
            "text": (
                "Detect the bridge. Return only the detection in the model's "
                "native object-detection format, with no explanation."
            ),
        },
    ],
}]
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=True,
    return_dict=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    add_generation_prompt=True,
).to(model.device)
input_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]
outputs

title: The first rival Android app store just arrived in the US Play Store
summary: Following the latest twist in Google's legal battles with Epic, US Android users are now able to open Google's Play Store and download a third-party digital store with its own selection of apps. Aptoide, a store specialized in mobile games, is the first to become available. Third-party app stores have always been available on Android, […]
full_text:
Following the latest twist in Google’s legal battles with Epic, US Android users are now able to open Google’s Play Store and download a third-party digital store with its own selection of apps. Aptoide, a store specialized in mobile games, is the first to become available.
The first rival Android app store just arrived in the US Play Store
Game store Aptoide is now available through Google’s own Android storefront in the US.
Third-party app stores have always been available on Android, which is a more open platform than iOS in that respect. However, until now they’ve only been available if pre-installed on a device — as with the Amazon Appstore on Fire tablets or Samsung’s Galaxy Store — or installed via sideloading. Listing rival storefronts within the Play Store makes them much easier for users to find and access.
The change is a direct result of Google’s litigation with Epic, which saw a judge rule in 2024 that the Play Store would have to open up to third-party stores. Google appealed the ruling, delaying its implementation, and after losing its appeal made a deal with Epic for a new global solution to the problem. Judge James Donato expressed repeated skepticism about the two companies’ joint proposal though, and last month they dropped it, finally paving the way for app stores to open.
Aptoide itself is relatively little known, but it’s likely to be the first of many alternative app stores. It’s presumably only a matter of time before the Epic Store makes its own appearance, and the likes of Amazon, Samsung, and other phone manufacturers may also want to put their stores in front of potential customers. It also opens the door to Microsoft’s long-gestating Xbox mobile store.
Aptoide is only available through the Play Store in the US, though it can be sideloaded on Android worldwide. The company also operates an iOS app store in the European Union, Japan, and Brazil, following Apple policy changes forced by legislation in those markets.
As part of its deal with Epic, Google had announced plans to launch a Registered App Store program worldwide. Those plans appear to still be in the works outside the US, raising the possibility that in the near future there will be two different methods to access third-party Android app stores depending on where you live.

title: Ford’s new AI assistant can check your fuel levels and tire pressure
summary: Ford is rolling out a new AI-powered assistant that can answer questions about your Ford or Lincoln vehicle, such as how much fuel you'll need for your next road trip or whether your truck can tow that new motor boat. The app is rolling out first to the Ford and Lincoln mobile apps, where it […]
full_text:
Ford is rolling out a new AI-powered assistant that can answer questions about your Ford or Lincoln vehicle, such as how much fuel you’ll need for your next road trip or whether your truck can tow that new motor boat.
Ford’s new AI assistant can check your fuel levels and tire pressure
The assistant is rolling out to the Ford mobile app now. And by 2027, it will be available through the vehicle itself.
The app is rolling out first to the Ford and Lincoln mobile apps, where it will work as a chatbot that can answer questions about the vehicle’s capabilities or future service needs. Since the app is linked to the customer’s vehicle, the assistant knows many of the details about the particular make and model, including fuel levels, cargo capacity, and towing capabilities. Ford plans on rolling out a voice-powered assistant that works inside the vehicles themselves sometime in 2027 — but for now, customers will have to make do with the app-based assistant.
The announcement comes as automakers scramble to add more AI-powered features for their customers in a race to stay on top of the fast-moving technology. Rivian recently launched its own voice assistant, as did Mercedes-Benz. Other automakers are turning to established suppliers, like BMW with Amazon’s Alexa and General Motors with Google’s Gemini. Meanwhile, cars with Google’s built-in operating system, like Volvo and Polestar, will also be getting Gemini.
Ford first announced its plans to introduce a chatbot earlier this year, alongside promises for a future Level 3 “eyes off” driver assist system. At the time, the automaker didn’t disclose which AI developers it was working with, noting that it was designing its assistant to be chatbot-agnostic so it can work with a variety of different large language models. As a stopgap measure, the company will be integrating Gemini into its vehicles as an “opt-in alternative” to Google Assistant, a partnership that was first previewed earlier this year.
Ford says that by starting with its mobile app, it can introduce more customers to its assistant than it could through a software update. The new assistant is being rolled out to customers in waves, with the goal of making it available to 8 million owners of Ford and Lincoln vehicles, the company said.
“By taking an app-first approach, we are bringing the future of Ford intelligence directly to customers instantly,” Mike Aragon, Ford’s president for integrated services, wrote in a blog post. “You don’t have to wait to buy a brand-new vehicle; we’re upgrading the ownership experience you already have, starting today.”
Aragon said that Ford’s assistant can answer questions from the owner’s manual, as well as offer live updates provided by the vehicle’s telemetry system. Owners can even upload pictures to check whether their vehicle is capable of carrying or towing certain payloads.
But the “true magic” will be when the assistant migrates from owners’ phones to their dashboard screens, Aragon predicts. This won’t be through phone mirroring, like Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, but through “deep, thoughtful intelligence embedded directly into the driving experience.” The automaker’s Android-based Ford and Lincoln Digital Experiences will feature Gemini in the meantime, which can help with navigation, sending text messages, or playing media.
In the future, Ford envisions all these tasks handled by the new assistant, merging vehicle-specific requests with infotainment-level queries to enable vehicle owners to create their own custom system tailored to their preferences.
Ford said the assistant will be free to use, rather than placed behind a paywall or subscription — though the company wouldn’t say whether that will remain the case after the assistant becomes available through the vehicle’s own operating system.

title: Space mirrors could ruin astronomy — and your eyes
summary: Solar energy, at any time of day or night - that's the dream of space mirror projects. Futurists have been imagining satellite mirrors that could reflect the sun's light onto the Earth's surface for over a century. Russian scientists experimented with the concept in the '90s with the Znamya project. The idea is to put […]
full_text:
Solar energy, at any time of day or night — that’s the dream of space mirror projects. Futurists have been imagining satellite mirrors that could reflect the sun’s light onto the Earth’s surface for over a century. Russian scientists experimented with the concept in the ’90s with the Znamya project. The idea is to put a large mirror in orbit and angle it such that sunlight can be reflected onto a specific geographical area for illumination or the generation of solar power.
Space mirrors could ruin astronomy — and your eyes
Astronomers warn that a recent FCC decision about mirror-equipped satellites could hinder their ability to observe the cosmos, as well as lead to permanent eye damage.
Space mirrors could ruin astronomy — and your eyes
Astronomers warn that a recent FCC decision about mirror-equipped satellites could hinder their ability to observe the cosmos, as well as lead to permanent eye damage.
Now, the California-based company Reflect Orbital wants to try this idea again, launching a test satellite named Eärendil-1 as a precursor to a fleet of up to 50,000 space mirrors that would provide sunlight on demand as a service. The 18-square-meter mirror satellite has recently been approved for launch by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and will create what the company has said will be a 5-kilometer-wide beam of light that could be used for capturing solar energy in so-called solar farms, for boosting agricultural yields, or assisting in search and rescue operations during nighttime emergencies.
The consequences range from disrupting scientific observations to concerns over the safety of the public.
The goal is to benefit companies and municipalities as well, with Reflect Orbital aiming to provide a service to cities to illuminate streets at night, or to provide construction and industrial projects with lighting so that work can be completed faster and more safely.
More clean, renewable energy and help during a crisis — what’s not to like?
If you ask astronomers, there are plenty of concerns. The satellite will be strikingly bright, with estimates placing the illumination as being as bright as Venus from outside the beam and four times as bright as the Moon within the beam. The consequences range from disrupting scientific observations to concerns over the safety of the public, including the potential for permanent eye damage for anyone unlucky enough to be using a telescope in the wrong place at the wrong time.
Experts like Roohi Dalal, deputy director for public policy of the American Astronomical Society (AAS), and Robert Massey, deputy executive director of the Royal Astronomical Society (RAS), have warned that the plan could have disastrous effects on astronomy as a whole, as well as directly harming humans and wildlife in affected areas.
Light pollution has been proven to be a genuine threat to human well-being by disrupting circadian rhythms, and can be devastating to local ecosystems and migratory species in particular. But in the case of Reflect Orbital, the concern is not just the increasing brightness of our skies, but the particular dangers to both people and astronomy that space mirrors can cause.
If you’ve seen reports of streaks of white light trails ruining images from the Hubble Space Telescope, then you already know the kind of damage that can be done to astronomical observations from bright satellites. Reflect Orbital says it will work to avoid shining light on astronomical facilities, but hasn’t stated which facilities will be part of its exclusion zones.
Even with the best intentions to avoid individual facilities, the overall brightness of the sky from the planned tens of thousands of reflective objects in orbit would be an existential threat to astronomy. Not only would the many reflective objects create light trails that could disrupt astronomical images, but the background illumination of the night sky would also rise due to atmospheric scattering. The resultant glow from this scattering would “make the night sky three to four times brighter” in affected areas, according to the RAS.
It could become impossible to observe distant objects like galaxies or even to spot Earth-threatening asteroids using telescopes on the ground. The planned 50,000-mirror satellite project “is likely the end of ground-based optical astronomy,” according to Dalal.
It’s not just professional astronomers who could be affected. One major concern is the potential harm to amateur astronomers who use their own backyard telescopes to observe the night sky. Reflect Orbital has acknowledged in its own filing to the FCC that accidentally observing a single satellite through a 12-inch telescope could cause permanent eye damage. That size telescope is “pretty common for amateur astronomers,” according to Dalal, and Massey described it as “quite shocking” that the company admitted to this risk and “extraordinary” that the FCC approved the launch.
The danger of eye damage from mirror satellites has been a known concern for decades, as experts warned as early as 2000 that the Russian Znamya experiment would carry a danger to observers “similar to that involved in looking at the Sun just before or after a total eclipse.”
Concerns over eye damage from the new satellite were raised to the FCC, including by the AAS, but the FCC stated that these issues “are far removed from the space station’s radiofrequency operations and are too attenuated from the Commission’s authority to license communications in the public interest,” essentially declaring them outside of its authority and washing its hands of the problem.
The planned 50,000-mirror satellite project “is likely the end of ground-based optical astronomy.”
— Roohi Dalal, deputy director for public policy of the American Astronomical Society
The FCC further states that the “small risk” that an amateur astronomer is subject to permanent eye damage from simply using a telescope at the wrong time in the wrong place must be weighed up “against the benefits of permitting American companies to test innovative technology in space,” a calculation that is not likely to inspire confidence in the estimated 100,000 amateur astronomers in the US.
Worse still, Reflect Orbital has not shared any plans to warn the public of when and where its service will be in use, meaning amateur astronomers will not even know that there is a potential danger they should be careful to avoid. Further concerns have also been raised that the satellite could inadvertently cause flash blindness to drivers or pilots during slewing, when the beam is moved.
Questioned on the potential dangers of its satellite, Reflect Orbital spokesperson Christopher Buscombe first highlighted the potential benefits of the technology, then said that the company has “engaged in substantive discussions with scientists, astronomers, environmental researchers and other stakeholders - and their feedback has already meaningfully informed the design of our spacecraft and operational plans.”
However, the company did not respond to a detailed list of questions including how it has modified its designs or operational plans, nor as to whether the public would be warned of potential dangers, nor how its acceptable brightness thresholds were calculated.
Buscombe did state that “Importantly, our approach is incremental and test-and-learn. Our first milestone is this single demonstration satellite. The mission will enable Reflect Orbital to test our technology, including the built-in safeguards governing precisely how, where and when our service is delivered.”
The argument seems to be that this single satellite will be used to develop the technology — including figuring out how safeguards will operate — and that astronomers, environmentalists, and others who are concerned should simply put up with any worries while the details are figured out.

title: Strategy sells 1,690 bitcoin, raises $653 million from MSTR shares
full_text:
Strategy sells 1,690 bitcoin, raises $653 million from MSTR shares
The company increased its USD reserve to $4.65 billion while reducing its bitcoin holdings to 840,447 BTC
- Strategy sold 1,690 bitcoin for $108.6 million and used the proceeds to repurchase 1.15 million STRC shares.
- The company raised $653.1 million through MSTR stock sales, directing $650 million to its USD reserve.
Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy (MSTR) had raised $108.6 million last week through the sale of 1,690 bitcoin and an additional $653.1 million from the sale of 6.59 million shares of common stock, according to a Monday filing.
The company used the bitcoin sale proceeds to repurchase 1,152,020 shares of its variable-rate preferred stock, STRC, for $108.6 million.
The bitcoin sales reduced Strategy’s holdings to 840,447 BTC, acquired for $63.36 billion at an average price of $75,385. The 1,690 bitcoin were sold at an average price of $64,262, net of fees and expenses.
Strategy directed $650 million of the proceeds from its common-stock sales to its USD reserve, lifting the balance to $4.65 billion as of Aug. 9. The remaining $3.1 million was added to the company’s cash balance.

title: Bitdeer increased Bitcoin mining output by nearly fivefold in Q2
summary: Bitdeer mined 2,694 BTC in Q2, but ended the quarter holding just 150 BTC after liquidating its treasury earlier this year.
full_text:
Bitdeer increased Bitcoin mining output by nearly fivefold in Q2
Bitdeer mined 2,694 BTC in Q2, but ended the quarter holding just 150 BTC after liquidating its treasury earlier this year.
Bitdeer mined 2,694 Bitcoin during the second quarter of 2026, up nearly fivefold from 565 BTC a year earlier.
The miner closed the quarter with 150 BTC held on its balance sheet, down 90% from 1,502 BTC a year earlier, according to the company’s Q2 report published Monday.
Bitdeer liquidated its entire 943 BTC treasury in February, citing liquidity decisions rather than a shift away from its core Bitcoin mining business.
Bitdeer is among the Bitcoin mining companies that have expanded into AI data centers and high-performance computing. In August, it signed a 16-year lease valued at $4.7 billion for 121 megawatts of AI computing capacity in Norway.
The company also reported $228.8 million in Q2 revenue, up 47% from $155.6 million a year earlier. Self-mining revenue accounted for $168.4 million of the total as average self-mining hashrate jumped 389% to 69.5 exahashes per second. Its net loss widened to $92.3 million from $62.9 million.
Bitdeer’s revenue slightly surpassed Wall Street’s $225 million consensus estimate, according to analyst estimates compiled by Yahoo Finance. The company’s shares rose 1.5% in premarket trading on Monday, after a 15% decline over the past month.

title: Strategy turns 1,690 BTC into $108.6M STRC buyback
summary: Strategy sold 1,690 Bitcoin to repurchase STRC shares as its US dollar reserve rose to $4.65 billion and its Bitcoin holdings fell to 840,447 BTC.
full_text:
Strategy turns 1,690 BTC into $108.6M STRC buyback
Strategy sold 1,690 Bitcoin to repurchase STRC shares as its US dollar reserve rose to $4.65 billion and its Bitcoin holdings fell to 840,447 BTC.
Strategy, which holds the largest corporate Bitcoin treasury, sold BTC for the second week in a row to repurchase its STRC preferred stock.
The company sold 1,690 Bitcoin for $108.6 million between Aug. 3 and Aug. 9, according to a Monday 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Strategy used the proceeds to buy back 1.15 million shares of its STRC preferred stock for $108.6 million. STRC is a variable-rate preferred stock designed to pay monthly dividends.
The transaction marked Strategy’s fourth disclosed Bitcoin sale of 2026, bringing its total Bitcoin sales for the year to 6,948 BTC, while the company still holds 840,447 BTC purchased for an aggregate $63.36 billion.
Bitcoin becomes part of the funding engine
Strategy sold the latest batch at an average net price of $64,262 per Bitcoin, while its total holdings carry an average purchase price of $75,385 per BTC, including fees and expenses.
Strategy’s prior disclosed sale involved 1,638 BTC for $104.73 million between July 27 and Aug. 2, when it also used Bitcoin sale proceeds to fund STRC repurchases.
Source: SEC
The latest filing shows that Strategy has $785.2 million remaining under its digital credit securities repurchase program, which covers its preferred stock, while another $1 billion remains available under its Class A common-stock repurchase program.
$4.65 billion reserve cushions preferred dividends
Strategy also continued building its US dollar reserve, reporting a balance of $4.65 billion as of Sunday, up from roughly $4 billion in the previous weekly update.
The company said $650 million of the $653.1 million in net proceeds from recent MSTR stock sales went toward the reserve, while the latest figure also includes expected proceeds from at-the-market (ATM) sales that had not yet settled.
Source: SEC
STRC shares have also rallied during Strategy’s recent buybacks, retaking $90 on Aug. 3 after rebounding 24% from their June lows.
STRC was up 0.46% at $95.45 in premarket trading Monday after closing Friday at $95, while MSTR gained 0.25% to $100.26, according to Yahoo Finance.

title: ‘Owning the rails’: Standard Chartered sees LINK at $200 by 2030 as Chainlink underpins tokenized-asset boom
summary: Standard Chartered bets Chainlink owns the rails for tokenized finance, initiating LINK coverage with a $200 target by end-2030.
full_text:
'Owning the rails': Standard Chartered sees LINK at $200 by 2030 as Chainlink underpins tokenized-asset boom
Quick Take
- Standard Chartered initiated coverage of Chainlink’s LINK with a $200 price target for end-2030, a 25-fold gain from about $8 today.
- The bank projects Chainlink’s fees could scale about 25 times by 2030 as tokenized assets onchain climb to $4 trillion by end-2028 from roughly $340 billion now.
We'd love your feedback.
Standard Chartered sees a roughly 25-fold gain for Chainlink’s native token from about $8 today, framing the network as critical infrastructure for a successful mass tokenization of real-world assets.
Analysts at the bank initiated coverage of Chainlink on Monday with a price forecast of $200 for its LINK token by end-2030,
"It is the only end-to-end platform capable of supporting the full lifecycle of tokenized assets across both DeFi and TradFi," wrote Geoff Kendrick, the bank's global head of digital assets research.
Details from Kendrick’s note suggest the call rests on a primary thesis: as more of the financial system moves onchain, the assets will need trusted external data, secure movement between networks, and compliance tooling.
Chainlink is currently the only provider offering all of it, Standard Chartered argues in Kendrick’s note titled "Owning the rails."
The tokenization forecast doing the heavy lifting
Standard Chartered projects that the value of tokenized assets onchain will climb to $4 trillion by end-2028, up from around $340 billion today. It also expects the share of tokenized and crypto-native assets deployed in DeFi to rise, reaching $2.7 trillion by end-2030, a 37-fold increase.
According to Kendrick, those assets are more data-hungry than crypto-native ones since funds require net asset value and share-class information, bonds require rates and payment schedules, and stablecoins require reserve attestations. Each of those needs routes back to an oracle.
Chainlink already secures much of that value, Standard Chartered asserted. Its total value secured stands above $110 billion, spanning roughly 70% of oracle-dependent value across DeFi globally and more than 80% on Ethereum, with over $32 trillion in transaction value enabled to date, according to the note.
Where the fees come from
Standard Chartered expects Chainlink's fee generation to scale about 25 times between now and end-2030, split across its oracle business, which currently dominates, and its cross-chain and interoperability lines.
Chainlink's Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol ranks second by volume, but the bank noted that more than $7 billion in token value migrated to CCIP after a $292 million cyberattack on a LayerZero bridge in April 2026. Quarterly CCIP volume reached $4.9 billion in the second quarter, up 353% year over year.
Assuming a linear relationship between activity, fees, and token price, that 25-fold fee expansion underpins the 25-fold LINK forecast, outpacing both ether and bitcoin over the horizon, Kendrick said.
DeFi still drives the bulk of fees, with Aave V3 alone accounting for 44% of Chainlink's total value secured. Standard Chartered expects the balance to tilt toward traditional finance as tokenization scales.
The bank also flagged the Chainlink Reserve, a fund that converts network fees into LINK. It holds around 5 million LINK worth roughly $40 million, and about two-thirds of fees are estimated to have flowed into it since it went live, according to Standard Chartered's estimate.
The institutional roster and the risks
Kendrick’s read of the tokenization sector pins Chainlink's traction with traditional finance anchors to its growth forecast.
Institutions already using its services include Swift, DTCC, Euroclear, JPMorgan, Mastercard, UBS, Fidelity, and S&P Global, the note said. Chainlink notably integrated Swift messaging with UBS last year to streamline tokenized fund workflows.
Despite optimism toward Chainlink’s position, Kendrick named three risks to the view.
A slower-than-expected pace of institutional tokenization, competition from specialist providers in individual product categories, and technical or configuration failures that could damage confidence in the platform, the analyst opined.
The Block's price page shows LINK traded around $8.31 on Aug. 10, near the level Standard Chartered cited as its starting point.

full_text:
Michael Saylor's Strategy sells another 1,690 BTC as USD reserve hits $4.65 billion
Quick Take
- Strategy has sold 1,690 BTC for approximately $108.6 million, cutting its total holdings to 840,447 BTC.
- Proceeds from the sales were used to repurchase STRC preferred stock.
We'd love your feedback.
Bitcoin treasury company Strategy sold 1,690 BTC for approximately $108.6 million between Aug. 3 and Aug. 9 at an average price of $64,262 per bitcoin, according to an 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday.
Strategy has therefore reduced its total holdings to 840,447 BTC — worth around $54.7 billion — bought at an average price of $75,385 per bitcoin for a total cost of around $63.4 billion, including fees and expenses.
The firm also sold 6,585,682 MSTR shares for $653.1 million last week, with $22 billion remaining under that at-the-market program, according to the firm.
Proceeds from the sales were used to fund repurchases of 1,152,020 shares in STRC preferred stock and to replenish its USD reserve by $650 million to $4.65 billion as of Aug. 9.
Strategy's holdings still account for around 4% of bitcoin's 21 million supply cap, but carry around $8.7 billion of paper losses at current prices.
Bitcoin traded flat on Monday immediately following the filing, per The Block's BTC price page. MSTR shares are currently up 0.2% in pre-market trading.
'Doing ₿usiness'
Strategy co-founder and Executive Chairman Michael Saylor posted another Strategy bitcoin tracker chart to X on Sunday with the caption "Doing ₿usiness." Saylor's regular Sunday posts have historically been used to telegraph acquisition announcements in advance, but have become more cryptic in recent weeks as the firm's strategy has varied.
Amid Strategy's continued bitcoin sales, Saylor cleared the air on his personal stash last week, contrasting his own preference with company's updated stance.
"When I say 'Never Sell Your Bitcoin,' I speak as one saver to another. I have never sold mine," Saylor wrote in a post to X. "Not one satoshi. Strategy is a public company, not my wallet."
Under its new Digital Credit Capital Framework, Strategy restricted its USD reserve to preferred stock dividends and interest payments, and authorized a $1 billion repurchase program for its digital credit securities, initially prioritizing STRC. It also approved a $1 billion common stock buyback and later expanded its BTC Monetization Program to allow up to $5 billion in bitcoin sales to fund its reserve, dividends, interest payments, and securities repurchases under the framework.
STRC has risen from below $75 in late June back above $95 as the company seeks to return the stock toward its $100 par value.
DATs in the doldrums
Per Bitcoin Treasuries data, 196 public companies have adopted some form of bitcoin acquisition model. Tether-backed Twenty One, Metaplanet, MARA, and Adam Back and Cantor Fitzgerald-backed Bitcoin Standard Treasury Company make up the rest of the top five, with 43,514 BTC, 43,000 BTC, 35,377 BTC, and 30,021 BTC, respectively.
However, the cohort's shares are down significantly from their summer 2025 peaks as their market cap-to-net asset value ratios sharply contracted. MSTR itself is still down around 78%, for example, with an enterprise mNAV of 1.07, according to the firm.
Strategy's stock gained 3.3% last week, closing on Friday at $100.01, according to The Block's MSTR price page. Bitcoin rose 2.4% during the same period.

title: Strategy Sells $109M in Bitcoin as Dollar Reserve Tops $4.6B
summary: All of the proceeds went into a $109 million STRC buyback, while the company sold six times as much again in its own stock.
full_text:
In brief
- Strategy sold 1,690 BTC for $108.6 million in the week to Aug 9, leaving 840,447 coins in its treasury.
- All of the proceeds funded a $108.6 million STRC buyback, its third under a $1 billion program.
- Separate sales of $653.1 million of common stock lifted the dollar reserve to $4.65 billion.
Michael Saylor's Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy sold 1,690 BTC for $108.6 million in the week to Aug 9, according to an 8-K filed Monday, cutting its Bitcoin stack to 840,447 BTC from the 842,138 held a week earlier. The coins went at an average of $64,262, net of fees.
The sales leave Strategy with an aggregate cost basis of $63.36 billion, or $75,385 per Bitcoin—$11,123 more than this week's coins fetched.
Every dollar went into buying back preferred stock. Strategy repurchased 1,152,020 STRC shares for $108.6 million, matching the sale proceeds exactly, in its third buyback under the $1 billion Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program announced June 29. That leaves $785.2 million of authorization. A week earlier, half the Bitcoin proceeds had funded preferred dividends and half an $81 million buyback.
The larger transaction was in equity. Strategy sold 6,585,682 common shares for $653.1 million net, more than double the 3,011,361 it sold the previous week, directing $650 million into its dollar reserve and $3.1 million to cash. The reserve stood at $4.65 billion as of Aug 9, up from $4 billion.
Strategy's capital framework
Strategy broke with its long-held "never sell" stance at the end of May, disposing of 32 BTC for $2.5 million to fund preferred distributions, its first sale since December 2022. A capital framework unveiled in June set out when it would sell, allowing up to $1.25 billion of disposals.
With this week's sale, the company has used about $429 million of that capacity, counting $216 million in July and last week's $104.7 million, and excluding the 32 BTC that preceded the framework.
The firm has not bought Bitcoin since June, building its dollar reserve against $1.76 billion in annual dividend obligations largely by selling stock. Its holdings now sit 6,916 BTC below the 847,363 peak reached in June, a reduction of 0.8%.
At around $65,100, where Bitcoin traded Monday morning, up 0.4% on the day per CoinGecko data, the stack is worth roughly $54.6 billion against the $63.36 billion Strategy paid for it. The company overhauled its investor metrics in July, making "net Bitcoin per share" the centerpiece—the holdings left for common shareholders once debt and preferred claims are stripped out.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Draw $854M Over Five Days as Rate-Hike Bets Fade
summary: Daily totals shrank as the week wore on, and analysts are split on whether the return of institutional money marks a genuine turn.
full_text:
In brief
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded five straight sessions of net inflows last week, totaling $853.5 million, according to SoSoValue.
- Around $690 million of that went into BlackRock's IBIT, about 80% of the week's total.
- Bitcoin traded at around $65,000 Monday morning, some 48% below its October 2025 record, according to CoinGecko.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $853.5 million across five consecutive sessions last week, SoSoValue data shows, after a $61.5 million net outflow the week before, lifting cumulative net inflows since launch to $52.18 billion.
Around $690 million came through BlackRock's IBIT, about 80% of the week's total, according to Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at Algoz Technologies. On Friday alone, IBIT drew $86.7 million and Fidelity's FBTC $41 million, while Invesco's BTCO shed $19.4 million and VanEck's HODL lost $10.6 million.
Momentum eased into the weekend, with daily inflows slipping from $128.7 million on Thursday to $98.9 million on Friday. The funds closed the week holding $79.5 billion, about 6.1% of Bitcoin's market capitalization.
"It shows that after the AI craze briefly entered a pullback period, institutional funds have started buying Bitcoin again," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt, adding that the flows likely combine portfolio rebalancing with a degree of basis trading.
The macro read
Sun pointed to weakening U.S. employment data and falling rate-hike expectations as the more important catalysts. Employers cut 23,000 jobs in July against forecasts for a 95,000 gain, Friday figures revealed, with Bitcoin in a death cross as its 50-day moving average remained below its 200-day. CME FedWatch odds of a September hike fell to 40% from 55% on Friday, rising to 46% Monday.
Softening AI-linked equities have loosened the pull on global risk capital, Sun said, sending money toward less crowded assets. He identified $60,000 to $61,000 as support the market has repeatedly tested.
He cautioned against reading the week as a turn. The inflows are "not enough to support a trend reversal," Sun said, noting that hike odds have not disappeared and long-dated Treasury yields remain elevated.
CoinShares struck a warmer note. "Our view remains that the cycle lows are probably now behind us," head of research James Butterfill wrote in an update on Friday, while cautioning that "this does not imply an immediate return to strong upside." He expects Bitcoin to trade range-bound for two to three months, potentially toward $80,000. Bitcoin traded at around $65,100 Monday morning, up 0.4% on the day according to CoinGecko data.
Butterfill cited three consecutive weeks of whale accumulation after some $40 billion of whale selling since October 2025, alongside $1.05 billion of inflows into digital asset investment products globally last week, a broader measure than U.S. Bitcoin ETFs alone and a fifth straight positive week. That pattern "increasingly resembles capitulation followed by early re-accumulation," he wrote. A move toward $100,000 would require "a clearer deterioration in employment data and a more meaningful reduction in rate expectations," he added.
The Coldcard theory
Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas floated a different explanation. IBIT, FBTC and several others have taken money every day since the Coldcard exploit began draining Bitcoin from air-gapped wallets, he tweeted, "making it hard not to see causation in the correlation." He called it the third-best week since October, and said it "would be ironic, but somehow on brand" if a theft from cold storage marked the start of the next run.
Decrypt reported this month that exchange deposits made up of sub-10 BTC transfers hit 7,300 BTC on July 31, the most since February, with CryptoQuant saying holders appeared to be moving coins for safety while noting the connection was not certain.
What could break the range
Wundke called it the funds' strongest week since April and said investors are treating current prices as a "bottom buying" opportunity. He sees little shifting before mid-September, when the Clarity Act gets another window and the Fed next meets, and doubts Republicans can find the votes in time. Traders are marginally less pessimistic, with Polymarket users pricing the bill's chances of becoming law this year at 21% on Monday, up from the 14% Butterfill cited on August 6.
Both looked to the Middle East instead. "Any realistic Iran peace deal would dampen inflation fears and very much temper the mood for rate rises," Wundke said, calling that the likelier catalyst for a market he described as oversold. For now, he added, it "mostly feels like 'Groundhog Day,'" with holiday malaise keeping volumes thin.

title: Archer shares surge after Boeing stake, electric aircraft subsidiary deal
summary: Boeing is selling three of its subsidiaries to Archer Aviation in exchange for a stake in the eVTOL startup.
full_text:
In a move to increase its focus on core operations, Boeing is selling three of its subsidiaries to Archer Aviation in exchange for a stake in the startup that focuses on electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, known as eVTOLs for short.
Boeing's stake in Archer will amount to 19.75% of Class A shares of the company and comes with options to purchase more shares over the next four years, according a regulatory filing.
Shares of Archer surged 16% in premarket trading, while Boeing slipped 0.2%.
The subsidiaries include Wisk Aero, which has been developing an autonomous eVTOL, and SkyGrid, which is developing air traffic management systems for air taxis as urban air mobility moves from test flights to commercial operations. The third Boeing subsidiary being sold, Insitu, develops and manufactures high-altitude drones that have been used worldwide, including by the U.S. Navy.
Brian Yutko, Boeing vice president of commercial airplanes product development, said the deal "allows Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu to accelerate capability development and time to market while ensuring Boeing capitalizes on its investments in these technologies over the past two decades through continued development in our core businesses."
For Archer, the transaction strengthens its position developing eVTOLs and the networks to support them. Insitu also helps Archer extend its military portfolio.
In announcing the acquisitions, Archer CEO Adam Goldstein said, "This is the next big step forward in becoming a diversified platform, rapidly growing our revenue base and bringing scale to our business."
Both companies stand to benefit from the deal. Archer is targeting commercial eVTOL flights by the end of this year or early next year and is eager to establish itself as urban air taxis take off around the U.S.
By acquiring Wisk and SkyGrid, Archer solidifies its portfolio, especially with the autonomous eVTOL technology Wisk has been developing.
Boeing also benefits by shedding subsidiaries that are not central to its commercial airplanes, defense and space operations. Since taking over as CEO in August 2024, Kelly Ortberg has repeatedly said Boeing needs to focus on improving its three primary businesses.
Just a few months after becoming CEO, Ortberg made it clear Boeing's path to profitability would mean streamlining the aerospace giant.
"We need to reset priorities and create a leaner, more focused organization," he said in October 2024.

title: Discovered Materials is playing AI whack-a-mole to hunt cooler chips
summary: Discovered Materials raised $9 million to fund the hunt for more novel materials to build more efficient chips.
full_text:
Chips running AI workloads are too hot: That’s one reason why data centers consume so much electricity and require cooling systems. And, inevitably, entrepreneurs are turning to AI to solve the problem it created.
Discovered Materials is the latest, with plans to use swarms of AI agents to find new materials that can be used to build more efficient integrated circuits. The startup said it recently closed a $9 million seed round from Lightspeed India Partners after emerging from from Y Combinator, with investment from Peak XV Partners and angel investors Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram, and Thariq Shihipar.
Founders Advaith Sridhar and Akash Ramdas teamed up to launch the company, drawing on Ramdas’ experience earning a doctorate in materials science from Stanford, and Sridhar’s work on agents at Persona AI and Luma Labs.
The two have created a software pipeline that uses Anthropic models in a custom harness to generate material leads, and then turns to foundational physics models they’ve trained to run simulations that verify if the candidate materials are actually of interest.
“[Ramdas] was doing maybe 20 guesses a day during his PhD,” Sridhar told TechCrunch. “We’re able to do thousands of guesses a day now by having these agents run 24/7 on the cloud, exploring research directions that he gives them.”
Discovered Materials released examples of hundreds of new materials today, as well as their “Material Discovery Bench” today, which is designed to track how frontier models take on this challenge.
Companies like MatNex, SandboxAQ, and CuspAI have all launched similar efforts, but Discovered Materials is betting that a laser-focus on the thermal problems of semiconductor materials is the path to success. The startup says it has already discovered several materials that match the properties of existing materials used by major chipmakers, but can’t share more details about them.
One challenge is the engineering trade-space: If they find a material that might reduce heat generation or improve dissipation, it might be too difficult to actually manufacture a chip out of it, or its electrical properties are compromised.
“It’s a bit of playing whack-a-mole with atomic structures,” Hemant Mohapatra, the Lightspeed partner who led this round, told TechCrunch. “A material is only useful in the real world if all of them converge at once, which is what makes this a really interesting search problem.”
Mohapatra expects that the business of predicting novel substances will be commoditized as models continue to improve. The difference with Discovered Materials is Ramdas’ deep experience in the field, and the ability to run a lab that can rapidly experiment and validate the candidates — something he says the two founders have already done with several new materials.
When they find valuable candidates, Sridhar says the company will attempt to patent the use of the materials in GPUs, or the process by which chips can be made out of the substance, licensing them out to chipmakers. He hopes that they will have new materials worth patenting in the next year.
However, for all the excitement, we still haven’t seen any drugs or materials discovered by AI actually make a commercial impact. The closest is perhaps Insilico Medicine’s Renterosib, the first drug discovered with generative AI to make it into a Phase II clinical trial. On the materials side, promising candidates have been found, like MatNex’s rare-earth free permanent magnets or new semiconductor materials worked out by Panasonic and Citrine Informatics. But these haven’t been commercially deployed at scale yet.
These techniques may be coming into their own now as AI continues to improve, but it’s one reason why Mohapatra says that he doesn’t believe finding more candidates is the hold-up for AI materials science; instead, “filtering them correctly and synthesizing them is the bottleneck.”
While Sridhar believes that Discovered Materials’ unique data and expertise will help the startup compete with deep-pocketed frontier labs, he acknowledged that the reality is that “a lot of this will involve actually going into wet labs and like making things as well. And this is the process that cannot be sped up.”

title: Google Play adds Venmo as a payment option
summary: The ability to add Venmo to Google Play comes as people are spending more money on apps and games.
full_text:
Google said that it is adding Venmo as a payment option today on Google Play for purchases including games, apps, add-ons, and other digital content.
The company said that users can use Venmo’s wallet or other linked payment methods, such as bank accounts and cards, to pay for subscriptions or tip creators within different content-based apps.
Users can go to payment methods within their account’s settings to link a Venmo account. Google Play already offers other digital payment methods including PayPal and Cash App along with cards from American Express, Visa, Mastercard, Discover and JCB in the United States.
Outside the U.S., the company has also experimented with allowing users to pay for digital purchases using cash at a nearby store.
People are spending more money on apps and games across the world. In 2025, user spend across iOS and Play Store was over $167 billion for in-app purchases, up 10.6% year-on-year, according to a report from analytics firm Sensor Tower.

title: The Outlaw Chemist Teaching People How to Make Drugs From Scratch
summary: Willy Myco has made over 120 videos showing people his exact process for making everything from LSD to DMT vapes. Not everyone’s a fan of his methods.
full_text:
“This is probably the most important video I have ever done,” William “Willy” Myco tells his nearly 2,500 paying Patreon subscribers. The video, posted on Halloween 2024, offers viewers step-by-step instructions on how to produce what he claimed is “100 percent pure LSD.”
Wearing a baseball cap that said “Mycelium Familia” over his shaved head with his brown beard peeking out from beneath his mask, he declares his tutorial on synthesizing the psychedelic over the course of three days to be the “world’s first.”
“It has been a dream of mine to record this process so everybody has the scientific knowledge they need,” says Myco, which is short for mycologist, a scientist who studies fungi, in the video. (He doesn’t share his real last name, and he spoke to WIRED on the condition we wouldn’t use his last name due to the illegal nature of some of his work.)
When the process is finished, the video shows his chemist collaborator holding out a lab flask of a greenish-blue liquid, but no test of the substance is conducted on camera to confirm its identity. Nonetheless, Myco issues a stark if hyperbolic warning about the final product, telling viewers, if it “touches your eyes, skin, mouth … you better cancel your plans for a month, ’cause you’re not going to be able to do anything.” (Most LSD trips wear off after a day, though there can be exceptions.)
It was once unthinkable to post a video on the internet demonstrating how to synthesize a controlled psychoactive substance. But the masked psychedelic educator has released more than 120 how-to videos over the past decade which run the gamut from the attempted LSD synthesis to explainers on cultivating psilocybin mushrooms, extracting mescaline from mind-altering cacti, and preparing DMT vape cartridges.
In addition to his Patreon, which had more than 14,500 subscribers, Myco sells mushroom genetics, merch (in the LSD video, he wore his own branded hoodie with the slogan “Love My Country But Fuck The Government”), and offers consultancy services for mushroom growers. His YouTube channel, called “Willy’s World,” had over 96,000 followers but was taken down after WIRED reached out to the platform for comment. YouTube spokesperson Boot Bullwinkle said it was removed “under our terms of service, which prohibit creating new channels after a termination.”
Myco responded on Instagram: “YouTube is back on their BS again. Channel had zero strikes whatsoever, I post super censored and safe content there … So if you’ve ever asked why I put all my energy into my patreon channel … this is why.”
But shortly afterward, his Patreon account was taken down too. In an email statement, a spokesperson for the platform said: “Patreon prohibits works that provide instructions around the creation of controlled substances or other recreational drugs. We take violations of our policies seriously, and after an internal investigation, we have removed the creator’s account.”
Myco hopes to successfully appeal the Patreon decision, as he pays his team through the funds accrued from his subscribers. “I know I’m a renegade, but I don’t promote the use [of drugs],” he says. “It’s all scientific. It’s all education, in the hopes to promote harm reduction.”
As hallucinogens edge closer to mainstream medicine, Myco is pushing in the opposite direction—away from clinics, regulators, and expensive trip-sitters, and toward radical self-sufficiency. To his many supporters, the outlaw chemist is democratizing psychedelic knowledge, out of the hands of academics, dealers, and erstwhile gatekeepers. To critics, his confidence occasionally outruns his science, and his commitment to secrecy raises questions about at least some of what he says.
Myco, a 38-year-old from Boston who now lives in his parents’ native Puerto Rico, seems at ease breaking the law.
He claims that, in 2002, he produced his own DMT by following a published scientific extraction method. Smoking the resultant hallucinogen was a transformative experience. Psychedelics “became my entire world,” he says, adding that he was dealing with “a really serious depression” at the time, after his parents split and his uncle died. He says he communed with his late uncle in the throes of that DMT trip. “He reassured me that everything's all right,” recalls Myco. From that point on, “I knew I wanted to be part of psychedelic history.”
After studying microbiology in college, Myco says, he started posting on drug forums like the Shroomery, Mycotopia, and Nexus in 2009 but was appalled by their cliquishness. “They treated new cultivators and chemists like shit,” he says. (A moderator from Shroomery says cliquish behavior does exist and can shut down people with new ideas, but they are glad it did not stop Myco “from pursuing his passion for chemistry and mycology.”)
Myco says he went on to work for a pharmaceutical company in Boston “making more money than I'd ever seen,” but it was only ever a stopgap. He says that in late 2014 he posted his first explainer video on YouTube on aspects of growing psilocybin mushrooms, while wearing a gas mask. Several months later Myco logged back into his YouTube creator account and discovered “it had completely blown up,” accruing thousands of subscribers. So he quit his job and created a Patreon—anointing his supporters as the “Trip Team family.”
In mid-2023 he started drawing up plans to brazenly educate people on how to produce LSD. “Sure, a chemist can go get a synthesis schematic and synthesize LSD, but for the average Joe it would look like hieroglyphics,” he says.
So he decided to try to become the first person to bring to the screen long-established LSD recipes shared by legendary psychedelic chemists Albert Hofmann and Sasha Shulgin. To minimize the threat of censure or even prosecution, Myco claims that in May 2024 he found a university laboratory in Pakistan, which apparently secured government approval to produce the psychedelics for scientific research.
Myco months later released a similar video synthesizing MDMA in Pakistan. Then, in March 2026, he published a video of what he says shows a synthesis of the psychedelic 2C-B, also known as “tripstasy” as its effects are like a mix of MDMA and LSD. “I could tell you from personal experience, this stuff is absolutely amazing,” he says. He signs off from the video with his trademark catchphrase: “Do good, be good, live good, namaste.”
Next up, he plans to undermine an incoming US Drug Enforcement Administration ban on the opioid-like compound 7-OH, which is found in kratom. “The Feds are about to schedule [7-OH] tablets and take them away from countless individuals that have been using them to successfully escape opiate addiction,” Myco wrote in a recent Instagram story. “So I think it’s time to film a synth video showing you how to make your own [7-OH] of the highest quality for next to nothing.”
Each video cost tens of thousands of dollars to produce, he says. “We should be able to explore our minds the way we see fit,” Myco said in the LSD video. “These aren’t just substances to me,” Myco says in our interview. “These are sacraments; these are medicines.”
But some are calling bullshit on Myco’s methods.
Hamilton Morris, an expert in psychedelic chemistry and creator of the Vice show Hamilton’s Pharmacopeia, saw the LSD video in June last year and claimed, “with absolute certainty this is not 100 percent pure LSD.” In a video to his Patreon subscribers, Morris said: “The fact it has this green-blue color is something that I have never heard of. Right off the bat that is a bit suspicious.”
Myco soon shot back against Morris on his Patreon. He acknowledged some minor errors in the presentation of the process but said the synthesis route was long-established. “I don’t know if he’s upset that I figured out how to do this legally, and I got it out there,” Myco said in his counter-response.

title: The Best Portable Solar Panels: My Take After Years of Testing
summary: Clean, free power from the sun is easier and more affordable to capture than ever with the best portable solar panels.
full_text:
A permanent solar panel installation can be expensive and tricky to navigate, and for some homes and renters it’s not a viable option. But the best portable solar panels can put the sun’s rays to use in any situation. Whether you want some backup power at home or collect some off-grid juice for a cabin, RV, or campsite, portable solar panels are a good way to get the job done.
I’ve been testing portable solar panels for a few years now, and these are the ones I recommend for different scenarios. They are best paired with one of the best solar generators or portable power stations. I’ll also offer some solar panel tips in an FAQ.
The Absolute Best Portable Solar Panel
There are loads of great portable solar panels on the market now, and much depends on what you need. You’ll want to consider the maximum wattage they can deliver, connection types, portability, price, and more. I go into more depth in the FAQ below, but another important consideration is brand. If you already have a solar generator, it is often a good idea to pair solar panels from the same brand, especially if it has a proprietary solar charging port.
The models from Jackery were consistently the most effective solar panels I tested. Both the 100-watt Solar Saga 100 and the 200-watt Solar Saga 200 generated a relatively good amount of power in full sun and in overcast conditions. Neither folds down very small, but they can easily be carried one-handed thanks to strong molded-plastic handles at either end in Jackery’s signature bright orange. Both fold neatly away very easily with the help of magnetic pads, and the legs attach via Velcro, so they’re very quick to put up or away compared to panels that use metal fasteners. Sun permitting, the SolarSaga 200 consistently delivered around 140 watts, sometimes reaching up to 170 watts. I fully charged the 4,085-watt-hour capacity Explorer 2000 Plus Portable Power Station from around 20 percent in two scorching days with my SolarSaga 200 panel.
It’s a shame Jackery insists on the proprietary DC8020 barrel connector designed for use with its own power stations; most panels come with MC4 connectors and an XT60 adapter (the most common solar charging port on solar generators). But Jackery solar generators often have two of these barrel ports, enabling you to plug in two panels. It’s vital to angle the panels correctly, but the fold-out legs make them easy to prop up. Jackery is now offering various versions of the Solar Saga 100, so you can pick the one that suits you. The latest version of the Solar Saga 200 is bifacial and offers increased conversion efficiency of up to 26.7 percent (up from 24 percent in the model I tested). It’s also IP68 rated, so you don’t need to worry about rain or dust.
Two Other Favorites
If you need more power in a single panel, I like both the Bluetti 350-W panels and the Bluetti 500-W panels, though they are expensive at the RRP. Make sure to look for discounts, as they commonly on sale. The 350-W panel uses a familiar folding design with fold-out feet and a sliding strap with metal fasteners to prop it at various angles. It’s heavy at just over 30 pounds, but the molded handles make it easy to carry. I got a maximum of around 290 watts out of this, and the conversion efficiency is 23.4 percent. The much larger 500-W panels fold down to a similar profile and weigh around the same, but they have a slightly better 25 percent conversion efficiency, and I was able to pull around 490 watts in ideal conditions. Both panels are IP67-rated, and they come with MC4 to XT60 cables.
The 350-W panels are fairly easy to set up; though the metal fasteners on the kickstands take a bit of fiddling. Unfortunately, the 500-W panels are downright finicky. To fold down compactly, it is broken into twelve separate sections and folds out in a double row, so I found I had to wrestle with it to get the feet set up and ensure it was stable. You’ll also need to watch out at the higher angle if there’s any wind, or a gust might just catch them and flip them over. The flip side is that they fold down impressively small with a nice rubbery handle that makes them easy to carry. Setup aside, I don’t think you’ll find anything more compact for the wattage.
Lightweight and flexible, this panel is ideal for mounting on top of your RV, van, or other vehicle. You could attach it to a cabin roof or a hardtop tent too, and it can bend up to 270 degrees. Though no fixings are included, it's possible using adhesive or strong double-sided tape and it also has holes for bolting. It’s thin, weighs just shy of 9 pounds, and boasts an IP68 rating. Conversion efficiency is 25 percent, and I was able to get 165 watts out of it when the sun was at its highest. Now, it’s not really all that portable, in that it doesn’t fold up or have a handle for easy carrying. But it’s a great option for mounting and has standard MC4 connectors. BougeRV also offers a smaller 100-W model.
Other Good Solar Panels I’ve Tried
Anker Solix PS200 for $450: I have tested several of Anker’s older solar panels, including the Solix PS200. These folding 200-watt panels are IP67-rated with a familiar design of molded plastic handles, folding feet, and metal fasteners. They offer 23 percent conversion efficiency and couldn’t quite hit the same highs as the Solar Saga 200 despite a higher price and weight. The reason you might pick Anker instead is the inclusion of MC4 connectors and an XT60 connector cable. Anker has just released some superior-looking bifacial panels, both PS100 ($220) and PS200 ($500), but I haven’t tested them yet. They appear more compact and efficient.
DJI IBC Power 200W for $419: DJI sent me these panels, and they have the same slide out folding feet with a strap and metal fasteners, though the molded handle is only at one end. They are IP67, came with an MC4 to XT60 cable, and produced up to 160 watts when the sun was out. Sadly, you need the DJI Power Solar Panel Adapter Module (MPPT) to use them with some DJI power stations, though they worked fine charging the Anker Solix C1000.
What I Plan to Test Next
The last EcoFlow panel I tested seems to be discontinued, but the latest 220W panel ($299) looks good and is reasonably priced. I haven’t been able to test any Renogy panels, but they seem to be highly rated in online reviews. Two other brands on my radar are Goal Zero and Biolite.
Portable Solar Panels: Frequently Asked Questions
What to Look For in Solar Panels
Portable solar panels come in all sorts of shapes and sizes, but they always have a stated maximum wattage they can produce. While a panel might be rated at 200 watts, it’s important to note that it will likely produce less in real-world conditions. Changing weather, the angle of the sun, the impact of temperature, and other factors can reduce the wattage your panels produce. Even in good conditions, you may only get 70 to 80 percent of the stated wattage, and it will be a lot less in challenging conditions. Solar generators will also have a stated maximum wattage that they can absorb through the solar charging port.
For portability, most panels fold up into a kind of briefcase design for easy carrying. They are generally rigid with fold out feet to prop them at different angles. You can also get flexible panels, like the BougeRV panel I recommend above that’s designed to be attached to an RV roof. There are also roll-up panels, though these don’t tend to be as durable or long-lasting. Make sure you check the dimensions and weight of your chosen panels before buying.
Lastly, always check the compatibility of your panels and your solar generator. It’s simplest to match panels and generators from the same manufacturer, but it’s easy to mix and match panels with generic MC4 connectors and solar generators with XT60 ports. title: 排除中國製！日本自衛隊擬導入國產「Sakana AI」，強化飛彈防禦決策
summary:
為了應對瞬息萬變的現代戰爭型態，日本自衛隊正計畫首度將人工智慧（AI）導入核心的指揮統制系統。據《讀賣新聞》報 […]

〈排除中國製！日本自衛隊擬導入國產「Sakana AI」，強化飛彈防禦決策〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
為了應對瞬息萬變的現代戰爭型態，日本自衛隊正計畫首度將人工智慧（AI）導入核心的指揮統制系統。據《讀賣新聞》報導，日本政府基於「AI 主權」與安全保障考量，將全面排除中國製模型，並鎖定由東京新創公司 Sakana AI 所開發的國產系統，以期在無人機與飛彈防禦中實現更迅速的情報分析與戰略決策。
（前情提要：通縮風險高於通膨！Cathie Wood：AI 資本開支非泡沫，比特幣與穩定幣將最受惠）
（背景補充：Meta 祖克柏公開信轟 AI 末日論：「未來屬於每個人」，超智慧應人人有份）
在無人機、衛星與感測器等尖端科技快速發展的今天，現代戰爭的型態正經歷前所未有的變革，如何在極短時間內處理龐大數據已成為各國軍方的關鍵課題。台北時間 8 月 10 日，據日本《讀賣新聞》報導，日本政府已開始正式檢討，計畫在自衛隊部隊運用的核心「指揮統制（Command and Control）」系統中，首度導入國產人工智慧（AI）技術，以協助指揮官快速進行高階戰略判斷。
確立 AI 主權，全面防堵中國技術
日本政府此次決策的核心考量，在於積極鞏固國家的「AI 主權」。為了確保本國能完全自主管理敏感的軍事數據與資訊系統，防衛省在選擇合作夥伴時設定了極為嚴格的經濟安全保障標準。
報導明確指出，儘管部分 AI 模型在早期開發階段無可避免地會接觸到開源技術，但未來提供給防衛領域的系統將會「完全排除」任何中國製模型。此外，參與該系統開發團隊的成員，也將被嚴格限制必須具備日本國籍，藉此徹底防堵潛在的技術外洩與國安風險，降低對外國技術的依賴。
點名新創 Sakana AI，發揮「編排」強大戰力
在這場國產 AI 的選拔中，位於東京的知名新創企業 Sakana AI 成為了最有利的候選者。該公司所開發的「Sakana Fugu」系統具備獨特的「編排（Orchestration）」功能，宛如一個強大的數位司令塔，能夠將複雜的情報處理任務高效分配給多個不同的 AI 子系統，不僅能大幅降低運算成本，更能展現極高的性能表現。
日本政府規劃，未來將以這套國產 AI 為核心，並嘗試與美軍現役的最先進外國製 AI 系統進行聯動統合。這種組合策略預期能同時兼顧極致的機密安全性，以及達到世界頂尖水準的運算與決策能力。
效仿美軍 Palantir 經驗，年底寫入安保戰略
事實上，將 AI 導入軍事指揮系統在國際間已有先例。美軍先前已成功採用由知名數據分析巨頭 Palantir Technologies 所開發的「Maven Smart System」，並在針對伊朗等區域的軍事行動中進行了實戰投入，成效斐然。
日本官方對此也正加速推進政策腳步。防衛省於 8 月 7 日公布的國家防衛戰略骨架中，已明確寫入「以 AI 支援提升決策速度與精度」的方針；而自民黨在今年 6 月的建議案中，也強烈要求必須確立 AI 主權。據悉，這項導入國產 AI 的具體計畫，將會在今年年底改定的《國家安全保障戰略》等安保三文件中正式確立，宣告日本自衛隊邁入全新的數位化指揮時代。

在機構資金持續湧入加密貨幣市場的浪潮中，一家名為 Bitmine Immersion Technologies（NYSE: BMNR）的美國上市公司，正持續以驚人的速度悄悄囤積以太坊（ETH），甚至被市場視為「以太坊版的 Strategy Inc.」。台北時間 8 月 10 日，Bitmine 發布了最新的資產持倉與業務進展更新，其龐大的 ETH 儲備與質押收益，震撼了整個加密圈。
狂囤 580 萬枚 ETH，目標買下全球 5% 供應量

若以當時 Coinbase 報價每枚 1,928 美元計算，這筆資產價值超過 111 億美元。更驚人的是，這相當於以太坊總供應量（約 1.207 億枚）的 4.8%。Bitmine 驕傲地宣布，他們僅用時短短 14 個月，就已經達成了名為「Alchemy of 5%」（持有全球 5% ETH）戰略目標的 96%。
質押 87% 持倉，每年躺賺 2.5 億美元
與純粹持有比特幣的 Strategy Inc. 不同，Bitmine 充分利用了以太坊的權益證明（PoS）機制來創造被動收入。報告指出，公司目前已將 5,067,309 枚 ETH（佔總持倉約 87%，價值近 98 億美元）投入質押。這些資產是透過其自家打造的驗證者網路平台「MAVAN」進行操作。
以目前約 2.63% 的 7 日年化質押收益率計算，這批已質押的 ETH 預估將為公司帶來高達 2.57 億美元的年化收入。公司更表示，若未來將所有 ETH 持倉全數質押，年化獎勵將上看 2.94 億美元。Bitmine 聲稱，他們不僅是全球質押 ETH 數量最多的實體之一，更是全球最大的以太坊國庫（在全球企業加密資產國庫中排名第二，僅次於持有約 84.2 萬枚 BTC 的 Strategy Inc.）。
總資產破 116 億鎂，獲華爾街巨頭力挺
除了以太坊，Bitmine 的資產負債表還包括 209 枚比特幣（BTC）、1.04 億美元的現金與有價證券，以及價值約 2.49 億美元的早期區塊鏈與科技創新投資（如持有 OpenAI 間接相關股票的 Eightco Holdings 等）。綜合計算，公司的總資產規模已達到 116 億美元。
這項大膽的囤幣計畫，也獲得了眾多華爾街知名機構與投資人的青睞。包含女股神 Cathie Wood 領軍的 ARK、Founders Fund、Pantera、Galaxy Digital 等巨頭，以及擔任公司董事長的華爾街知名多頭分析師 Tom Lee，皆公開支持其累積 5% ETH 的長期目標。Tom Lee 也在報告中評論，隨著 9 月聯準會降息機率大增，預期未來更寬鬆的金融條件，將為加密貨幣市場帶來進一步的成長動能。

title: 微策略 Strategy 上週再拋售 1690 枚比特幣！連兩週倒貨 3327 枚 BTC
summary:
比特幣最大企業持幣者持續倒貨！根據 Strategy Inc（前身為 MicroStrategy）於 10 日 […]

〈微策略 Strategy 上週再拋售 1690 枚比特幣！連兩週倒貨 3327 枚 BTC〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣最大企業持幣者持續倒貨！根據 Strategy Inc（前身為 MicroStrategy）於 10 日向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的 最新 8-K 文件 顯示，該公司在上週再次拋售了 1,690 枚比特幣。這意味著在過去兩週內，Strategy 已經連續拋售高達 3,327 枚 BTC。本次拋售套現的約 1.08 億美元，主要用於回購其優先股。
（前情提要：Michael Saylor：我用 ChatGPT 設計優先股方案，Strategy 靠 AI 融資 150 億美元）
（背景補充：Strategy 優先股 STRC 強勢反彈突破 94 美元！Michael Saylor：目標成為全球市值最大公司）
全球持有最多比特幣的上市企業 Strategy Inc（前身為 MicroStrategy，那斯達克代碼：MSTR），其長期以來的「只買不賣」策略似乎正在發生顯著轉變。台北時間 8 月 10 日，根據該公司向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的最新 Form 8-K 當前報告顯示，Strategy 近期在市場上進行了密集的比特幣拋售行動與財務重整。
上週再賣 1,690 枚 BTC，連兩週拋售達 3,327 枚
報告詳細指出，在 2026 年 8 月 3 日至 8 月 9 日期間，Strategy 共計出售了 1,690 枚比特幣，總出售金額約為 1.086 億美元，平均每枚比特幣的出售價格落在 64,262 美元。值得注意的是，若加上前一週的數據，Strategy 在過去短短兩週內，已經連續拋售了高達 3,327 枚比特幣，這在該公司過去的財務操作歷史中相當罕見。
截至 8 月 9 日，Strategy 的比特幣總持有量微降至 840,447 枚 BTC。根據官方揭露，這些龐大持倉的總購買成本高達 633.6 億美元，平均購買價格約為 75,385 美元。從帳面數據來看，近期的拋售價格（約 6.4 萬美元）明顯低於其歷史平均持倉成本（約 7.5 萬美元）。
拋售套現 1.08 億鎂，全數用於回購優先股
為什麼 Strategy 要在低於平均成本的位置拋售比特幣？文件給出了答案。公司表示，出售這 1,690 枚比特幣所獲得的 1.086 億美元淨收益，已全數用於資助其「數位信用證券回購計畫（Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program）」，在市場上回購了 1,152,020 股相關證券（主要對應 STRC 可變利率優先股）。
此外，除了拋售比特幣，Strategy 也持續透過 ATM（At-the-Market）機制發行新股籌資。同一期間內，透過發行 MSTR 普通股，公司扣除佣金後獲得了約 6.531 億美元的淨收益；其中高達 6.5 億美元被投入以增加其「美元儲備（USD Reserve）」，剩餘約 310 萬美元則撥入公司現金餘額。
滿手現金！美元儲備高達 46.5 億美元
經過這一系列的財務操作，Strategy 目前擁有極其充沛的法幣流動性。截至 8 月 9 日，該公司的美元儲備餘額已攀升至 46.5 億美元（包含 ATM 已出售但尚未結算的預期現金）。官方表示，這筆龐大的美元儲備將主要用於支持優先股股息，以及支付未償債務的利息。
與此同時，Strategy 手上仍握有龐大的回購籌碼。根據文件，其優先股回購計畫（6 月 29 日宣佈）目前仍有約 7.852 億美元的剩餘額度；而針對 MSTR 普通股的回購計畫，更還有高達 10 億美元的完整額度尚未使用。未來該公司是否會動用這些資金進場護盤，或是繼續調節比特幣持倉，將成為市場密切關注的焦點。

title: 年費 120 萬鎂！川普媒體正式向華爾街兜售「優先看帖權」，一則貼文曾讓原油暴跌 5%
summary:
川普的貼文究竟值多少錢？答案可能是每年 120 萬美元！據知名財經帳號 Walter Bloomberg 於 […]

〈年費 120 萬鎂！川普媒體正式向華爾街兜售「優先看帖權」，一則貼文曾讓原油暴跌 5%〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
川普的貼文究竟值多少錢？答案可能是每年 120 萬美元！據知名財經帳號 Walter Bloomberg 於 10 日發布的貼文指出，川普媒體科技集團（TMTG）正向華爾街交易公司出售優先存取權，讓付費客戶能以「毫秒級」速度提前獲取川普在 Truth Social 上的貼文。
（前情提要：川普媒體集團結束與 Crypto.com 合作，64 億鎂 CRO 金庫收攤）
（背景補充：川普鎖喉半導體命脈，傳多晶矽將開徵 15% 關稅、加設進口地板價）
在金融市場中，速度就是金錢；而當這份速度與美國總統川普（Donald Trump）的言論綁定時，其價值更是不言而喻。台北時間 8 月 10 日，知名財經新聞帳號 Walter Bloomberg 在 X（前 Twitter）上發布了一則引人注目的消息：川普媒體（Trump Media）據報正向交易公司收取高達 120 萬美元的年費，讓他們能更快取得川普在自家社群平台 Truth Social 上的貼文。
TRUMP MEDIA SELLS EARLY ACCESS TO MARKET-MOVING POSTS
Trump Media is reportedly charging trading firms up to $1.2 million annually for faster access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts.
The service could carry significant market value: a recent Trump post canceling planned…
— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) August 10, 2026
毫秒之差的暴利：Truth API 正式上線
這項引發市場熱議的服務名為「Truth API」，已於 2026 年 8 月 1 日正式上線。該服務主要鎖定高頻交易（HFT）公司、量化基金與機構投資者，提供毫秒級的高速數據饋送。付費客戶可以避開手動刷新或推播通知的延遲，第一時間獲取 Truth Social 上排名前 10 的高影響力帳號貼文，其中當然包括川普本人及其家族成員的發言。
根據 Walter Bloomberg 的貼文指出，這項服務確實具有實質且重大的市場價值。他舉例，近期川普一則關於「取消計畫中伊朗打擊行動」的貼文，就直接導致西德州中級原油（WTI）在單一交易日內重挫約 5%。對於高頻交易商而言，能在一般散戶看到貼文前的幾毫秒內搶先建立部位，其潛在的套利空間難以估計。
搶救虧損財報，數據授權成新金雞母？
川普媒體科技集團（TMTG）為何選在此時推出這項服務？這與該公司疲軟的財務狀況脫不了關係。TMTG 長期面臨嚴重虧損（例如今年第一季淨虧損近 4 億美元），此次推出最高年費約 120 萬美元的 Truth API，是公司首次正式進軍高毛利的「數據授權」業務，希望能藉此創造穩定的經常性收入。由於川普本人透過信託持有 TMTG 約 41% 的股權，這意味著他將直接從這項服務中獲利。
民主黨強烈反彈，SEC 介入調查呼聲起
然而，這項將總統級政策宣示「商品化」的商業模式，已經引發了嚴重的道德與法律質疑。「這項安排正引發質疑，因為交易商可能因提前收到具有市場影響力的總統公告而獲得不公平優勢，」Walter Bloomberg 在貼文中總結道。
事實上，早在這項服務正式上線前的 7 月底，美國民主黨參議員 Elizabeth Warren 與 Adam Schiff 就已致函美國證券交易委員會（SEC），要求深入調查這是否構成內線交易或濫用職權謀利，並擔憂此舉將嚴重損害散戶投資人的權益與市場的誠信原則。面對外界的猛烈砲火，TMTG 則辯稱，他們只是加速傳遞「已經公開」的資訊，並未提供任何非公開的內線消息。

title: 城堡證券 Citadel Securities 喊盤「現在是買黃金的時候」！五大催化劑激發不對稱上漲機會
summary:
華爾街巨頭發出黃金買入訊號！據《Investing.com》報導，Citadel Securities 全球市 […]

〈城堡證券 Citadel Securities 喊盤「現在是買黃金的時候」！五大催化劑激發不對稱上漲機會〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
華爾街巨頭發出黃金買入訊號！據《Investing.com》報導，Citadel Securities 全球市場情報主管 Scott Rubner 指出，在聯準會（Fed）轉鴿、各國央行狂買以及散戶尚未回流等「五大催化劑」的匯聚下，目前是再次建立黃金與白銀結構性配置的絕佳時機。他強調，這將是近幾個月來最具吸引力的不對稱上漲機會。
（前情提要：英國正著手製定代幣化黃金監管框架，FCA 與大型銀行已展開討論）
（背景補充：橋水達利歐警告：AI泡沫已至！快投資黃金5-15%、比特幣1%）
在全球宏觀經濟充滿不確定性、美國聯準會（Fed）貨幣政策即將轉向之際，華爾街頂級造市商與對沖基金巨頭 Citadel Securities 對貴金屬發出了強烈的看漲訊號。台北時間 8 月 7 日，Citadel Securities 全球市場情報主管 Scott Rubner 在最新分析中，於 2026 年首次公開主張投資人應開始進行「結構性配置黃金」。他將當前的黃金與白銀市場，形容為「近幾個月來最有吸引力的上漲機會之一」。
Fed 轉鴿與中國央行狂買，奠定宏觀利多
Rubner 在報告中點出了五個同時匯聚的看漲催化劑，其中宏觀政策的轉向最為關鍵。首先是聯準會的鴿派定價：市場目前正積極重新定價 Fed 走向更寬鬆的貨幣路徑，再加上美元持續走弱，這對不具備孳息特性的黃金來說是直接的宏觀利多。
其次，全球官方部門的黃金需求正在加速。基於對美國公債與外匯干預的擔憂，黃金作為儲備資產的角色被大幅強化。Citadel Securities 的內部數據特別指出，自 2024 年 12 月以來，中國的黃金購買量正呈現每月加速的趨勢，成為帶動全球央行需求回升的重要引擎。
CTA 淨空頭成「燃料」，選擇權現看漲訊號
在市場籌碼與衍生品動態方面，形勢同樣對多頭極為有利。截至 8 月 6 日，趨勢跟隨基金（CTA）在黃金與白銀的部位均呈現「淨空頭」狀態。然而，Rubner 認為這並非上漲的阻力，反而將成為推升價格的「燃料」。他預期，一旦貴金屬價格向上突破，極可能引發系統性的空單回補買盤，進而形成自我強化的上漲行情。
同時，選擇權（Options）市場也透露出濃厚的看漲情緒。以 SPDR 黃金 ETF（代號：GLD）為例，其隱含波動率已從低基數開始攀升，且 Put/Call 偏斜（Skew）已反轉至今年 2 月以來的最深水平；歷史經驗表明，這通常是看漲情緒正在累積的強烈特徵。不僅如此，iShares 白銀 ETF（SLV）也出現了類似的隱含波動率上升與偏斜反轉現象，顯示白銀正緊跟黃金腳步，重新定價上漲風險。
散戶尚未進場，貴金屬具不對稱上漲潛力
最後一個催化劑，則來自於散戶資金的缺席。Rubner 分析，過去一段時間內，貴金屬的光芒長期被人工智慧（AI）熱潮所掩蓋，導致零售投資人的參與度與關注度極低，這點在白銀市場尤為明顯。這意味著目前仍有大量潛在的買盤資金在場外觀望。他以今年 1 月至 2 月的黃金上漲行情為例，證明散戶資金一旦重新回流，將能迅速轉化為推升價格的龐大增量需求。
綜合上述五大因素 —— Fed 鴿派定價、央行加速購金、CTA 淨空頭、選擇權看漲動態，以及散戶資金的潛在回流，這五大條件罕見地同時對齊，為貴金屬創造了極佳的不對稱上漲環境。因此，Rubner 建議投資人可透過 GLD 與 SLV 等 ETF 獲得直接曝險，把握這波結構性的避險與增值契機。

full_text:
人工智慧的終局，該由少數菁英掌控，還是普及至每個人？Meta 執行長 Mark Zuckerberg 於 10 日發表了一篇名為《未來屬於每個人》的重磅長文，正面挑戰了當前充斥科技圈的 AI 末日論調。他主張，超智慧不應被政府或單一實驗室壟斷，而是應透過「廣泛分配與權力制衡」作為安全基礎，將其打造為每個人的「發明超能力」。
（前情提要：Meta 想做自己的 Google！單季 91 億次爬蟲把開發者 VPS 爬到報警）
（背景補充：MetaMask 推出「Agent Wallet」！支援 AI 自主 DeFi 交易，守護模式防禦鏈上風險）
在全球 AI 軍備競賽白熱化、安全監管聲浪四起之際，Meta 掌舵者 Mark Zuckerberg 選擇了截然不同的道路。台北時間 8 月 10 日，Zuckerberg 發表了一篇標題為《未來屬於每個人（The Future is for Everyone）》、副標題為「通往正面 AI 未來的路徑」的深刻長文。在這篇被視為 Meta 未來十年 AI 戰略宣言的文章中，他強烈反對將強大的 AI 能力集中於少數機構之手。
三核心原則：個人賦權、發明創造與權力制衡
Zuckerberg 認為，人類目前正處於一個歷史的關鍵分水嶺，超智慧將在未來幾年徹底改變人類的創造、學習與創業方式。然而，最核心的問題在於「誰能取得這些技術」以及「我們要把它導向何方」。
他提出了構建未來 AI 的三大核心原則：首先，「個人賦權」是繁榮的根本來源；其次，超智慧的主要目的應該是促進「發明創造」，而非單純的自動化取代人力；最後，也是最關鍵的一點，他認為真正的安全不是來自封閉，而是建立在「權力制衡」的基礎上。
Zuckerberg 在文中嚴厲批評了目前許多 AI 開發者所抱持的「末日論調」。他回顧歷史指出，每一次重大的技術變革都曾引發「人們會被拋下」的恐慌，但事實證明，新技術最終帶來了更多的繁榮、健康與自由。他呼籲業界應摒棄恐懼，延續自由、開放探究與自由企業的價值觀。
Meta 的下一步：讓每個人擁有「發明超能力」
為了實現將超智慧廣泛分配的願景，Zuckerberg 詳細描繪了 Meta 正在打造的具體應用藍圖。首當其衝的是「個人代理人（Personal Agent）」，這將是一個 24/7 運作、深刻理解用戶目標並具備強大隱私保護（如 WhatsApp 般的端對端加密）的 AI 助手，未來甚至可透過智慧眼鏡等穿戴裝置無縫互動。
此外，Meta 計畫推出強大的「創作工具」與「創業工具」，讓即使是不會寫程式的普通人或小孩，也能快速製作影片、設計機器人，甚至讓「一人公司」輕鬆實現商業點子。在教育與醫療方面，未來的 AI 將化身為具備博士級知識的「個人化導師」，並協助加速新藥開發與個人化治療。Meta 承諾將提供免費版本給全球數十億人使用，付費進階功能則會透過動態拍賣機制來確保價格處於最低水準。
拒絕「單一仁慈超智慧」，倡導開源制衡
面對外界對 AI 可能引發就業流失、網路攻擊甚至「存在風險」的擔憂，Zuckerberg 坦承技術確實伴隨風險，但他認為，試圖打造一個符合所有人價值的「單一仁慈超智慧」在根本上是有缺陷的。他的解方是透過「廣泛分配超智慧」來建立系統性的制衡。
在政策層面，Zuckerberg 宣布 Meta 將繼續堅定支持開源 AI 生態，並計畫恢復發布部分開源模型。同時，Meta 將實施獨立董事會來監督模型發布的安全標準。他在文末呼籲各國政府，應避免制定會導致超智慧中央集權的政策，並樂觀地預測，只要以個人賦權與權力制衡為導向，未來幾十年將迎來人類歷史上最精彩的時期。
