title: Meta’s new Glimmer AI model offers a hint at Zuckerberg’s personal intelligence vision
summary: Meta’s new open-weight Muse Glimmer model offers a glimpse of Mark Zuckerberg’s personal superintelligence vision, as well as  the emerging divide between AI users can own and access.
full_text:
Meta on Monday released Muse Glimmer, an open-weight model designed to power AI agents locally on consumer hardware, providing the clearest picture yet of what CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of “personal superintelligence” could look like in practice.
The 30-billion parameter model is essentially an open version of Meta’s most powerful closed model, Muse Spark, which the company debuted in April. Glimmer’s weights are available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, so developers can download them and modify as necessary.
Glimmer is designed to run AI agents that can perform multi-step tasks — like call tools, write and debug code, work with files and screenshots, and execute on a task over an extended workflow — locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. It supports text and images, and was trained across more than 100 languages, the company said.
Meta imagines Glimmer being used for things like managing schedules, drafting messages, and organizing files — tasks that would require large amounts of access to personal data. By processing the information on a user’s device instead of sending it to the cloud, Meta is laying the groundwork for a more privacy-sensitive personal agent. Glimmer is also designed to be “always-on” and able to operate “anywhere, anytime, with or without an internet connection.”
That vision mirrors the future Mark Zuckerberg has previously laid out for Meta. Last year, he argued that advanced AI should empower individuals rather than stay concentrated in the hands of a few companies, while also warning that Meta would have to be careful about which of its increasingly powerful models it released openly due to safety concerns.
In a new letter Monday, Zuckerberg reiterated that vision, arguing that distributing superintelligence widely “has the potential to begin a new era of personal empowerment where individuals can use this powerful new capability to reach their full potential, pursue their interests, and improve their lives and the world more than ever before.”
Zuckerberg went on to list the ways Meta’s superintelligence can improve a person’s life, from providing a capable personal agent that “will work 24/7 on your behalf to improve your relationships, health, career, finances, home management, hobbies, and more” to giving people access to tools needed to create a new business or advance scientific progress. The biggest promise of all is that “everyone will have free or affordable access to these tools.”
But access isn’t the same as ownership. Zuckerberg’s promise to distribute superintelligence widely comes as Meta is increasingly distinguishing between models it will release openly and those it will keep under its control. Muse Spark, its more powerful mode, remains closed-weight, while the smaller Glimmer can be downloaded, fine-tuned, and run on a user’s hardware.
As a result, Glimmer offers an early indication of where Meta may draw the line between the AI it wants people to own themselves and the more powerful intelligence that remains under the company’s control.

title: Sila lands $1.4B Pentagon loan as militaries demand more batteries
summary: Battery materials startup Sila will use a $1.4 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Defense to scale production at its factory in Washington State.
full_text:
Sila has landed a $1.4 billion loan from the U.S. Department of Defense to help the U.S.-based startup expand production of its silicon-carbon battery material.
The loan, which was announced Friday, arrives as U.S. battery buyers, from automotive companies to defense contractors, struggle to procure battery materials that are made outside of China. Most of today’s lithium-ion battery anodes use graphite, and the supply chain for the material is dominated by Chinese companies.
Many companies, including Group14 and Amprius, are pursuing silicon anodes. The material promises to store 20% to 40% more electricity than graphite anodes. The improved energy density could pave the way for longer-lasting cells or smaller, lighter batteries. Both are appealing traits for defense and mobility applications, including drones and EVs.
Sila makes its silicon-carbon material at its factory in Moses Lake, Washington, making it one of the few sources of anode material that isn’t encumbered by tariffs or geopolitical concerns.
The factory began operating in September and, at its current size, can produce about 2 gigawatt-hours of anode material annually. Sila is working to expand its Moses Lake factory fivefold, allowing it to produce enough material for more than 100,000 EVs.
In July, Sila raised $300 million to help fund the factory expansion. Atreides Management and Sutter Hill Ventures led the round. To date, Sila has raised more than $1.5 billion from private investors, according to PitchBook.
Sila has already lined up deals with Mercedes and Panasonic. The new loan from the Pentagon could open the door to contracts with defense companies, which have been landing massive deals as wars in Iran and Ukraine drag on.
Alongside the loan to Sila, the Department of Defense also announced deals with three other companies.
Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian company, will receive a $400 million loan to mine scandium, a rare earth element that’s widely used in lightweight alloys. Niron Magnetics, a Minnesota-based company, landed a $150 million loan to manufacture new rare earth-free magnets for smartphones, missiles, and electric motors. Lastly, the government made an $85 million equity investment in Strategic Bauxite, which mines a mineral that contains aluminum.

title: Archer buys former rival Wisk Aero
summary: The two companies were once embroiled in a trade secret theft lawsuit. Now, Wisk is being absorbed into Archer.
full_text:
Three years after settling a trade secret lawsuit, electric aircraft company Archer Aviation now owns its former rival, Wisk Aero.
Under the terms of the deal, Boeing has agreed to sell Wisk Aero and two other subsidiaries to Archer in exchange for an ownership stake in the company, according to a regulatory filing released Monday. The other subsidiaries are SkyGrid, a digital airspace and air traffic management software company and drone maker Insitu.
Boeing will receive newly issued Archer shares equal to 19.75% of Archer’s shares outstanding immediately before closing, resulting in about a 16.5% stake in the company after the deal, according to a regulatory filing and a person familiar with the matter.
The acquisition is a capstone to a once-embittered relationship between two companies developing electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft.
In April 2021, Wisk sued Archer for “brazen theft” of confidential information and intellectual property. The legal wrangling lasted two years before the companies reached an unusual settlement that not only ended the lawsuit as well as Archer’s counter-suit against Wisk seeking $1 billion in damages, but kicked off a new collaboration. Under the terms of the settlement, Archer agreed to make Wisk the exclusive provider of autonomous technology. Archer also agreed, at the time, to give Wisk the option to purchase up to 13,176,636 shares of common stock at a price of $0.01 per share.
Wisk Aero got its start as a Kittyhawk, an electric aviation startup led by Sebastian Thrun, who co-founded the Alphabet moonshot factory X, and backed by Google co-founder Larry Page. Kittyhawk, which shut down in September 2022, had several aircraft programs, including a single-seater, all-electric, vertical take-off and landing vehicle known as Flyer, and Heaviside, a more capable, quieter and once-secret electric aircraft that could fly and land anywhere autonomously.
But it was Kittyhawk’s Cora program that would end up living on. Cora, a two-person, autonomous flying taxi, was spun off in late 2019 into a joint venture with Boeing. The joint venture was renamed Wisk and set out to develop and commercialize electric, self-flying air taxis.
Boeing poured millions into the effort. In early 2022, Boeing invested another $450 million into Wisk. And by 2023, Wisk was a fully-owned subsidiary of Boeing.
Meanwhile, Archer, a California-based startup founded in 2018, has expanded its electric vertical takeoff and landing vehicles (eVTOL) program beyond its initial plan to build an air taxi network. The company expanded into the defense sector a couple of years ago, raising $430 million round in December 2024 to fund its new Archer Defense program. In 2025, it raised another $300 million from institutional investors like BlackRock and Wellington. Archer also struck an exclusive deal with weapons manufacturer Anduril to jointly develop a hybrid gas-and-electric-powered VTOL aircraft for critical defense applications.
Archer, which went public in 2021 through a merger with a blank-check company, continues to make progress on its all-electric Midnight aircraft as well. Earlier this month, Archer completed a piloted round-trip flight between Salinas Municipal Airport and Monterey Regional Airport as the company prepares to begin operations later this year under the White House’s eVTOL Integration Pilot Program.

title: One of China's workhorse rockets just exploded in flight
summary: If the failure involved the YF-100 engine, there are broader concerns for China's space program.
full_text:
One of China’s most used rockets, the Long March 7A, exploded a little more than a minute after lifting off on Monday evening, local time.
The medium-lift rocket’s payload was classified, but it was believed to be a military communications satellite. The rocket’s liftoff from Wenchang Space Launch Site appeared to be nominal, but publicly captured videos (such as this one) showed that the rocket’s first stage exploded about 1 minute and 20 seconds into flight.
The Long March 7A rocket was developed by the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation and is operated by the state’s space agency. As of Monday night in China, state officials have not commented on the explosion.
Was it an engine issue?
Based on the timing of the explosion, it occurred during the flight of the first stage of the vehicle, likely around the time of maximum dynamic pressure as the rocket accelerated through the lower atmosphere. It’s possible that the vehicle’s flight was ended by on-board ordnance known as a “flight termination system,” which ignites when the vehicle veers off course.
China’s state-operated launch industry has had considerable success in the last half-decade as it has grown its annual launch total to 50 or more flights per year. During that time, it has only suffered a handful of launch failures.
Due to the uncertainty surrounding the cause of Monday’s failure, the significance of the problem is difficult to ascertain. Given the closed nature of China’s state-operated space program, it may never be clear what caused the rocket to explode.

title: Dogs can tell if you're scared or sad
summary: fMRI scans show happiness, fear, anger, and sadness have distinct brain activity patterns in doggy brains.
full_text:
Any dog owner would tell you that their canine companions are attuned to their humans’ emotional state and respond accordingly. Scientists have performed fMRI scans on dogs and identified a specific brain region that processes happy human facial expresses, like a smile, according to a new paper published in the journal iScience. They also found that dogs can tell the difference between negative facial expressions, specifically anger, sadness, and fear.
“Humans are really good at picking up small details on the face, and so are dogs,” said co-author Raúl Hernández-Pérez of the University of Vienna. “This makes dogs very interesting. By studying their brains, we can understand what adaptations have developed to support their remarkable social and emotional understanding of humans.”
Prior behavioral studies have shown that dogs are sensitive to emotion in human faces. Dogs will, for example, choose a box their human has identified with a happy expression over one the human treats with fear or disgust. Past fMRI studies found that an area in the canine left temporal cortex showed a stronger response to human faces compared to dog faces, as well as a greater response in the caudate, hippocampus, and amygdala to human faces showing emotion versus neutral faces.
This latest study sought to use fMRI to unravel the underlying neural correlates of processing human facial expressions in dogs. For the first experiment, the team recruited eight dogs (six border collies, one labrador, and one gold retriever) who lived with humans and were well-socialized. Seven of the dogs had previously participated in fMRI studies and were trained to sit still in a sphinx position during the scan; the new participant, Molly, underwent training using the same protocol. The researchers provided the dogs with a chin rest to support their heads during the scan and ear muffs for noise protection. No restraints were used.
Each dog was randomly shown a series of human faces as stimuli, with either neutral or happy expressions, for seven seconds while in the MRI machine. They used the faces of strangers to rule out any familiarity effects. The resulting analysis showed that the temporal cortex (associated with higher cognitive functions) and the caudate nucleus (associated with reward) had the most activity in response to happy faces.

title: 2026 Subaru Outback review: Great interior, refined drive, divisive looks
summary: The newest Outback sticks to the script; that's no bad thing if you like Outbacks.
full_text:
When station wagons headed for the same retirement home as the vinyl roof and the opera window, Subaru looked at its sensible Legacy wagon and had a different idea. Raise it a few inches, wrap the lower body in plastic cladding, name it for the Australian bush, and suburban families would drive to soccer practice while imagining themselves fording streams and climbing sand dunes.
In giving birth to the Legacy Outback in 1995, Subaru more or less created the template for the modern, adventure-minded, off-road-themed crossover. By the 2000 model year, the Outback had graduated from trim level to standalone model, and it has been paying the bulk of Subaru’s bills ever since.
Today, the 2026 Outback marks a new era in the model’s history. The wagon silhouette that defined six generations has given way to a sharpened two-box shape that’s much more at home parked next to an upright Forester or Ascent. Tall, square, and profusely SUV-like, the new edition won’t win any beauty contests, but form follows function more than ever in the Outback.
More crossover than wagon, the new Subaru Outback is not the best it has ever looked, at least as far as the exterior is concerned.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
More crossover than wagon, the new Subaru Outback is not the best it has ever looked, at least as far as the exterior is concerned.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
Standard all-wheel drive across all six trim levels (starting at about $36,000 to just under $49,000, including the required $1,450 destination) ensures all Outbacks have similar poor-weather and poor-road ability, though the Wilderness version rides 0.8 inches (20 mm) higher off the ground and comes with more dedicated all-terrain tires. My Limited test vehicle stickered at $43,165.
Much improved interior
The new Outback isn’t pretty, but spend a week driving it, as I did, and you’ll quickly care less about the outer skin than the inner capability. The extra height over the 2025 version affords much improved passenger and cargo room. There’s one caveat, though: The new interior steps threateningly close to premium quality, and a new infotainment system and electronics package pull everyday usability and convenience up the ladder by a rung or two.
Climb in and close the door, and you’ll find the dashboard cleaner than before, with climate controls thankfully presented as tangible knobs and buttons rather than the sometimes-lethargic digital renderings of the prior Outback. The only demerit here is the mesh fabric covering the upper door panels and part of the dashboard. This material looks a bit cheap and can be pulled like a shirt, making the pattern askew.
The new interior is an improvement.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
The new interior is an improvement.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
While the front seats offer lots of legroom and adjustability and are very comfortable even on multi-hour drives, the rear seat offers even more space and shoulder room. But the seatbacks do not recline, as in many SUVs. Ingress and egress from both front and rear seats is also excellent. The Limited trim includes heated outboard rear seats. Thoughtful shopping bag hooks and tie-downs in the cargo area come standard, and there’s also meaningful under-floor storage back there, too.
On the technology front, a new 12.1-inch infotainment system responds quicker and proves easier to navigate, with large, highly legible icons. You can also more easily read the new 12.3-inch, hi-res, and configurable digital instrument cluster. Several USB-A and USB-C ports come standard front and rear, and there’s wireless charging up front.
My Outback Limited’s Harman Kardon audio system (12 speakers, 576 watts) reproduced sound better than I anticipated, whether I was piping in Miles Davis, MC5, or Mahler. The top Touring trims include a hands-free highway driving system that bridges the adaptive cruise control and lane-centering already aboard the Limited test vehicle.
ADAS needs work
A few words about active driving assists. Though the generous list of standard lane-keeping, lane-centering, and adaptive cruise features worked well, it was hard to appreciate them because the DriverFocus Distraction Mitigation system’s functions were so overbearing. Look away from the road dead-ahead for more than a second—even to glance at the infotainment screen—and you get an electronic finger-wagging that you’re not paying attention.
Go here to tweak the advanced driver assistance systems.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
Go here to tweak the advanced driver assistance systems.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
With lane-centering and adaptive cruise engaged, the Outback repeatedly scolded me to put my hands on the steering wheel—when my hands were on the steering wheel. And then, when I intentionally let go to try to wake the system up and re-gripped the wheel with the firmness of a General Patton handshake, the system took about five seconds to register the re-grip.
Of course, you can disable the DriverFocus system, but you’d need to disable it on every restart of the car. Yes, Subaru laudably has put safety at the forefront, but I gave up driving with my mother 40 years ago.
Underneath the new boxy sheetmetal, Subaru avoids reinventing what already worked. The test Limited’s standard 2.5 L flat-four-cylinder engine develops 180 hp (134 kW) and 178 lb-ft (241 Nm) of torque. That’s adequate oomph, but it’s hardly brisk when toting around the Outback Limited’s 3,741 lbs (1,697 kg).
The turbocharged 2.4 L engine of the XT versions, making 260 hp (194 kW) and 277 lb-ft (376 Nm) of torque, offers power that the base engine can only dream of (if engines could dream). No hybrid version is available yet, but I suspect a hybrid Outback will arrive for 2027, likely with a version of the 194 hp (145 kW) drivetrain currently used in the Forester Hybrid. For those looking for something entirely electric, the new Subaru Trailseeker is marketed in other regions as the E-Outback and is close to, if not identical in, dimensions.
Both engines pair with Subaru’s continuously variable transmission, which performs adequately in sedate, everyday driving but lurches when pushed and can elicit some droning when climbing long freeway grades and accelerating hard.
For now, there’s a choice of two engines.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
For now, there’s a choice of two engines.
Credit:
Jim Resnick
Behind the wheel
More impressive is how much more refined the new Outback feels when not asked to perform like a sports car. The Outback hushes wind noise, smooths bumps and harshness on the freeway, and seems to dispatch dirt road roughness with nearly the same ease as it does on the highway. Twisty back roads are not really on the menu. I’d save that for the BR-Zs and WRXs of the world.
Though no off-road match for a Jeep Wrangler, the new Outback does everything the prior generation did when the road ends, meaning quite a lot given natural limitations. Both old and new Outbacks provide the same 8.7 inches (221 mm) of ground clearance (though the new Wilderness version yields 9.5 inches/241 mm).
Various traction-seeking features come standard on the Limited, like X-Mode Traction Management, which softens the throttle opening to avoid an initial loss of traction; variable torque split, which apportions more or less power to the wheels with more traction; and hill descent control, which regulates downhill speed so the driver can focus on steering on slippery downslopes. In addition to extra ground clearance and knobbier all-terrain tires, the Outback Wilderness adds selectable snow/dirt and deep snow/mud settings to the X-Mode system.
Thankfully, it’s not an all touchscreen interface. There are plenty of buttons.
Jim Resnick

The back seat has decent legroom.
Jim Resnick

Jim Resnick

title: A researcher bought noreply.net. Companies started sending him secrets.
summary: Companies treat some email domains as digital trash cans, despite the risks.
full_text:
Cory Solovewicz receives more unwanted emails than you. Seriously—it’s a lot more. Since December 2024, one of the domains at which the security researcher receives email has registered 401,796 messages—by his calculations that’s an average of 699.99 pings per day.
This deluge isn’t the regular flood of spam, newsletters, and unwanted deals that fill many people’s inboxes. Instead, companies and other organizations are inadvertently sending Solovewicz other people’s private information and company secrets. Over the last few years, he’s received injury reports from a city government, confirmation of people’s pizza orders, and account setup emails from a school platform. “I get service orders for people that need repairs. I get lots of test platform credentials,” says Solovewicz, a security researcher and consultant.
Solovewicz is receiving the avalanche of messages as he’s the owner of the domains noreply.us and noreply.net, which he purchased in 2020 and 2024, respectively. After originally planning to use the noreply.us domain as a catch-all email—which receives mail sent to any @ address on that domain—to filter messages and enhance his privacy, the researcher quickly noticed that other systems were sending mail to @noreply.us addresses. “I created an accidental honeypot,” Solovewicz tells WIRED. “I had no idea it was going to turn into this.”
Companies may send emails to [companyname]@noreply.net or similar variations believing they aren’t going anywhere, or could not be monitored in any way. Broadly it’s also possible that they may transform a person’s individual email address to send to one of these placeholder style domains if someone leaves a company or deletes their account.
What started out as a personal email project has become a large-scale effort to warn businesses and other groups that they have misconfigured their internal systems and are accidentally sharing sensitive information. Solovewicz, who presented his work at the Defcon security conference yesterday, says ultimately he is relieved that he ended up with the domains rather than criminal hackers or nation states who could use the data maliciously.

title: BitMart 停運後爆提現危機！造市商怒控「資不抵債」，千萬美元大戶慘遭凍結
summary:

〈BitMart 停運後爆提現危機！造市商怒控「資不抵債」，千萬美元大戶慘遭凍結〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
BitMart 交易所的「有序停運」恐演變成流動性危機？據 X 平台用戶 @0xDeltaHedged 於 10 日發布的貼文指出，其造市商（MM）的資金因 BitMart 已經「資不抵債」而無法提領。該用戶更怒斥，BitMart 在宣布關閉前一週，竟還要求代幣持有者將資金鎖定在平台上，痛批這根本是惡意吸取流動性的操作。
（前情提要：BitMart 創辦人喊：沒跑路也不會跑路，社群甩大量「提幣卡單」截圖怒轟快還錢）
（背景補充：BitMart 收攤後提幣延遲，BMX 一週暴挫 81.5%，CZ提醒：交易所關門要收購不簡單）
加密貨幣交易所 BitMart 在 2026 年 7 月 26 日突發公告，宣布將進行「有序停止運營」，並承諾提現通道將持續開放。然而，官方的保證並未平息市場的恐慌，隨著時間推移，越來越多用戶與專案方出面指控，提現申請宛如石沉大海。
千萬美元大戶求救，VIP 經理集體失聯
這場風暴在 8 月 9 日迎來了一波高潮。一名名為 @BeardStaffX 的用戶在 X 平台上發布了一篇獲得高度關注的求償貼文，將矛頭直指 BitMart 創辦人 Sheldon Xia（@sheldonbitmart）。該用戶聲稱，自己在 BitMart 平台上存放了高達 1,010 萬美元的龐大資金，但自 7 月 26 日停運公告發布以來，完全無法提領任何一分錢。
更令人毛骨悚然的是，該用戶透露，其專屬的 BitMart VIP 經理 Tony 在 7 月 26 日當天就刪除了 Telegram 帳號（但用戶已保留完整對話紀錄），其他團隊成員也相繼上演「人間蒸發」。過去積極回覆、安撫並分享內部資訊的官方團隊，如今卻陷入死寂。他在貼文中絕望地質問：「資金到底在哪？為什麼無法提領？什麼時候能拿回錢？」並聲稱有數萬名用戶正經歷同樣的煎熬。
Hey everyone — and a special hello to @sheldonbitmart and the wonderful BitMart team.
I normally wouldn’t post something like this, but I’m out of options.
At the time, I had around $10.1 MILLION on BitMart. Since July 26, I haven’t been able to withdraw single dollar.
On… pic.twitter.com/ZWRzbr17UE
— BeardStaff (@BeardStaffX) August 9, 2026
造市商補刀指控：BitMart 已資不抵債
就在大戶絕望求援的隔日（8 月 10 日），自稱為造市商（MM）的用戶 @0xDeltaHedged 引用了該篇貼文，並拋出了更具毀滅性的指控。他表示，他們的造市商資金同樣被卡在 BitMart，而背後的殘酷真相是，這家交易所已經「資不抵債（Insolvent）」，根本無力應付用戶的提款需求。
@0xDeltaHedged 還加碼爆料，指出 BitMart 團隊在宣布關閉的「前一週」，竟然還在積極要求代幣持有者將資金鎖定（Lock）在他們的交易所上。他憤怒地批評，這從頭到尾就是一場為了吸取最後流動性（Play for liquidity）的惡意操作，完全不顧用戶的死活。
our MM has our balances stuck on @BitMartExchange that we can't get out cuz theyre insolvent.
also insane that they were asking token holders to lock tokens on their exchange literally 1 week before they shut down.
it was always just a play for liquidity. https://t.co/NzHd1PM0M1 pic.twitter.com/HtRm3VpFFq
— Matthew (∇, ∇) (@0xDeltaHedged) August 10, 2026
官方稱有序清退，鏈上數據卻現端倪
回顧這起事件，BitMart 雖然在 7 月 26 日的公告中強調這是一次「有序清退」，並將正式停止運營時間定在 2027 年 1 月 31 日；但根據 Lookonchain 等鏈上數據追蹤機構的觀察，在公告發布後的 24 小時內，僅有約 58 個地址成功提現約 80.5 萬美元，期間甚至出現長達 8 小時的「零提現」空窗期。超過 2.5 萬美元的大額提現幾乎完全停擺，且 BitMart 相關錢包的穩定幣流動性已降至極低水準。
儘管 BitMart 創辦人 Sheldon Xia 終於在 8 月初打破沉默，強烈否認跑路、挪用資金等傳聞，並表示核心團隊仍在進行資產盤點以實現「有序清退」；但在提現問題遲遲未解，以及造市商與千萬大戶連番提出實質性指控的雙重打擊下，市場對 BitMart 償付能力的最後一絲信任，恐怕已蕩然無存。

〈Vitalik 釋出 2026 版以太坊路線圖：AI 輔助形式驗證成核心，強隱私與抗量子成新焦點〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
以太坊的未來藍圖迎來重大更新！據以太坊共同創辦人 Vitalik Buterin 於 X 平台發布的最新貼文指出，對比 2023 年的版本，最新的以太坊路線圖「Strawmap」在優先順序上出現了顯著變化。除了將量子安全大幅提前外，更新增了包含「強隱私（Strong privacy）」與依賴 AI 加速的「形式驗證」等全新項目，揭示了以太坊走向精簡、安全且高度可擴展的未來。
（前情提要：加密通訊軟體 Signal 正開發「免電話」註冊！Vitalik 讚賞但警告：防不了 AI 大數據肉搜，偽匿名性已死）
（背景補充：Vitalik 解析密碼學聖杯 Diamond iO：讓智能合約「完全隱身」的行星級協議）
在區塊鏈技術快速更迭的浪潮中，以太坊（Ethereum）未來的發展方向始終是全市場關注的焦點。台北時間 8 月 10 日，以太坊共同創辦人 Vitalik Buterin 在 X（前 Twitter）上分享了一份詳細的技術反思，他將 2023 年廣為人知的「六大階段」路線圖（The Merge、Surge 等），與涵蓋至 2029 年以後的最新版「Strawmap」進行了深度對照，揭示了以太坊核心開發團隊在戰略優先級上的重大轉變。
I updated my 2023 roadmap diagram to overlay where the items that were there sit in the current Strawmap ( https://t.co/9deLIQWG24 ).
In general, a lot of overlap, but:
* Some things got reshuffled in order (eg. quantum safety up-prioritized)
* Some things deprioritized (eg.… pic.twitter.com/XLdIt4kAgT
— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) August 10, 2026
抗量子提前，強隱私首度列入一級目標
根據 Vitalik 的貼文分析，雖然兩個版本的路線圖在大部分項目上仍保持高度重疊，但有幾個關鍵領域經歷了重新的排序與調整。最明顯的變化之一，是因應未來運算威脅，「量子安全（Quantum safety）」的優先級別被大幅提前；相對地，VDFs（可驗證延遲函數）與許多 EVM（以太坊虛擬機）的改進則被降低了優先級，甚至部分舊方案（如 State expiry）已被更具潛力的「新狀態類型（New state types）」所取代。
更值得注意的是，2026 年版的 Strawmap 中出現了多個在 2023 年完全不存在的全新項目。首當其衝的便是被列為第一級優先的「強隱私（Strong privacy）」架構，這反映了生態系對用戶資料保護的重視程度正急遽上升。此外，路線圖也新增了「後量子時代的激進擴展」、「Blob and gas futures」以及因 SNARKs 技術成熟而得以實現的「Native rollups」。
重押 STARKs 與 AI 加速形式驗證
在技術底層的變革上，Vitalik 點出了一個極為關鍵的共同主題：以太坊未來的擴展策略，不再是盲目追求最大化「所有」鏈上活動的吞吐量，而是轉向建立具有更嚴格屬性、且能針對高負載活動（如代幣轉帳與隱私協議）進行優化的專門機制。
為了實現這個願景，以太坊團隊正願意將協議的技術未來，押注在「STARKs」與「現代 AI 加速的形式驗證（Formal Verification, FV）」之上。Vitalik 解釋，遞迴 STARKs 技術將出現在共識層、資料層與執行層等多個協議層級中；而這種深度的架構整合，唯有仰賴現代 AI 工具協助進行徹底的形式驗證，才能確保系統的絕對安全，並進一步推動協議規範的「精簡化（Lean-ification）」。
EVM 的未來：開放架構與精簡主義
除了底層技術的升級，EVM 本身的設計空間也將迎來開放。Vitalik 透露，未來協議可能會向用戶暴露非 EVM 的指令集架構（ISA），例如更現代且高效的 leanISA 或 RISC-V。這意味著 EVM 未來可能轉型為運行在這些架構之上的中間碼（IR），而非作為基層的內建功能。
「以太坊將會是量子安全的、把用戶隱私放在第一位的、安全的、抗審查的、高效能且可擴展的，同時也是精簡（Lean）的，」Vitalik 在結語中感性地總結，這份藍圖不僅是技術的演進，更是眾多以太坊研究者與開發者多年來不懈努力的結晶。

title: 世代級警告！標普 500「席勒本益比」飆破 40，重現網路泡沫極端估值
summary:
美股多頭狂歡背後暗藏隱憂？據《The Motley Fool》報導，標普 500 指數近期屢創歷史新高，但一項 […]

〈世代級警告！標普 500「席勒本益比」飆破 40，重現網路泡沫極端估值〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美股多頭狂歡背後暗藏隱憂？據《The Motley Fool》報導，標普 500 指數近期屢創歷史新高，但一項被視為「世代級」的股市警告指標 —— 席勒本益比（Shiller CAPE）已飆升破 40，創下自 1990 年代末網路泡沫以來的歷史次高紀錄。專家警告，投資人對 AI 成長的過度樂觀可能面臨估值重置的風險，呼籲市場轉向尋求高品質且財務穩健的資產。
（前情提要：FOMO 情緒引爆美股！選擇權市場閃現極端看漲訊號，分析師警告反轉風險）
（背景補充：那斯達克拍板年底開跑 23 小時交易：美股一天只休 1 小時，向全日無休交易邁進）
美國股市正處於一場狂歡之中。截至 2026 年 8 月初，標普 500 指數（S&P 500）不僅屢創歷史新高，今年迄今更已上漲約 13%。如果這波多頭行情延續，標普 500 將在今年底達成連續四年雙位數成長的傲人紀錄，這是自 1990 年代中期網路泡沫時代以來從未見過的多頭連勝。然而，在市場一片樂觀之際，歷史的警鐘卻悄悄敲響。
席勒本益比飆破 40，歷史僅見兩次
據財經媒體《The Motley Fool》特約撰稿人 Steven Porrello 的最新分析指出，目前的股市與網路泡沫時期有著驚人的相似之處。其中最令人擔憂的，是標普 500 指數的「席勒本益比（Shiller CAPE）」。該指標以過去 10 年經通膨調整後的平均盈餘來計算，能有效平滑短期波動，被視為衡量市場估值的權威標準。
歷史數據顯示，席勒本益比過去 150 年的平均值約落在 16 至 17 之間。當該比率超過 24 時，通常預示著嚴重的市場調整，甚至可能演變成大蕭條或網路泡沫般的崩盤。然而，目前的席勒本益比竟高達 41.4，這是歷史上僅有的第二次突破 40 大關（第一次發生在 1990 年代末期，峰值約 44）。這意味著投資人為了標普 500 過去 10 年平均一美元的盈餘，付出了約 40 美元的代價，溢價幅度高達 135%。
世代級警告：AI 成長預期面臨嚴峻考驗
作者強調，席勒本益比超過 40 堪稱「世代級」的罕見事件。不過，這並不代表股市明天就會崩盤，而是反映出當前投資人對未來成長寄予了極高的期望——尤其是對於人工智慧（AI）相關的龐大資本支出能否帶來足夠回報的樂觀預期。一旦未來的企業盈餘成長不如預期，高昂的股價估值將可能面臨極其痛苦的「重置」。
專家建議：放棄炒作，回歸高品質資產
面對估值過高的潛在下行風險，投資人該如何應對？報導建議，如果市場確實如 CAPE 指標所示被嚴重高估，當下最佳的投資策略是「選擇品質而非炒作」。投資人應優先考量財務體質健康的企業，尋找具備低負債、充裕現金、穩定現金流，以及強勁盈餘表現的公司。
雖然高品質股票未必能帶來最刺激的短期雙位數報酬，也沒有任何股票能完全免疫市場大跌；但歷史經驗證明，圍繞財務穩健公司建立分散的投資組合，仍是應對未來不確定性的最佳防禦方式。截至撰稿時，標普 500 指數報價約在 7,767 點，市場是否會迎來估值修正，仍有待時間驗證。

title: 比特幣礦企 MARA Holdings 上半年狂倒 2.3 萬枚比特幣！套現 16 億鎂、拋售庫存近 4 成
summary:
比特幣礦企巨頭 MARA（原 Marathon Digital）的倒貨規模，遠比市場想像得還要龐大！據知名鏈上 […]

〈比特幣礦企 MARA Holdings 上半年狂倒 2.3 萬枚比特幣！套現 16 億鎂、拋售庫存近 4 成〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣礦企巨頭 MARA（原 Marathon Digital）的倒貨規模，遠比市場想像得還要龐大！據知名鏈上數據分析帳號 The Data Nerd 於 10 日發布的追蹤指出，根據 MARA 最新提交的 SEC 財報顯示，該公司在今年上半年已悄悄出清了高達 23,093 枚比特幣，套現約 16 億美元，拋售比例直逼其庫存的四成。
（前情提要：熊底到了？比特幣礦企 PowerCompute 以 307 BTC 再融資 1800 萬美元）
（背景補充：礦企 Cipher Digital 上半年狂賣 1,619 枚比特幣！慘賠 4,770 萬鎂，急轉型 AI 資料中心求生）
比特幣礦企的「信仰」是否正在動搖？台北時間 8 月 10 日晚間，知名鏈上數據分析帳號 The Data Nerd 透過 X（前 Twitter）平台發布了一則附帶視覺化圖表的驚人數據，直指北美最大的比特幣礦企之一 MARA Holdings（前稱為 Marathon Digital Holdings），其實際賣出的比特幣數量，遠比早期新聞標題所暗示的還要驚人。
Turns out MARA has been selling a lot more than the headlines let on.
The miner offloaded 23,093 $BTC ($1.6B) in the first half of 2026, at an average of $70,631.
It still holds 35,577 $BTC ($2.3B). pic.twitter.com/aLpdLGINVa
— The Data Nerd (@OnchainDataNerd) August 10, 2026
上半年狂倒 2.3 萬枚 BTC，均價破 7 萬鎂
這項數據的源頭，來自 MARA 於近日向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的 Q2 2026 Form 10-Q 季報。根據文件揭露，這家礦業巨頭在 2026 年上半年（H1 2026）期間，總計出清了 23,093 枚比特幣。若以當時的市場行情計算，這波拋售的總價值高達約 16 億美元，平均售價落在相當亮眼的 70,631 美元。
The Data Nerd 的圖表進一步突顯了這波倒貨的規模。在拋售之前，MARA 的持倉量在 2025 年底還維持在 53,822 枚 BTC 的高位；經過這半年的密集減持，其庫存已大幅下滑約 34%，拋售比例占其總庫存的近 39%。截至 6 月 30 日，MARA 帳上仍持有 35,577 枚 BTC（現值約 23 億美元）。
放棄死忠 HODL？轉向 AI 與基礎建設
值得注意的是，MARA 過去長期以來一直是比特幣「HODL（長期持有）」策略的死忠擁護者，鮮少出售其開採的比特幣。然而，隨著比特幣減半後利潤遭到嚴重壓縮，該公司的策略已出現重大轉向。從 2025 年開始，MARA 便允許出售新開採的 BTC；到了 2026 年，更進一步擴大彈性，開始從現有庫存中大舉套現。
這筆高達 16 億美元的龐大資金，究竟流向了何處？根據財報與市場消息指出，MARA 將這筆橫財主要用於四大用途：首先是回購約 10 億美元的可轉換債券以降低槓桿（總債務從約 36 億降至 24 億美元）；其次是資助日常營運與流動性管理；再者是支持包含 AI／高效能運算（HPC）基礎設施與能源專案的成長投資；最後，部分資金也搭配了以 BTC 作為抵押的借款操作（如 8 月初剛取得的 6 億美元融資）。
相較於先前市場僅聚焦於 MARA 在 3 月份出售 1.5 萬枚 BTC 用於還債的單一事件，The Data Nerd 的這份總結，完整揭露了礦企在面臨生存與轉型壓力時，如何將手中的比特幣庫存化為靈活的資本工具。MARA 的策略大轉彎，不僅反映了礦業生態的劇變，也為比特幣市場帶來了不容忽視的拋售壓力。

title: New weight loss pill approved for use in UK
summary: Foundayo is made by Eli Lilly, the drug firm behind the Mounjaro jab.
full_text:
New weight loss pill approved for use in UK
- Published
A daily weight-loss pill made by the drug firm behind the Mounjaro jab has been approved for use in the UK - the first country in Europe to do so.
Foundayo, made by Eli Lilly, is for treating obesity and type 2 diabetes.
But while people will be able to buy it privately with a prescription, the approval by the Medicines and Healthcare productors Regulatory Agency does not automatically mean it will be made available on the NHS.
Foundayo is a form of GLP-1 medication that blunts appetite, and comes after the MHRA approved a pill version of a similar weight-loss drug, Wegovy, in June.
Eli Lilly said while it could immediately be used by the NHS for type 2 diabetes, it would be making an application to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence in England for it to be recommended as a weight loss treatment as well.
Dr Simon Cork, from Anglia Ruskin University, said while the weight-loss benefits of Foundayo were less than other treatments, patients could still expect to see "significant, clinically meaningful changes to their weight".
And he said a key advantage was that it was likely to be cheaper than other weight-loss treatments, which have tended to be tightly restricted by the NHS.
University of Glasgow expert Prof Naveed Sattar agreed it was "good news".
He said another benefit was its convenience, pointing out that unlike the Wegovy pill, which has to be taken on an empty stomach, this pill could be taken at any time of the day.
"The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences," he added.
Experts believe it could help people coming off weight-loss jabs remain slim.
Trials found that patients who had used weight loss jabs and then been given the tablet, also called orforglipron, every day for a year avoided regaining much of the weight they had lost - a known risk when coming off GLP-1 injections.
People on weight loss medication are also advised to eat a healthy diet and get enough exercise.
And, like any medication, there can be side effects to using Foundayo, including nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and vomiting.

title: MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
summary: Scottish Green MSP Q Manivannan is facing criticism from rape survivors groups and politicians over a podcast interview.
full_text:
MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
- Published
A newly-elected MSP has apologised for the hurt caused by comments in which they talked of the "demonisation" of rape.
Scottish Green Party politician Q Manivannan has also faced criticism for suggesting rape is a "spectrum of things" during a podcast recorded before they were elected to the Scottish Parliament.
Earlier, the Scottish Rape Crisis Alliance (SRCA) - which represents four rape crisis centres - said there is "no hierarchy of rape" and warned the MSP not to minimise sexual violence.
In a statement, Manivannan said clips from the podcast had been "selectively edited" but said they were "sorry" for the upset, and insisted they would never seek to diminish a rape survivor's experience.
The comments, which were made during The Subjective Space podcast , externalrecorded last year, sparked fury after they re-emerged online at the weekend.
Manivannan, who identifies as non-binary and uses they/them pronouns, was being interviewed about care and carers in society, when host Sindhu Rajasekaran raised the rehabilitation of criminals, saying she could have no empathy for rapists.
The Edinburgh-based former writer and academic said there was a "myth of the monster rapist" and "a demonisation of rape in the sense of it is a spectrum".
They continued: "It is a spectrum, none of which is any less or worse, but it is a spectrum of things that constitute one homogenised word 'rape'".
Manivannan went on to argue that the idea of a rapist as a "big burly man" was understandably a source of fear.
But the MSP told Rajasekaran that "any individual is capable of rape, including yourself and me, and I think that scary thought is the hardest to contend with".
'No hierarchy of rape'
The comments have been widely criticised by survivors groups and political opponents who said they downplayed the seriousness and lasting trauma of rape.
The SCRA, which comprises support groups in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Ayrshire and the Western Isles, said the impacts of rape can last a lifetime, and the crime should never be reduced to a theoretical debate.
In an open letter the alliance said: "We are not demonising rape. We are naming it."
The authors strongly opposed the idea of rape existing on a "spectrum", insisting "there is no hierarchy of rape" and that no survivor should feel compelled to ask whether their experience was serious enough."
The letter urged politicians "not to normalise" rape or sexual violence, and "not create hierarchies of harm".
While not naming Manivannan, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on Violence against Women and Girls, Reem Alsalem, posted on X that rape should never be spoken about in terms of it being a spectrum.
Scotland's Children's Minister Siobhan Brown told the BBC's Sunday Show Manivannan's words were misjudged.
Scottish Labour and the Scottish Liberal Democrats have also been critical, while the Scottish Conservatives called on the Scottish Greens to suspend the MSP.
Meghan Gallacher, the party's equalities spokeswoman, said: "It is deeply alarming that anyone, but especially an elected representative, would ever seek to minimise the seriousness of rape and suggest that there is a spectrum of offences."
'Malicious' editing
In a statement issued on Monday afternoon, Manivannan said they were "horrified" that the comments had been "selectively edited in order to mislead people and misrepresent me".
The MSP said that during the interview they had categorically stated that every rape in every context is equally serious and harmful but this had been "maliciously" left out of clips.
They added: "I recognise that the words in the clip shared, without the full context of the conversation, have caused considerable upset.
"For that I apologise. I will always stand with and for victims and survivors."
Manivannan said they were themselves a survivor of sexual violence and understood the enduring trauma of such an experience.
"I would never seek to diminish or dismiss any survivor's experience, or to make anyone feel that their pain was not heard or understood," they added.
"I am genuinely sorry to everyone who has been distressed, hurt or triggered by the clips, and by the discussion and coverage that has followed.
"Words matter, particularly when speaking about something as deeply personal and painful as sexual violence, and I regret this hurt caused."

title: From Dubai to a Dublin court - how alleged cartel boss Daniel Kinahan returned to Ireland
summary: Law enforcement agencies in Ireland and the US believe he is a leading figure in the Kinahan Organised Crime Group.
full_text:
From Dubai to a Dublin court - how alleged cartel boss Daniel Kinahan returned to Ireland
- Published
Armed police took up positions at the entrances to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin, as the plane carrying Daniel Kinahan approached the city.
On the steps of the building, journalists from Irish and international media tracked the flight online.
The Irish government had sent its jet to Dubai.
It is usually used to transport ministers, but it left the United Arab Emirates (UAE) with a suspected crime boss on board.
The doors of the court opened around half an hour after the aircraft landed at a military airfield nine miles (14km) away.
As reporters went through security, we heard the sound of sirens outside - indicating the arrival of the accused.
The courtroom filled up over the next 45 minutes - as detectives, prosecutors, and some members of the public took up seats along with the media.
From the moment Kinahan entered the dock, until he was led out 13 minutes later, almost everyone was looking towards him - and the proceedings were accompanied by constant typing from the press benches.
Complex international investigations, and diplomacy, had led to this moment.
Kinahan was charged with a single offence - directing the activities of a criminal organisation between October 2015 and April 2017.
He did not have to enter a plea at this stage of the court process.
But his lawyers have previously told the BBC that the allegations he is a crime boss are false and have no evidential basis.
They also said he had no criminal record or convictions.
Law enforcement agencies on both sides of the Atlantic believe he is a leading figure in the Kinahan Organised Crime Group.
The gang began as a street drug dealing operation in Dublin in the 1980s. From there, it became an international player in organised crime.
It has been linked to drug trafficking, money laundering, and murder.
The former deputy director of the UK's National Crime Agency, Roy McComb, said the group had grown globally because it had the "ambition and drive" to do so.
McComb told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that the Kinahan group had created links with other organisations from South America, Eastern Europe, Pakistan and Afghanistan, who were involved in the "wholesale distribution" of drugs.
He said the cartel became "the go-to organised crime group to move large quantities of narcotics around Europe".
McComb explained they were "seen to be a threat to the stability of the US dollar", because they were trading in the currency.
In 2022, the US offered a reward of $5m (€4.3m; £3.7m) for information about Kinahan, his father Christopher Senior and brother Christopher Junior.
The organisation had previously come to more widespread global media attention in 2016, as the result of a vicious feud with another Irish gang known as the Hutch organisation.
During that year, Kinahan was targeted by gunmen at a boxing weigh-in at a hotel in north Dublin.
Mobile phone footage of the shooting captured the chaos and brutality of the violence.
One man was murdered in that incident. During months of gangland violence, 18 people were killed.
Kinahan left Ireland shortly after the attempt on his life.
The Irish government put a major diplomatic effort into negotiating an extradition treaty with the UAE, which was signed in 2024.
Kinahan is the second person to be brought to Ireland under the terms of the agreement.
The first was Sean McGovern, who was described by a judge to be a "senior lieutenant" in the Kinahan group.
In June, McGovern was sentenced to 24 years in jail after pleading guilty to two charges of directing a criminal organisation.
Kinahan rose to his feet, with his hands clasped in front of him, when a court official read his charge to him on Sunday.
I was sitting about three metres from Kinahan.
His appearance was slightly different compared with the well-known photographs of him.
He wore plain clothes, including a black hoodie, and glasses.
He spoke several times during the hearing, when one of the three judges addressed him directly.
His tone was polite.
He indicated he would decide later whether he would come to court in person for the next hearing on 5 October, or appear via video link from prison.
Outside the court, a crowd of more than 100 people were waiting to see a police convoy carry him away at speed.
The prosecution has formally commenced.

title: From Stonehenge to the Serpentine - satellite images show impact of hot, dry summer
summary: From Stonehenge to the Serpentine the impact on parts of the UK from a long, hot, summer can be seen from space.
full_text:
From Stonehenge to the Serpentine - satellite images show impact of hot, dry summer
- Published
With more parts of England set to join Wales as being officially declared to be in drought, BBC Verify has been gathering satellite imagery showing the impact of this year's extreme summer heat.
From historic sites and parks to reservoirs and golf courses, the hot, dry weather has changed how large parts of the UK usually look.
This year's consecutive heatwaves and above-average temperatures have had a noticeable effect - even compared with last summer which was the UK's warmest on record.
Drop in Welsh reservoir level
According to the UK government, almost all reservoirs in England and Wales are officially classed as having water levels below normal or low.
Five are exceptionally low - among them Clywedog reservoir in Powys which provides water supplies for parts of the West Midlands.
These satellite images show how more of the banks of the reservoir are visible this August compared with the same month last year.
Low reservoir levels have not been the primary cause of recent hosepipe bans and drought declarations - which are ultimately triggered by a lack of rain - across large parts of England and Wales.
The Environment Agency has reported that reservoir storage is now at 69% in England, which is below the long-term average of 82% for the time of year but higher than during last year's drought.
However, in its latest report the agency says water storage levels are above those recorded during similar periods in 2022 and 2025.
While Scotland has not been as badly affected as England and Wales, July's rainfall was below average for the south and east of the country, with many areas seeing less than half the long-term average for the month.
This has led the Scottish Environment Protection Agency to warn of "significant" water scarcity in the Borders and "moderate scarcity" in areas on the eastern side of Scotland.
Brown fairways at Open golf course
Hard and dry fairways were a key talking point at golf's Open Championship which was held at Royal Birkdale on Merseyside last month.
A side-by-side comparison shows how much greener the fairways appeared in summer 2025 compared with this year.
As the BBC reported earlier this month while domestic users face hosepipe restrictions the rules for commercial users - including golf courses - vary.
When hosepipe bans are in force sports grounds can use hoses or sprinklers - but only to water grass areas "actively used for play". For golf courses this means the greens and tees can be irrigated but the fairways cannot.
Algal blooms in reservoirs and lakes
Right in the heart of the UK capital, Hyde Park's famous Serpentine lake was closed for swimming on Monday because of high levels of blue-green algae.
Blue-green algae occur naturally, but warm, sunny and settled conditions can help blooms develop. Some can be harmful to people and animals.
A similar issue is affecting Killington Reservoir in south Cumbria. Satellite images show a visible change in the water between 24 May and 8 August, where a blue-green algal bloom has been confirmed.
Looking at the rest of Hyde Park and what is one of London's prime green spaces is now mostly brown following consecutive heatwaves since May.
It's a similar sight in south Wiltshire where the usually green rolling fields surrounding the ancient stone circle at Stonehenge have become almost as pale as the path around the prehistoric site.
As BBC Verify previously reported parts of the country are suffering from "vegetation stress" where the development and growth of plants, grass and crops can be severely affected.
Vegetation turning brown, even on this scale, does not mean the plants have disappeared or died, as grass, shrubs and some trees can recover once rainfall returns, provided their root systems remain intact.
Experts have said the combination of next-to-no rainfall and prolonged hot weather is likely to cause significant issues for the farming industry and could have an impact on agriculture and food prices in the coming months.
And perhaps counter-intuitively, prolonged dry weather can raise the risk of flash flooding when it eventually does rain. That is because parched, rock-hard ground may struggle to absorb water at first, so some rainwater may simply run off the surface instead.
Scientists also warn the UK is facing a growing risk of water shortages in the decades ahead, driven by human-caused climate change and increased demand.
Graphics by Tom Shiel

title: The transgender row surrounding the WNBA
summary: After the Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham said it was "common sense" to ban transgender women from women's sports, a row has emerged in the WNBA - with former NBA players saying eligibility rules mean they can enter the 2027 Draft.
full_text:
The transgender row surrounding the WNBA
- Published
The WNBA is still in the midst of its 2026 season and yet it is next year's Draft for North America's top women's basketball league that is dominating the headlines.
Why? Because some former men's NBA players have declared they will enter for selection - citing the current eligibility guidelines, or lack of, for transgender women players.
"I'm officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect," said Enes Kanter Freedom, who played 11 seasons in the NBA.
It is the latest development in a story ignited by a comment made by Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham, who said she wanted to protect young girls "who shouldn't have to go against biological men" in sport.
Her words have instigated protests - albeit not grand in scale - on both sides of the argument, and once again catapulted the debate around transgender women in sport into the spotlight.
How did we get here?
Last month, Cunningham, one of the league's most high-profile players, gave an interview to ESPN, external in which the conversation turned to the topic of "protecting" women's sports.
The Indiana Fever guard said she had received criticism from people who believed she "hated" transgender people, something she denied.
She said she wanted to "extend love" to everyone, but added: "I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."
She later doubled down on her comments, saying it was "common sense", external to bar transgender athletes from competing in women's sports.
Her words quickly moved beyond basketball and into a wider political debate in the United States.
President Donald Trump expressed his support for Cunningham, while vice-president JD Vance said she was "inspiring".
Though the 29-year-old later said she is "not a very political person", her remarks have followed her around the country. Competing rallies from critics and supporters were organised at Indiana's games, along with small-scale protests.
The scale of the debate in the media, online and in politics was striking given no openly transgender woman is due to play, or has ever played, in the WNBA.
What do the rules say?
The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.
On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."
The WNBA has yet to comment publicly on the row since Cunningham's comments but league commissioner Cathy Engelbert reportedly sent a memo to teams last week in which she said the matter would be discussed at an upcoming pre-arranged meeting with team presidents.
In the memo, seen by the Associated Press, external, Engelbert said the league would "always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league".
She added: "Our player eligibility rules, unlike the eligibility rules of some other leagues and governing bodies, are collectively bargained. Preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league's highest priorities."
However, the lack of detail in the league's eligibility criteria has been brought to light by Kanter Freedom, who finished his playing career with the Boston Celtics in 2022.
"If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA," he wrote on Instagram, external.
Kanter Freedom, who has previously spoken out about human rights violations in China and Turkey, among other issues, added: "I know my presence on the court will stir up strong opinions. I am definitely not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any community or personal choices.
"I'm simply asking that the current rules be applied equally to everyone - the rules that represent the very values many WNBA players and coaches have publicly advocated for."
A day after Kanter Freedom's 'announcement', Royce White - who made three appearances in the NBA as a player and is now a Republican Senate candidate - said he would also declare for the Draft, adding: "I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball."
Whether the vagueness of the rules are by design to leave it open to transgender women or a sign of an oversight that genuinely needs tightening up is not clear.
BBC Sport has contacted Cunningham's representatives, the WNBA and WNBPA for comment.
What has the reaction been?
Cunningham's comments have become a flashpoint inside a league which has a long history of player activism on issues including race, gender equality and LGBTQ+ rights.
The players' association did not mention Cunningham by name when it eventually addressed the debate.
In a statement the WNBPA denounced "hate abuse and demonisation of the transgender community" and reaffirmed its commitment to "justice, equity, diversity and inclusion".
It called on fans to report abusive behaviour at games and added that it would continue to have "hard" conversations but it "will not be used as political pawns".
There is strong feeling on both sides of the argument. Minnesota Lynx head coach and president Cheryl Reeve, who said: "I come from a space of inclusion.
"The narrative that I think is problematic is to suggest that transgender athletes are the biggest problem in women's sports."
Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt before Minnesota played Indiana earlier this month and was seen speaking to Cunningham on court before the game.
Cunningham later said the pair had exchanged their perspectives and that the conversation ended with "love and respect".
Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams said she would welcome a transgender athlete "on my team or against my team, any time".
Last month, the WNBA suspended Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton from attending the team's next five home games after an exchange with two fans, who were sat courtside displaying signs thanking Cunningham for "speaking up for girls".
Keaton reportedly confronted the teenage fans and admonished them during the game. The Storm have since apologised.
As for Cunningham, the attention has increasingly become an unwelcome distraction.
Having defended her original comments, she said recently that she now wanted the conversation to return to what was happening on court.
"I want to get back to basketball, it's always been about basketball" she said, arguing that the standard of play in the WNBA was being overshadowed by issues away from the game.
But that may prove difficult, as pressure grows on the league to clarify exactly who is eligible to play.
What are the rules in other sports?
In recent years, many governing bodies in sport have amended their rules about the inclusion of transgender athletes at the elite level, moving more towards restrictions.
Athletics, cycling and aquatics, for example, have implemented outright bans on transgender women taking part in women's events.
In March, it was announced that the women's category of Olympic sports will be limited to biological females from the LA Olympic Games in 2028.
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) says eligibility will be determined by a "once-in-a-lifetime" sex test, which would prevent transgender women and those with differences in sexual development (DSD) who have gone through male puberty from competing.
In the United States, transgender women and girls are banned from competing in women's sports categories in schools, universities and the grassroots level.
That was part of an executive order - titled "Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports" - signed by President Trump last year.
It does not cover professional sport.

title: Should Liverpool fans be worried about Iraola's fitness comments?
summary: Should Liverpool fans be worried about Andoni Iraola's comments concerning the squad's fitness?
full_text:
Should Liverpool fans be worried about Iraola's fitness comments?
- Published
For the second friendly in a row, Andoni Iraola's Liverpool threw away a two-goal lead and went on to lose the game.
In Chicago on 2 August, new Liverpool manager Iraola said the 4-2 friendly defeat against Leeds was useful as he "learned a lot of things" about his side.
However, at Anfield on Sunday against Monaco, the Spaniard was a little more candid after a 3-2 loss.
Two weeks out from the start of the Premier League campaign, Iraola's verdict was that his side had "work to do" because they could not sustain the level that he wanted for the duration of a game.
Iraola said that his side played a good first 30 minutes but "they don't have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this".
For what it's worth, the first half against Leeds and the first 30 minutes against Monaco was the best that Liverpool have looked throughout pre-season. They moved the ball with pace, were direct, pressed with intensity and both Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have looked sharp.
But as the game progressed and changes were made - Iraola made nine against Leeds and 11 against Monaco - Liverpool have looked like a different team and certainly not for the better. Leeds scored four goals in 25 minutes without reply while Monaco scored three unanswered goals in 44 minutes too.
Some of the squad are still working their way back to full fitness after some time off following the World Cup while others such as Conor Bradley, Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni are sidelined for lengthy periods of time.
Uruguay defender Ronald Araujo, who can play at centre-back and right-back, is close to completing a season-long loan move from Barcelona.
On Sunday, skipper Virgil van Dijk said: "Let's see what the next couple of weeks are going to bring. Any quality we can add to the team will definitely be welcome so let's see."
But with the squad at his disposal, Iraola is adamant that the general fitness must improve if they are to play the style that he wants. Pablo de la Torre, one of Iraola's assistants, has also made the move to Liverpool and was previously the fitness coach at Bournemouth.
Across the small sample size of four games, there have been enough signs of Liverpool playing in a busy manner in the early phases of games and that intensity was evident to see during an open training session in Chicago, where Iraola used phrases like "quicker, quicker" repeatedly.
One player told BBC Sport how he felt sick after the first few sessions while the punishment for losing sides in training has been to sprint to the other end of the pitch and back.
In Chicago, Milos Kerkez said that Iraola is asking the players to "play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to always be on the front foot".
Iraola's Bournemouth side ranked first in the Premier League season for direct attacks and third when it came to high turnovers.
It is worth noting that it took him 10 games to secure his first win at Bournemouth in the 2023-24 season. Any such run at Liverpool would be unacceptable but you only have to look at the way Bournemouth performed throughout his tenure to see why Iraola persisted with his ways.
His comments on Sunday were certainly concerning but he has had less than a month to work with his players and only a week or so with some. The signs are there that this team will entertain but as Iraola pointed out in Chicago, it will take time.
"I would like to say, no, on the first day, we are going to be perfect, everyone will be in place, but probably it is not going to be like this," he said, when asked if it would take a while before fully seeing his style of play. "We will have to do this as quickly as possible."
