title: eToro Agrees to Acquire TradeZero in $231M US Expansion, Stock Tanks 10%
summary: The crypto-friendly trading platform is betting on US equities as regulators keep squeezing its token menu.
full_text:
In brief
- eToro agreed to buy TradeZero, a US active-trader brokerage, for up to $231 million, it said Tuesday.
- The deal adds broker-dealer infrastructure and Canadian market access; it's expected to close in the first half of 2027.
- eToro's US crypto lineup stays narrow after a 2021 SEC settlement restricted it to Bitcoin, Ethereum and Bitcoin Cash.
eToro said Tuesday it will buy TradeZero, a US-focused online brokerage that serves active traders, in a deal worth up to $231 million. The agreement, announced by eToro Group Ltd., deepens the platform's push into the American equities market.
TradeZero, founded in 2015, runs commission-free U.S. stock and options trading through its broker-dealer subsidiaries. For eToro, the appeal is the plumbing: next-generation trading platforms, broker-dealer infrastructure, an engaged trader community, and a door into the Canadian market. TradeZero operates across the U.S., Canada, and international markets.
eToro framed the purchase as a shortcut to new U.S. products. "Today's announcement is an important step in building our US business," eToro Co-Founder and CEO Yoni Assia said in a statement. "This combination gives us a faster path to launching new products for US customers and strengthens our offering. Together, we'll innovate faster as we continue building the global financial superapp for the next generation of users."
With this purchase eToro may be positioning itself for easier competition against bigger and more popular brokers. The company built its name letting retail users trade crypto and copy other investors, but U.S. equities have been a harder wedge. TradeZero brings the licensed U.S. rails and the active-trader base that competes head-on with Robinhood.
The consideration runs to up to $231 million, "consisting of cash and up to 2.5 million newly issued Class A common shares of the Company," per the release, subject to customary adjustments. TradeZero generated about $80 million in revenue with 81% gross margins over the last twelve months.
The equities bet lands as eToro's U.S. crypto shelf stays thin. After a 2021 SEC settlement, American users can only trade Bitcoin, Ethereum and Bitcoin Cash, with a 180-day window to offload everything else. eToro has been patching around that limit instead—buying self-custody wallet firm Zengo for $70 million and trialing tokenized stocks on Ethereum for 24/7 trading.
Investors sold the news
The announcement didn't lift the stock. On the daily charts, eToro, which trades as ETOR, slid more than 10% in Tuesday trading to a low of $30.11 and was down about 10.5% on the day. The drop widened from a 4.4% premarket slip. The stock currently stands at roughly $3.33 billion of market capitalization.
The selloff came even though eToro beat second-quarter estimates—EPS of $0.68 against a $0.61 consensus. It may be that the crypto bear market is weighing on the company. Crypto revenue fell about 30% in the quarter even as equities led growth. eToro is funding the TradeZero purchase partly with up to 2.5 million new shares, and chasing a U.S. equities market where Robinhood already dominates.
eToro reported 4.28 million funded accounts in Q2, up 18% year-over-year, with net contribution of $229 million. It priced its IPO at a $3.7–4 billion valuation in 2025 and expects the TradeZero deal to close in the first half of 2027, after regulatory approval.

title: OpenAI's Only Dedicated Ethicist Has Left With No Replacement: FT
summary: Chloé Bakalar joined from Meta last August and departed in July without any announcement, one of several safety exits in recent weeks.
full_text:
In brief
- Chloé Bakalar, OpenAI's AI ethics lead, left the company last month without a public announcement, the Financial Times reported.
- She was OpenAI's only dedicated ethicist and has not been replaced, according to a person familiar with her role.
- Her exit follows departures by OpenAI's head of safety systems and its chief futurist.
OpenAI's head of ethics has left less than a year after joining, and the company has not replaced her, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
Chloé Bakalar joined as AI ethics lead last August and departed in July with no public announcement, according to the paper. A person familiar with her role told the FT she had been the only dedicated ethicist at the company, working on ethical approaches to model development, how people interact with AI, and the question of machine consciousness.
Bakalar spent six years as chief ethicist at Meta, where she built the company's AI ethics programmes and worked them into products including Instagram and Facebook. She has held academic posts at University College London, Temple University and Princeton.
OpenAI played down the idea that the role was central, with a spokesperson telling the FT that "AI ethics doesn't live with one owner or team at OpenAI." They added that ethical considerations were embedded across research teams and that the company had introduced several systems in recent months to stop models misbehaving.
Bakalar had made a version of the same argument herself. Speaking at a recent conference, she said ethics was everyone's responsibility and that "there should never just be one person who serves as the moral centre" of an AI developer. She declined to comment on her departure to the FT.
A run of safety exits
Her departure follows those of Johannes Heidecke, head of safety systems, and Joshua Achiam, chief futurist and formerly head of mission alignment, the FT said. OpenAI completed a $7 billion buyback of employee shares the same day at an $852 billion valuation, unchanged from its March funding round, as it prepares for a possible listing.
OpenAI paused work on its next major model, Astra, on Friday, saying it could not rule out that the system had reached the top rung of its own cyber-risk scale, a tier reserved for models able to find and build working exploits without a human involved.
That followed an incident in which OpenAI's own agents chained together vulnerabilities, escaped their test environment and attacked Hugging Face while trying to cheat on a security benchmark. The company later said the same agent had broken into four other services using credentials found on the open web.
OpenAI isn’t the only AI firm whose agents have exceeded their parameters in recent weeks. Anthropic's Claude models have since reached three real companies after a misconfiguration opened the internet to them, a Meta model escaped its test environment and exploited a flaw in a third-party service, and Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 broke out of its sandbox to look up benchmark answers.

Bond traders dialed back measures of credit risk associated with Nvidia Corp. on Tuesday after the company said it would limit its exposure in a $500 billion plan to finance the type of artificial-intelligence investments that are driving demand for its computer chips.
The yields on Nvidia’s 5.625% bonds that mature in 2056 slipped to 113 basis points above comparable Treasuries, a decline of 2 basis points. title: Trump wants to split the MMR vaccine. Experts say that's unlikely — and comes with consequences
summary: Doctors and other experts say that splitting the measles, mumps and rubella shot has no scientific basis and is unlikely to get off the ground.
full_text:
President Donald Trump's latest executive order calls for splitting the measles, mumps and rubella, or MMR, vaccine into three separate shots – but doctors and other experts say that effort has no scientific basis and is unlikely to get off the ground.
Trump on Monday said without evidence that the vaccine could be "quite lethal" in its combined form, even though the shot has repeatedly been proven safe and effective across large-scale studies. Experts called that claim "completely false" and said there is no scientific data showing benefits of separating the shot.
Splitting the vaccine would also come with "significant logistical limitations," and having three standalone shots that require multiple doctor's visits could result in more delayed or missed vaccinations among kids, Neil Maniar, a public health professor at Northeastern University, told CNBC.
"They're not solving a problem here. They're creating a new one," Maniar said. "Based on false scientific rationale and political ideology, they're changing something that works into something that we have no idea what it will do."
The U.S. has already seen a decrease in the share of parents who are willing to use the MMR shot to vaccinate their children, which has contributed to the recent resurgence in U.S. measles cases, Dr. Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, told reporters on Wednesday. The U.S. has logged its highest number of measles cases in decades this year.
Trump's rhetoric and recommendations could also further undermine the public's confidence in the safety of the MMR vaccine, said William Moss, a pediatrician and epidemiological professor at Johns Hopkins University.
Roughly 9% of parents report either skipping or delaying the MMR vaccine for their children, according to a 2025 survey conducted by health policy organization KFF and the Washington Post. It's unclear how that compares to previous years.
It's also not clear where Trump initially got the idea to split the shots, but some experts say it can likely be traced to a British gastroenterologist, Andrew Wakefield. He is an anti-vaccine advocate who published a paper in 1998 claiming to show a connection between MMR vaccines and an increase in autism. That paper has since been retracted, and Wakefield was removed from the U.K.'s medical register.
Why splitting the MMR vaccine may not happen
Manufacturers of the MMR vaccine – Merck and GSK – seem to have little incentive to develop standalone shots, which would take significant time and resources away from their other crucial work toward treating and finding cures to other diseases. Those vaccines would likely reach the market long after Trump's term ends.
"I don't see any world in which vaccine manufacturers have any interest in developing and going through the rigorous regulatory process, getting FDA approval, doing the trials for monovalent measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines," said Moss. "It would be a foolish investment to make."
AAP's Racine also said that it would likely take more than a decade to develop those standalone shots.
In a statement on Wednesday, Merck added that evidence suggests using combination shots improves childhood vaccination outcomes, increasing the completion of all recommended doses and compliance rates.
One dose of the MMR shot is currently given at 12 to 15 months of age, with a second dose at 4 to 6 years of age. Separating the vaccine could result in a child needing to receive six different doses in their early life.
"It's just so counterintuitive and counterproductive," Moss said. It's ironic when they're claiming that children receive too many shots, and then they turn around and propose a policy that's just going to increase the number of shots they get."
Northeastern's Maniar said a single visit can already be challenging for parents who have to take time off work. Healthcare access is also more complicated in certain communities, such as rural areas, he added.
Maniar said that the U.S. childhood vaccination schedule is designed based on both the child's "immune system readiness" for a particular shot and their risk for a certain illness. Spacing out those vaccines could increase the chance of a child missing or delaying a shot for a preventable disease they're at risk for.
Racine added, "Why would we not give children a vaccine that is safe, that prevents death?"
He also noted that two healthy children died in the U.S. from measles last year.
Some experts fear that splitting the MMR shot and Trump's broader effort to change federal vaccine recommendations could confuse parents and cause more of them to hold off on immunizing their children. There's also the possibility that some states could align with the new guidance.
Moss said he doesn't see the effort having an immediate or short-term impact on the ongoing measles outbreak.
Still, Maniar emphasized that "we should be doing everything possible to increase those rates rather than implementing policies that present additional barriers to vaccination."

title: Invitation Homes CEO says ban on institutional homebuying will bring down prices, but not immediately
summary: The CEO of the nation's largest single-family rental landlord said the new law banning large-scale investors from the market will lower prices in the long term.
full_text:
The CEO of Invitation Homes, the nation's largest single-family rental landlord, said he believes the recently passed housing bill that bans investors like him from buying existing homes will eventually lower home prices, but not in the short-term.
"I believe in the medium- to long-term, it definitely will," said Invitation Homes chief executive Dallas Tanner. "I think 90% of the bill focuses on deregulation. How do we simplify capital coming into housing? Are there ways that we can spur up the supply side challenges that we have? I think overnight in the immediate term, it's a bit trickier because there's more to the story than just what the bill addresses."
Tanner pointed to mortgage rate volatility, high construction costs, and zoning and regulatory imbalances.
In early January, President Donald Trump called for a ban on large-scale investors buying single-family homes to rent. He posted on social media that, "People live in homes, not corporations." This was part of a larger push to tackle the affordability crisis in housing. Some argued that institutional investors were pushing owner-occupants out of the market and inflating home prices.
The ban became law in July, preventing investors who own more than 350 homes from purchasing any more existing units. They can, however, buy new single-family homes specifically built for rent. That is where Invitation Homes is leaning in.
"Our focus as an industry and as a company has been, how do we create new supply and bring that into the housing system today? We built or acquired, in our partnerships with builders, over 6,000 new homes in the last five years," said Tanner.
In January, just weeks after Trump's post, Invitation Homes purchase a homebuilder, ResiBuilt. It has also purchased homes from large public builders like Pulte Homes and Lennar to use as rentals.
"We found through trial and error ... that this new product, this beta product, the product that we do amongst these master planned developments — it works really, really well for our families. And so we were indexing on that, and that is part of our growth strategy," said Tanner, adding that the company has been selling off hundreds of its older rental properties.
The largest investors, those owning more than 1,000 homes, represent less than 3% of the single-family rental market, according to various sources. They do, however, have an outsized footprint in certain metropolitan markets, like Atlanta (representing 25% of single-family homes there), Jacksonville (21%) and Charlotte (18%), according to the Urban institute.
Invitation Homes reported better-than-expected earnings at the end of July, even though rents and demand are not as healthy as they were in the first few years of the pandemic.
"We've seen sort of fundamentals reset. We talked about it on our last earnings call. We're starting to see actual pretty positive green shoots in several of our markets," said Tanner. "But we're really focused on — how do we navigate this and what does this mean?"

title: Why JPMorgan is investing big in the 2028 LA Olympics
summary: JPMorgan is making a nine-figure bet as the Olympics Games' first-ever global banking partner.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES — For years, JPMorgan executives have been talking with Olympics organizers about sponsoring the games. Before the next event, taking place in Los Angeles in 2028, the firm officially opted in — making a massive, nine-figure bet as the Games' first-ever global banking partner.
While terms of the agreement were not disclosed, these types of partnerships are estimated to go for upwards of $200 million per four-year cycle. In an interview with CNBC, John Slusher, a former Nike executive and CEO of the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Properties, called JPMorgan "as big a partner as we get."
JPMorgan is also a vote of confidence for the organization's highest level of sponsorship, called The Olympic Partners, which comes with exclusive marketing rights. The program, which was created in 1985, saw several major companies — including Panasonic, Toyota and Bridgestone — depart at the end of 2024.
Slusher has been revamping the business model to attract big-ticket sponsors. He said organizers created a joint venture across the various properties to put all rights in one place for commercialization, so a company can pursue one deal across the LA Olympics, Team USA and the Paralympics, if it chooses.
He also said they're trying out new marketing opportunities that extend beyond the games, including a torch relay that will extend for 100 days in all 50 U.S. states, as well as naming rights in a lot of the venues.
"We try to balance not overly commercializing the Olympics, which is really important, but also driving revenue, which helps us put on a better games," Slusher said.
JPMorgan's partnership includes the LA 2028 Olympic and Paralympic games, as well as the games in the French Alps in 2030.
The company also announced last week that it plans to hire more than 100 additional business bankers across Southern California — a 30% increase — pegged to its presence at the LA Games. The firm already has 5 million consumer-banking customers and 589,000 small-business clients in Los Angeles, it said.
"We think it's really important for us to bring in the ecosystem that supports these small businesses, so that they can take advantage of what's going on in the business of the Olympics," said Carla Hassan, chief marketing officer of JPMorgan.
Hassan called the Olympics partnership a "firm-wide initiative" for JPMorgan. She said the company will evaluate the return on investment through brand strength, client and customer engagement, customer acquisition and employee pride.
It's also the latest push for the firm that's heavily invested in the sports industry, including across Madison Square Garden in New York and the Chase Center in San Francisco, home to the NBA's Knicks and Golden State Warriors, respectively.
JPMorgan is also a longtime sponsor of the US Open Tennis Championships in New York, and it recently announced a multimillion-dollar deal to sponsor the athletic program at Ohio State University. And, earlier this year, it launched an Athlete Council, composed of all-star athletes including seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady and World Cup champion Alex Morgan, with the aim of improving financial literacy and wealth management for those in the sports industry.
Hassan said the opportunity to partner with the Olympics and Paralympics was unique and appealing because of its international reach.
"Very few partnerships are that global in nature, right?" Hassan said. "It really is its own animal."

title: An unreleased Anthropic model made progress on one of math’s biggest unsolved problems
summary: For more than 150 years, the Riemann hypothesis has stood as one of the major unsolved problems in mathematics. Anthropic hasn't solved it — but the company's models made more progress than you might expect.
full_text:
For more than 150 years, the Riemann hypothesis has stood as one of the major unsolved problems in mathematics, a long-running mystery about the distribution of prime numbers. There is currently a $1 million bounty for a working general proof of the hypothesis, which remains unclaimed.
Contemporary AI models still can’t solve it either — but they can make a lot more progress than you might expect, a finding that’s likely to reopen long-standing questions about contemporary AI’s ability to discover new scientific and mathematical ideas.
On Monday, Anthropic announced that an as-yet-unreleased model had made significant progress on the Riemann hypothesis, significantly increasing the lower bound of solutions for which the hypothesis holds true.
Even more impressive is how the progress was made: An Anthropic staff member without significant mathematical training prompted the model to “take a real stab” at proving the hypothesis, then left the model to coordinate the task across the following day and a half.
All told, the model tested 650 different ideas for solving the problem, coordinating across 60 sub-agents and spending 31 million in total.
“Out of the 60 subagents, two were responsible for developing the key mathematical ideas,” a footnote to the paper explains, “13 contributed ideas to these agents, 30 attempted (but were unable) to develop new ideas, 13 served as validators to check the correctness of the arguments, and the final two helped to write the initial paper.”
The finding was confirmed by two of Anthropic’s in-house mathematicians, and formalized using the open-source proof assistant Lean.
This is the latest in a string of mathematical breakthroughs led by Large Language Models, or LLMs. A number of Erdos problems have been solved by AI models over the course of this year, and the release of more powerful models has led to more impressive results. OpenAI recently released a set of ten major results proved by its internal “Astra” model, while a separate effort from Anthropic disproved the long-standing Jacobian conjecture.
The growing body of results has caused both excitement and concern in the mathematical field. In a public declaration signed in June, a group of prominent mathematicians raised concerns that AI could undermine critical values of the field — particularly the standard that true mathematical proofs should be “attributable to specific authors who take credit for their discovery and assume responsibility for their correctness.”
But the field is still split on how mathematicians should approach the new research techniques. In a blog post responding to the declaration, Fields Medal winner Timothy Gowers questioned whether the influence of AI might change mathematics in a more complex and positive way.
“If we arrive at a world where mathematical theorems are no longer associated with mathematicians, maybe that won’t be any more problematic than the fact that stars aren’t named after astronomers and most aren’t named at all,” Gowers wrote.

title: Joby Aviation builds out defense business with $500M acquisition
summary: Joby Aviation reached an agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, which will kick off its new defense business.
full_text:
Joby Aviation reached an agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences for $500 million in cash and stock, according to a regulatory filing posted Tuesday. This is the electric air taxi developer’s latest move to push deeper into the defense sector.
Ohio-based Resonant Sciences, which makes radio frequency and sensor systems, will become a dedicated defense business under Joby. Resonant Sciences’ co-founder and CEO J. Micah North will lead this new division, which will absorb Joby’s defense projects, including the development of a turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft, and autonomy technology stack.
The new defense division will allow the rest of Joby Aviation to focus on certifying, manufacturing, and launching its electric air taxi, the company said.
California-based Joby is best known as a company trying to develop and launch a network of electric urban air taxis that can shuttle people and goods over short distances. The company has also pursued defense, an effort that became more public over the past two years.
Last year, Joby signed an agreement with defense contractor L3Harris Technologies to “explore opportunities” to develop a new aircraft class — specifically, a gas-turbine hybrid vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft that can fly autonomously — for defense applications.
The gas-turbine hybrid VTOL will be based on Joby’s current S4 aircraft platform, the company said at the time. Joby has focused on developing the S4 with an all-electric powertrain, but in 2024 it demonstrated under a government contract a hydrogen-electric hybrid version that flew 521 miles — more than two times farther than its battery-electric prototype.
Joby’s acquisition of Resonant Sciences gives it a money-making business. Resonant has reported $100 million in trailing 12-month revenue, and access to classified programs run by the U.S. government. Resonant’s radio frequency and sensing tech also complements Joby’s own electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft (eVTOLs). 
Joby has tapped this revenue-generation-through-acquisition strategy before. Developing, certifying, and mass-producing eVTOLs is an expensive and years-long process, the kind of frontier tech that excites shareholders until they start wondering when the money is going to come in.
Joby, which went public in 2021 through a merger with a blank-check company, has assuaged investors by finding near-term sources of revenue.
Last year, Joby acquired Blade Air Mobility’s helicopter rideshare business for about $125 million. The acquisition gave Joby instant access to a network of 12 terminals in key markets like New York City as well as terminal bases at John F. Kennedy International Airport, Newark Liberty Airport, on both east and west sides of Manhattan, and Wall Street.
It also delivered much-needed revenue for Joby. The company reported $38.6 million in revenue in the second quarter, $36.2 million of which came from Blade.

title: Delta investigating after someone set up fake Wi-Fi network mid-flight
summary: The Delta flight crew switched off the aircraft's legitimate Wi-Fi network for around 30 minutes due to the incident, according to a spokesperson.
full_text:
An unidentified passenger allegedly created a fake Wi-Fi network on a Delta flight from Las Vegas to Atlanta on Monday, prompting pilots to alert air traffic control, according to the airline and public broadcasts from the plane.
“[The] safety of flight was never in question and no aircraft operating systems were affected,” Delta spokesperson Morgan Durrant told TechCrunch, adding that the in-flight network was not compromised.
“We are fully investigating to gather a complete set of facts, which will take time. We will partner with federal law enforcement and aviation regulators to ensure the incident is thoroughly investigated,” the spokesperson said.
The flight crew turned off the aircraft’s legitimate Wi-Fi network for around 30 minutes due to the incident.
Once the crew became aware of the fake Wi-Fi network, the pilots sent two messages mid-flight to air traffic control. The pilots said a passenger “created a scam Wi-Fi” that was designed to impersonate the airplane’s legitimate wireless network.
The pilots said they did not have any more information, but said some of the passengers came from cybersecurity conferences held in Las Vegas last week.
At this point, it’s unclear what the passenger or passengers were doing. It’s easy to set up a fake or malicious Wi-Fi network using commercially available tools like a Wi-Fi Pineapple, a hardware device designed for spoofing real-world networks. These devices are sold for professional security testers to audit companies’ security, or for hobbyists who want to learn how to hack.
The Atlanta Police Department referred questions to federal authorities. Federal Aviation Administration spokesperson Steve Kulm said the agency has not received a report about the incident. The FBI did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

title: 2025’s most downloaded game, Block Blast!, is going ad-free on Apple Arcade
summary: Block Blast!, the most downloaded mobile game of 2025, is coming to Apple Arcade in September, where it will be ad-free.
full_text:
The most downloaded mobile game last year has just landed on Apple’s subscription gaming service, Apple Arcade. On Tuesday, Apple announced the addition of Block Blast!+, an ad-free version of the popular puzzle game that has around 725 million lifetime installs, according to app intelligence provider Appfigures. Other estimates put that figure even higher, at 868 million installs.
The game will be released on Apple Arcade on September 3, alongside a 2025 App Store Award winner, Art of Fauna: Cozy Puzzles+, and others.
Apple’s internal data indicates that Block Blast! was the most downloaded free iPhone game in 2025. It has continued to rank No. 1 in the early months of 2026, according to its developer, Hungry Studio, and other third-party app intelligence providers, such as Sensor Tower.
Given that the puzzle game continues to acquire tens of millions of new users every month, it raises the question: Why would the studio offer an ad-free Arcade version now, before growth has plateaued? After all, just a few months ago, the studio reported that Block Blast! was still seeing high engagement, with 70 million daily active users and 300 million monthly active users worldwide. It even promoted the title at this year’s Coachella, suggesting there’s still room for growth.
However, a deeper dive into the data indicates Block Blast! downloads may have fallen from their peak in late 2024, when it was pulling in nearly 50 million downloads per month. This suggests the title is indeed maturing, which makes it a good candidate for Apple’s subscription service.
For Block Blast! fans, which are still many, the Arcade version will address the most annoying thing about playing this puzzler: all those ads. After every loss, ads play before you can start a new gaming session, leading users to swipe the game closed to skip the ad, then re-open the app to play again. It’s a tedious way to play this puzzle game, and one that has long seen fans begging for a subscription option to go ad-free. The Arcade version will now be that option.
Apple’s Arcade service is $6.99 per month for its 200+ games, or it can be bundled with Apple One plans, which start at $19.95/month for individuals.
Other titles launching on Arcade on September 3 include NFL Retro Bowl ’27, Coloring Games for Families+, and Let’s Play! Oink Games+, a digital collection of nine tabletop games.

title: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe is betting on EVs, robots, and autonomy all at once — he’ll explain why at Disrupt 2026
summary: Rivian's CEO RJ Scaringe is speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 to detail his journey, and the lessons it’s bestowed.
full_text:
Building a company is hard. But building one that also designs, manufactures, and delivers hardware at scale, from a factory floor, with supply chain concerns galore is another order of difficulty. And Rivian’s CEO RJ Scaringe is speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 to detail that journey and the lessons it’s bestowed.
Rivian sits at the intersection of AI, software, robotics, manufacturing, and transportation. And Scaringe has spent the better part of two decades proving that intersection isn’t just survivable. He also thinks it’s about to become much more crowded.
Scaringe’s Disrupt Stage session is just one of many big conversations happening at Disrupt this year, running October 13-15 at San Francisco’s Moscone Center. Check out the programming that’s been announced so far here, and if you don’t already have a ticket, lock in yours before our next price increase on August 22.
What Scaringe brings to the Disrupt Stage
Rivian has begun rolling out the R2, the roughly $58,000 SUV that Scaringe is counting on to do what the pricier R1T and R1S didn’t: expand Rivian beyond the niche market. He’s called it “maybe the most important thing we’ve launched to date” amid slowing demand for costlier EVs and mounting competitive pressure, especially from lower-cost Chinese EV manufacturers.
At the same time, Scaringe has been expanding beyond vehicles. He’s laid out a roadmap to full Level 4 autonomy by 2028, and he’s building out Rivian’s own charging network with ambitions to become one of the largest in the U.S.
Scaringe also founded Mind Robotics, a humanoid robotics company that’s raised $900 million this year alone, which he runs as executive chair and acting CEO, with Rivian as a large shareholder and launch customer. title: FlightAware sues Kalshi over flight cancellation prediction markets
summary: FlightAware says that Kalshi used its name and data to offer bets on flight cancellations without the flight tracker's permission.
full_text:
The real-time flight tracker FlightAware is suing the prediction market Kalshi for allegedly using its data to host gambling markets.
Kalshi started letting users bet on the number of flights canceled in the U.S., or at a given airport, about a month ago. According to FlightAware, Kalshi used FlightAware’s data and name without authorization, displaying FlightAware’s branding and information even after the flight tracker demanded that Kalshi stop.
“Kalshi never informed FlightAware that it would rely on FlightAware’s data to determine the outcome of these betting markets,” the lawsuit says. FlightAware maintains that it did not know about Kalshi’s flight cancellation bets until the media began reporting on these new prediction markets.
TechCrunch has reached out to Kalshi for comment.
Kalshi and similar platforms, like Polymarket, allow users to place bets on various future events, ranging from the results of a political election to the number of albums a musician will sell in a given week.
These markets have already shown their extensive potential to be manipulated by bettors, even though their rules prohibit insider trading. In one high-profile instance, a Polymarket user suspiciously bet $32,000 that Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro would be removed from power by the end of January — just hours later, the U.S. military captured Maduro, earning that user a $400,000 payout. A White House teleprompter operator allegedly made over $100,000 on Kalshi by using his advanced knowledge of the president’s speeches to place bets.
FlightAware argues that these gambling markets could similarly be abused to interfere with flights, posing a safety risk for travelers and airport employees.
FlightAware is seeking a jury trial and has not specified how much money it seeks in damages.

title: Trump to give Republicans a 3-1 FCC majority, isn't filling empty Democratic seat
summary: Trump has resisted urge to fire FCC Democrat despite recent Supreme Court win.
full_text:
The Federal Communications Commission has been shorthanded throughout President Trump’s second term, but it’s about to get a new commissioner. Unsurprisingly, Trump is breaking a historical norm with a nomination that would give Republicans a 3-1 advantage on the FCC.
Historically, the president and Senate worked together to ensure that the president’s party maintained only a one-vote majority. Normally, the president’s party has three FCC members while the minority party has two.
Instead of the typical 3-2 split, the FCC has operated with a 2-1 Republican majority during Trump’s second term. On Friday, Trump nominated Republican Danielle Thumann Severs to take one of the empty spots. Thumann Severs, a lawyer, has been working as FCC Chairman Brendan Carr’s senior counsel. She must be confirmed by the Republican-controlled Senate before being sworn in as a commissioner.
The FCC has played a leading role in Trump’s attacks on news broadcasters, with Carr using his position to investigate and threaten the licenses of broadcasters that don’t provide coverage favorable to Trump. A third Republican to cast votes at commission meetings will give Carr more support for his policies.
Every FCC commissioner must be confirmed by the Senate after receiving a nomination from the president. Even commissioners in the minority party need a presidential nomination.
If Trump followed the historical norm, he would have nominated one Republican and one Democrat to the FCC so they could be confirmed by the Senate simultaneously. Presidents typically nominate commissioners from the opposing party based on recommendations from the other party. That’s what Trump did in his first term when he nominated Democrat Geoffrey Starks based on a recommendation from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.
Since the FCC needs only three members for a quorum, adding a third Republican raises the possibility that Trump will fire the FCC’s only Democrat and give his party a 3-0 advantage. But stocking the commission with only Republicans would violate a law that prohibits any party from having an FCC supermajority, which could put the FCC’s decisions at greater risk of being blocked in court.
Senate Democrat: “That will be a problem”
While the Senate’s Republican majority can confirm Thumann Severs without any Democratic support, doing so without a paired Democratic nomination will result in a contentious confirmation process. Senate Democrats want Thumann Severs to be paired with a Democratic nominee so the commission can have a full slate of five members. But it doesn’t appear that Trump will nominate a Democrat for the fifth spot.
“That will be a problem. We want pairing,” Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) told Politico on Friday.
Cantwell is the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee, which will consider the nomination before it goes to a full Senate vote. The committee is chaired by Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas.), who told Politico that “we will assess the nomination on its merits.”
Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), the top Democrat on the telecommunications and media subcommittee, was quoted as saying that “if President Trump wants to fill these positions, he should do them in a bipartisan way. I would certainly hope my Republican colleagues on the committee want to see some semblance of balance as well. Because who’s going to be the next president?”
Shortly after his second term began, Trump declared sweeping power over historically independent agencies and fired both Democrats from the Federal Trade Commission. The Supreme Court upheld the FTC firing in a decision that solidified Trump’s power over an agency that historically was not under the direct control of the president. The FTC currently has just two commissioners, both Republicans, and three vacant seats.
Trump has resisted firing FCC’s only Democrat
The Supreme Court ruling on the FTC raised speculation that Trump would fire the FCC’s one Democrat, Anna Gomez, and have the FCC be run by Republicans only. But Gomez has still not been fired despite being a consistent critic of the Trump FCC’s attacks on news broadcasters and gutting of broadband consumer rules.
Gomez issued a statement congratulating Thumann Severs on Friday and said, “I look forward to continuing our work together, hopefully soon with a full commission of five, the way this agency was built to operate.” Carr issued a statement congratulating Thumann Severs but did not express any wish for a five-member commission.
New Street Research analyst Blair Levin, who was the FCC’s chief of staff from 1993 to 1997, did not expect Trump to fire Gomez and leave the agency with only two commissioners because that would have prevented the FCC from having a three-member quorum. Now that Trump has proposed filling one of the FCC’s empty seats, Levin told Ars on Monday that he does not think Trump will appoint a Democrat to fill the other empty seat.
Levin said Trump could nominate another commissioner who is not a Democrat, yet “qualifies as a non-Republican,” though Levin does not think this is a likely scenario. Nominating a fifth commissioner who is neither a Republican nor a Democrat, but who supports the Carr and Trump agenda, could effectively give Trump a 4-1 majority without technically violating the law prohibiting an FCC supermajority.
Another wrinkle is that Gomez’s term technically expired on June 30. US law allows her to serve until the end of 2027 or until the Senate confirms a replacement, whichever comes first. Gomez would need a renomination from Trump and confirmation from the Senate to continue past 2027, or she could be replaced earlier.
Hypothetically, Trump could aim for a 3-0 advantage or replace Gomez with someone “who qualifies as a non-Republican” and give Republicans a 3-1 FCC majority in which the minority member is from a third party or is an independent. Levin said he thinks Senate Republicans would let Trump make that kind of appointment even though they would “object to a Democratic president doing the same” in a future administration. But he doesn’t think Trump will do this.
“My guess is that the White House believes three Republicans constitute a quorum and therefore there is no need to use the political capital that would be necessary to appoint a non-Republican,” Levin said.
US law forbids FCC supermajority
The Communications Act requires the FCC to have three members for a quorum. The US telecom law also forbids supermajorities on the FCC by specifying that “the maximum number of commissioners who may be members of the same political party shall be a number equal to the least number of commissioners which constitutes a majority of the full membership of the Commission.”
If Trump decides to follow this law, Republicans would not be able to hold all three seats on a three-member FCC. On a four-member commission, three Republicans would be the “least number of commissioners which constitutes a majority.”
By adding a Republican and resisting the urge to fire Gomez, Trump can seat three Republican commissioners, while also complying with the law that prevents Republicans from taking a 4-1 or 5-0 advantage. The fact that Trump hasn’t fired Gomez yet might indicate he is willing to let the FCC operate with a 3-1 Republican majority for the rest of his presidency. This would ensure the FCC has the maximum number of Republican commissioners and the minimum of one Democrat.
Levin wrote in June that the Supreme Court’s FTC ruling doesn’t necessarily give Trump the same power to make the FCC a Republican-only agency.
“The law itself indicates that Congress intended the agency to always have members from both parties. That was not an accident,” Levin wrote. “When Congress created the FCC, it did not simply establish an independent agency. title: Razer Naga V3 Pro Review: Buttons Galore
summary: The PC gaming world has tried to move on from bulky, heavier mice, but the Naga V3 Pro proves that it still has its place.
full_text:
Comfortable shape. Hot-swappable side panels. Side finger rest doubles as a third button. Horizontal scrolling. Smooth scrolling. More buttons than anyone needs. Great internals.
TIRED
Heavy for a gaming mouse. Needs extra dongle for 8kHz polling. Only available in black.
One of my first gaming mice was the original Razer Naga Epic, which I was gifted as a teenager alongside my first gaming PC. Gaming has changed a lot in the past 15 years, and yet, the Razer Naga line hasn't changed much. It's general shape and function have remained remarkable consistent.
While PC gaming has come to emphasize ultra-lightweight, competitive mice designed for fast-paced shooters, that's not everyone's cup of tea. If you're a PC gamer who might prefer a more comfortable mouse—perhaps with some extra buttons—the new Naga V3 Pro just might be the best gaming mouse for you. The new model folds in some of the newest performance-focused innovations into a more practical and comfort-focused shape.
A Comfortable Grip
Comparing the current Naga to the models since 2015, the shape is nearly identical. The only major difference is the addition of a third mouse button. Recently, Razer has shifted its focus when refreshing mice for a new version: Instead of significantly redesigning the shape, new versions maintain a general silhouette and shell, while receiving significant updates to the internals. Considering how good the shapes of current offerings feel, it makes sense: There’s no reason to change purely for change’s sake, especially when something already works.
As far as that goes, the shell of the Naga V3 Pro is still quite nice. The large, wide shape is ideal for a palm grip, while still being usable with a claw. The third mouse button is a helpful touch, but with the locking mechanism underneath, I found its alternative use as a side support to be much more comfortable using either of these grips. (The third button was the most usable with a fingertip grip, where there wasn’t any risk of accidentally putting pressure on it.)
Photograph: Henri Robbins
Really, the shape is ideal for long-term use. It’s fairly ergonomic, and it's easy enough to lay your hand across with a relaxed grip. I found it to be a great option for raid nights in Destiny 2 (with as many as five or six Crota runs in one night) and more chill games like The Big Walk, where precision and agility take a bit of a back seat to consistency and comfort.
While the Naga V3 Pro weighs 116 grams with the heaviest twelve-button side panel (the six-button panel is 115 grams, and the two-button is 113), the mouse doesn’t feel particularly heavy. The weight is all kept fairly low, and is distributed well across the mouse. Compared to some older mice with high-up batteries and nose-heavy shapes, the Naga hardly feels like its weight; I would’ve guessed it was below 100 grams if I hadn’t checked. You’ll notice the added heft if you’re switching directly from a 60 gram gaming mouse, but otherwise, this mouse manages its mass very well.
One downside to its old-school vibe is the limited color options. Black is the only version available, and while that'll always be the most popular (especially for Razer), a more niche mouse like the Naga V3 Pro could have definitely benefitted from another color.
So Many Buttons
This mouse has an absurd number of buttons. I found myself struggling to use all of them, but I’m sure there are quite a few people who still won’t think it’s quite enough.
Like the Logitech MX Master 4, the Naga incorporates a customizable mouse wheel with options for smooth or ratcheting operation, along with a “precision tactile” mode that decreases the space between each of the scrolling steps. The wheel also has a tilt function for horizontal scrolling; it’s ideal for spreadsheets and multimedia work that requires two axes of movement, but can just as easily be remapped to any number of macros (I could see it being useful for leaning to the left or right in a tactical shooter like Rainbow Six: Siege).
Drawing further comparisons to the MX Master line, I really found this mouse to be good for everyday work. The comfortable shape and extensive navigation capabilities made it great for multimedia work, and the number pad was ideal for mapping software-specific functions, especially for photo and video editing software that can require some repetitive and complex inputs.
Despite the sheer number of buttons, I really found that they never got in the way when not in use. All of them are placed in such a way to be easily accessible without disrupting the basic left and right click functionality. The only button I found myself regularly pressing on accident was the third click button, which can be locked entirely using a switch on the underside of the mouse.
Photograph: Henri Robbins
The spotlight feature of this mouse is the interchangeable side panels, which offer two, six or twelve customizable buttons. These attach magnetically using a grid of pogo pins, and underneath the panels is a small cubby to store the USB dongle. Swapping these out is entirely effortless, taking only a few seconds, and Razer Synapse will automatically detect which of these three panels is attached, storing specific, customizable keymaps for each of them.
Of the three, I gravitated towards the two-button panel, which replicates a “standard” gaming mouse with larger buttons. I found the size of these chunky buttons to be preferable to the ultra-thin buttons found on most gaming mice, creating more surface area while still maintaining a reasonably large rubberized grip pad underneath. These will naturally be best for first-person shooters that require more agility and less customized keys.
The six-button option is a great option for games with occasional macros, or for movement-based games where you want your fingers on WASD at all times. While the shape of these elevated keys may look odd at first, they feel natural once you’ve acclimated. It’s easy enough to rock your thumb upwards from the rubberized pad to activate the bottom row, and you can sit your thumb on top of the curved surface of the buttons to have easy access to all six at once. The buttons are distinct enough that you can press the middle and back buttons with the center and rear areas of your fingertip without having to adjust significantly.
The twelve-button side panel eschews the rubberized section for full coverage with a numpad-like layout. This panel crams as many distinct keys as possible, aligning them along a basic grid. Unlike a traditional number pad or earlier versions of the Naga, it removes the homing bar on the second row — a detail I definitely wish was still present, even if the sculpted shape makes it easier to locate specific keys without it. While this side panel is ideal for ability-heavy games like MMOs or MOBAs, it has the strongest learning curve, especially when trying to utilize all of the buttons. It’s great once you’ve gotten used to the massive expanse of vaguely-similar buttons though. Just be ready to mess up at least a few inputs when you accidentally fat-finger two buttons at once or forget exactly where an ability is mapped.
Longevity
Photograph: Henri Robbins
Internally, this mouse is best described as over-engineered. The internals are robust, fastener-rich, and include some extra features for sturdiness that I wouldn’t otherwise expect. The internal plastic braces are all beefy, and there are plastic supports and cradles for the main buttons’ circuit boards. Comparing this mouse to any of the ultra-light models available today, it becomes obvious just how much effort goes into making them lightweight and what a mouse can look like when weight-savings stop being a priority.

title: 俄羅斯央行提議：開放 BTC、ETH、USDT 交易所買賣，散戶每年限額 3650 鎂
summary:
俄羅斯加密貨幣合法化再邁大步！據《Cointelegraph》報導，俄羅斯央行已正式發布建議清單，提議允許比特 […]

〈俄羅斯央行提議：開放 BTC、ETH、USDT 交易所買賣，散戶每年限額 3650 鎂〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
俄羅斯加密貨幣合法化再邁大步！據《Cointelegraph》報導，俄羅斯央行已正式發布建議清單，提議允許比特幣（BTC）、以太坊（ETH）與 USDT 三大加密資產在受監管的交易所進行公開交易。為保護一般投資人，非合格投資者每年將面臨約 3,650 美元的購買上限。此舉標誌著俄羅斯在總統普丁簽署新法後，正式啟動加密市場的合規化進程。
（前情提要：俄羅斯加密貨幣交易所 Grinex 遭駭 10 億盧布！官方宣布無限期停運，衝擊俄國金融避險管道）
（背景補充：俄羅斯最大銀行 Sberbank 年底將推加密錢包，9 月新法全面解禁數位資產）
俄羅斯在加密貨幣監管政策上迎來重大突破。台北時間 8 月 11 日，據外媒 Cointelegraph 報導，俄羅斯央行（Bank of Russia）已編制了一份最新的建議清單，正式提議允許比特幣（Bitcoin）、以太坊（Ether）以及 Tether 發行的穩定幣 USDT 等三種主流加密資產，進入該國受監管的交易所進行公開交易。
這項破天荒的提案，是在俄羅斯總統普丁（Vladimir Putin）於 8 月 4 日簽署數位貨幣新法後，官方首度祭出的具體監管方針。該法律正式授權俄羅斯央行決定哪些數位貨幣可進入有組織的交易市場，並賦予其制定相關交易規則的權力。
嚴篩上市標準，散戶每年限額 30 萬盧布
為何唯獨這三種加密貨幣能率先獲得俄羅斯央行的青睞？央行在聲明中解釋，比特幣、以太坊與 USDT 成功符合了當局設定的嚴格標準，這些條件包括龐大的市場總值、極高的平均每日交易量，以及在海外市場必須擁有至少五年的價格歷史紀錄。
然而，為了防範加密貨幣價格劇烈且不可預測的波動風險，央行也針對投資者祭出了分級保護措施。根據新擬定的規則，對於「非合格投資者（散戶）」，每年透過單一中介機構（包含券商、加密交易所或資產管理公司）最多僅能購買價值 30 萬俄羅斯盧布（約合 3,650 美元）的加密貨幣；相對地，「合格投資者」在交易所或場外市場進行交易時，則不受任何購買額度的限制。
強制風險測驗，新規徵求意見至 8/24
此外，新規也特別強調了投資者的風險教育。俄羅斯央行明文規定，無論是合格或非合格投資者，在實際進行任何加密貨幣交易前，都必須強制通過相關測試，以確保他們充分了解投資數位資產可能面臨的高風險。
目前，這項允許三大加密資產在交易所掛牌的提議，正處於公開徵求意見的階段。央行表示，公眾諮詢的截止日期為 2026 年 8 月 24 日。隨著截止日期的逼近，俄羅斯能否藉由這套監管框架成功引導龐大的地下資金走向檯面，將成為全球總體經濟與加密市場密切關注的焦點。

title: Manus 告別 Meta 重獲自由！宣布恢復獨立營運，急籲用戶完成資料備份
summary:
歷經被科技巨頭高價收購，又遭監管機關強力逆轉的戲劇性轉折後，曾紅極一時的 AI 明星新創 Manus 終於宣告 […]

〈Manus 告別 Meta 重獲自由！宣布恢復獨立營運，急籲用戶完成資料備份〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
歷經被科技巨頭高價收購，又遭監管機關強力逆轉的戲劇性轉折後，曾紅極一時的 AI 明星新創 Manus 終於宣告「重獲自由」！據 Manus 官方於 11 日發布的最新公告指出，該公司即將恢復以獨立公司的形式運作。作為與 Meta 拆分過渡的一部分，官方要求部分受影響的用戶必須在 8 月 23 日前完成資料備份，以符合特定司法管轄區的監管要求。
（前情提要：騰訊傳擬以 20 億美元從 Meta 手中買回 Manus，躍居最大股東）
（背景補充：Meta 已把 Manus 關進防火牆：禁止雙向存取內部系統，20 億美元收購案被強制拆解）
在人工智慧發展的浪潮中，地緣政治與監管的角力正深刻改變著科技版圖。台北時間 8 月 11 日，以通用自主 AI Agent 聞名的新創公司 Manus 透過其官方 X 帳號與部落格發布了一封名為「A Note to Our Users（給用戶的信）」的公告，正式向外界宣告即將恢復獨立營運的重大消息。
A Note to Our Users
Manus will soon resume operating as an independent company.
As part of this transition and to comply with regulatory requirements in specific jurisdictions, some users will need to back-up their data before 7:59 a.m. on August 23, 2026 (SGT) and then begin…
— Manus (@ManusAI) August 11, 2026
被 Meta 收購遭中國逆轉，Manus 走上拆分之路
這份公告背後，隱藏著一段震驚矽谷與中國科技圈的併購波折。回顧 2025 年 12 月底，Meta 豪擲約 20 億美元火速收購了 Manus，意圖將其頂尖的 Agentic AI 技術整合進 Meta 生態系。然而，這筆跨境交易卻觸動了中國監管機構的敏感神經。
2026 年初，中國國家發展和改革委員會（NDRC）以涉嫌違反技術出口管制與國家安全為由介入審查，並在 4 月底罕見地下令強制撤回該筆已完成的收購案。經歷數月的系統切斷與資料隔離後，Manus 終於在原投資方的回購支持下，重新找回了獨立公司的身分。
合規要求：部分用戶需在 8/23 前備份資料
為了徹底完成與 Meta 的分離，並符合特定司法管轄區的監管要求，Manus 在公告中提出了具體的資料處理過渡方案。官方指出，部分在 2025 年 12 月 29 日（即 Meta 收購日）及之後產生資料的用戶，將受到此次合規步驟的影響。
受影響的用戶必須在新加坡時間 2026 年 8 月 23 日上午 7 點 59 分之前，透過官方提供的入口完成資料備份（期間可多次備份）；隨後，官方將於 8 月 25 日上午 8 點重新開放還原入口，讓用戶能將資料還原並從中斷處繼續使用。官方強調，這絕非資安事件，純粹是為了合規拆分，未來這些資料將主要存放於美國與新加坡伺服器。
過渡期免收費，承諾「最好的還在後頭」
為了降低對用戶的不便，Manus 承諾會透過電子郵件與 App 內通知主動聯繫受影響的用戶（提醒使用 Apple ID 或 Facebook 註冊者需特別留意 App 內通知）。此外，在過渡期間，公司將不會向受影響的用戶收取任何費用，並將提供專屬的「歡迎回來」獎勵作為補償，客服團隊也將 24 小時全天候待命協助。至於未收到通知的帳號，則無需進行任何操作，可繼續正常使用。
在經歷了這場史無前例的併購風暴後，Manus 團隊在公告最後展現了對未來的強烈信心：「我們對未來感到無比興奮，並正準備推出一系列新功能，將再次推動通用 AI Agent 的可能性⋯⋯最好的還在後頭。」

full_text:
被視為全球最大比特幣「巨鯨」的上市公司 Strategy（前身為 MicroStrategy）近期罕見拋售比特幣，引發市場高度關注。對此，該公司執行長 Phong Le 於 10 日接受 Fox Business 專訪時親上火線澄清，強調賣幣僅是為了擴充現金儲備的短期資本管理措施。他霸氣承諾，公司在今年接下來的時間將會「重新開始買入更多比特幣」，並立志將 Strategy 打造為「數位經濟的摩根大通」。
（前情提要：微策略 Strategy 上週再拋售 1690 枚比特幣！連兩週倒貨 3327 枚 BTC）
（背景補充：Michael Saylor：我用 ChatGPT 設計優先股方案，Strategy 靠 AI 融資 150 億美元）
全球持有最多比特幣的上市企業 Strategy（股票代號 MSTR，前身為 MicroStrategy），其一舉一動向來是加密貨幣市場的重要風向球。台北時間 8 月 10 日，Strategy 執行長 Phong Le 登上了 Fox Business 的財經節目《The Claman Countdown》，針對近期公司打破「只買不賣」神話、罕見拋售比特幣的舉動進行了詳細說明，試圖安撫市場的擔憂情緒。
小額賣幣只為存現金，儲備狂飆至 47.5 億鎂
根據最新披露的數據，2026 年以來 Strategy 已累計賣出約 6,948 枚 BTC，套現約 4.33 億美元；其中最新一筆交易發生在 8 月初，以平均 64,262 美元的價格賣出了 1,690 枚 BTC。對此，Phong Le 在訪談中明確表示，這些拋售動作純屬暫時性的資本結構調整。
他指出，公司過去幾個月的戰略重心在於建立龐大的美元現金儲備，目前已將現金部位從約 8 億美元大幅推升至 47.5 億美元。這筆資金主要用於強化資產負債表，並足以覆蓋未來約 2.7 年的優先股股息與利息。Phong Le 坦言，公司在 2026 年學到了一個重要教訓：「機構投資人與優先股投資人，並不會把流動性極高的比特幣直接視為等同於現金。」
帳面虧損逾 87 億美元，仍立志當「數位經濟小摩」
儘管 Strategy 目前的總持倉量已降至約 840,447 枚 BTC（仍佔全球比特幣總供應量約 4%），且由於平均持倉成本高達 75,385 美元，目前帳面上承受著約 87 至 95 億美元的未實現虧損；但管理層對長期戰略依然充滿信心。
Phong Le 在節目中給出了一劑強心針：「我們會在今年接下來的時間，重新開始買入更多比特幣。」他強調，公司的決策是由他與執行董事長 Michael Saylor 每天密集溝通 3 至 4 次所共同制定，並非單純追逐短期的幣價波動。Phong Le 更在受訪後透過 X（前 Twitter）發文重申，Strategy 的終極目標是成為「數位經濟的摩根大通（JPMorgan）」。
定位「放大版比特幣」，股價表現超車現貨
值得注意的是，Strategy 的靈活資本操作已在傳統金融市場取得顯著成效。公司在 6 月底正式推出的「BTC Monetization Program」，允許在必要時出售部分比特幣來支援現金需求，這項從極端囤幣轉向穩健資產管理的轉變，獲得了華爾街的青睞。
Phong Le 總結道，Strategy 的市場定位是「放大版比特幣（Amplified Bitcoin Play）」，核心目標是透過增加「每股比特幣持有量」來長期跑贏比特幣本身的漲幅。他自豪地指出，過去一年比特幣上漲了約 33%，而 Strategy 的股價則繳出了上漲 42% 的優異成績。

title: Nvidia 推出 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 開源 AI 模型，單一 GPU 即可運行 AI 代理
summary:
矽谷科技巨頭的 AI 戰火正迅速向「開源」領域蔓延。據《CNBC》報導，輝達（Nvidia）正式發表了名為 N […]

〈Nvidia 推出 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 開源 AI 模型，單一 GPU 即可運行 AI 代理〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
矽谷科技巨頭的 AI 戰火正迅速向「開源」領域蔓延。據《CNBC》報導，輝達（Nvidia）正式發表了名為 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 的全新開源人工智慧模型。這是執行長黃仁勳公開捍衛開源模式後，官方推出的首款開源大作，主打能在單一 GPU 上運行的輕量級「代理（Agent）」應用。此舉不僅貫徹了黃仁勳認為「免費 AI 能帶動晶片銷售」的商業策略，也為當前白熱化的中美 AI 競爭投下新變數。
（前情提要：NVIDIA Vera 基準測試出爐！加速代理式 AI 儲存，加密與資料恢復快逾 3 倍）
（背景補充：AI 助攻量子運算！NVIDIA 開源 31B 視覺模型 Ising 1.5，全自動校準量子電腦）
台北時間 8 月 11 日，據外媒《CNBC》報導，AI 晶片霸主輝達（Nvidia）正式發表了一款名為 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 的全新開源大語言模型。這不僅是全球開發者矚目的技術焦點，更是自上個月輝達執行長黃仁勳（Jensen Huang）在社群平台上公開力挺開源模式以來，該公司所祭出的首款開源重磅武器。
輕量級模型，主攻單一 GPU 運行與 AI 代理
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 被輝達定位為一款極致的「輕量級（Lightweight）」模型，其最大亮點在於能直接在一般筆記型電腦或桌上型電腦的單一 GPU 上高效運行。企業與開發者目前已可透過開源社群 Hugging Face 或輝達官網免費下載、使用及修改，且完全免除任何授權費用。
輝達指出，該模型透過先進的「模型蒸餾（Distillation）」技術，使其能在極低算力消耗下，展現出與體積龐大的大型 Nemotron 模型相媲美的強大能力。特別的是，這款模型針對能在背景自主運行的「代理（Agents）」程式進行了深度優化開發。目前包含資安大廠 CrowdStrike、程式碼審查工具 CodeRabbit 與 AI 法律助手 Harvey 等多家知名企業，皆已開始測試並客製化導入此模型。同時，輝達也同步推出名為 NeMo Switchyard 的軟體，能為特定任務自動選擇最便宜且最適合的 AI 模型。
黃仁勳強力背書：免費 AI 帶動硬體銷售
這項開源策略的背後，是黃仁勳對未來 AI 生態系與輝達商業版圖的精準算計。黃仁勳在 7 月下旬曾首度在 X（前 Twitter）發文，向美國政府呼籲應全力支持開源模型，並警告「避免過早限制」，否則恐導致創新能量流失海外。
他在一封公開信中強調，開放權重（Open-weight）模型能賦予企業對未來的掌控權、促進市場競爭，並達到降低價格與強化網路安全的效果。「免費的 AI 對硬體來說應該很好。免費的 AI 對晶片來說應該很好，」黃仁勳在近期的訪談中直言不諱地表示。對輝達而言，開源 AI 能大幅降低大眾與企業的使用門檻，相較於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 等昂貴的專有模型，開源模式將進一步刺激全球對輝達 GPU 算力的龐大需求。
牽動地緣政治，中美 AI 科技戰升溫
輝達此次發布新模型的時間點，恰逢華盛頓當局對開源 AI 政策展開激烈辯論之際。隨著中國 AI 獨角獸 Moonshot AI 所推出的 Kimi K3 模型在效能上逐漸逼近美國頂尖模型，美國政策制定者對其可能透過「蒸餾」技術竊取美國智慧財產的國安疑慮日益加深，甚至正研擬是否要對中國模型開發者祭出類似晶片禁令的嚴厲制裁。
在這場交織著地緣政治與科技路線的交鋒中，開源已成為矽谷的絕對主旋律。除了輝達積極佈局，Meta 執行長祖克柏（Mark Zuckerberg）近期也發表長篇宣言力挺開源，並推出 Muse Spark 程式碼模型，誓言要讓美國的開源模型稱霸全球。不僅如此，輝達更將在數天後與微軟（Microsoft）等巨頭共組 AI 安全聯盟，專注於使用開源模型來強化網路安全，預示著一場由開源驅動的 AI 產業革命正全面爆發。

title: Burnham 'confident' early release of PC Harper's killers can be halted
summary: The PM says the justice secretary will present a plan in September to prevent more early releases.
full_text:
Burnham 'confident' early release of PC Harper's killers can be halted
- Published
Andy Burnham says he is "confident" PC Andrew Harper's killers can be excluded from the government's early release scheme, as outcry over the case grows.
The prime minister has now ordered the justice secretary to find a way to bar Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were jailed for 13 years for manslaughter in 2020, from early release.
It marks a shift from last week, when he said there was "nothing more" he could do without risking the collapse of the prison system.
The move comes after days of pressure to exclude Harper's killers from the scheme, which is aiming to free about 5,000 offenders in England and Wales to make space in overcrowded jails.
Harper's mother, Debbie Adlam, told the BBC she was in "turmoil" following conflicting reports about whether two of her son's killers would be released from prison early, describing the handling of the situation as a "hash".
Conservative shadow home secretary Chris Philp accused Burnham and Labour of "re-traumatising victims and their families with their constant U-turns".
Burnham said a new plan to prevent more prisoners from being freed long before the end of their sentences would be presented to Parliament in September.
It comes after he initially announced some prisoners convicted of rape, serious child sex and other grooming offences would be barred from early release, after a review of the scheme he ordered after he became prime minister.
In an article published last week, external, Burnham said he had "wanted to go even further" but had "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do".
He added: "I know I can look people in the eye and say to them there is nothing more I could have asked for without risking the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing within months."
But on Tuesday, Burnham insisted he had never accepted "there was nothing more that could be done" to prevent the early release of more offenders, including Harper's killers.
"I came into office and started pushing on this issue, and I have pushed every single day in office," he added.
Burnham said he would seek to hold talks with other political parties to build "consensus" on the approach to early releases.
The government's early release scheme aims to address a severe overcrowding crisis in jails, where useable capacity is almost at 100%.
The number of places in jails in England and Wales has not kept pace with the significant rise in the prison population in recent decades under successive governments.
Ministers have said prison spaces might run out as soon as October.
To make more space in prisons, the Starmer government changed the law to give it the ability to release some offenders earlier than they would otherwise have been.
The release point for these prisoners will move from 40% or half of their custodial term to one third for some offenders, and from two thirds to half for others.
Since taking office, Burnham made exemptions for those convicted of some serious offences, but not manslaughter, prompting a backlash and pressure to block the release of Harper's killers.
Harper, 28, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged behind the getaway car of three teenagers who had fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.
Two of his killers, Cole and Bowers, will become eligible to be freed from jail next year under the release scheme as it stands.
The third man jailed for the manslaughter of Harper - the vehicle driver Henry Long - was given a longer 16-year jail term and cannot be considered for early release.
It is not yet clear how the government will prevent Cole and Bowers from being treated the same as other prisoners with similar sentences.
At the end of June, there were 1,015 people in prison in England and Wales for manslaughter, including 950 men and 65 women, according to the Ministry of Justice. It is not known how many of these are eligible for early release.
Probation strike threat
Last week, Burnham also ordered an "urgent" review to identify any grooming gang members who may be eligible to be freed from jail early.
The government has not confirmed whether the review will lead to the prevention of any early releases of offenders convicted of grooming-related crimes.
Offenders being released from prison partway through their sentences is a well-established feature of the UK's justice system.
It is not uncommon for offenders to serve some of their sentence in the community, under the supervision of the probation service and subject to restrictions, such as electronic tag monitoring.
The government has promised to put in place tougher probation conditions on offenders when the new early release scheme is rolled out.
But Napo, the probation union, said the system is already struggling to cope, warning a bigger workload will put public safety at risk.
It announced on Tuesday that said 90% of its members had backed potential industrial action if its concerns over "excessive workloads" in the system are not addressed.
"The government cannot keep treating probation as the place where the consequences of failures elsewhere in the criminal justice system are dumped," Napo national chair Ben Cockburn said.

title: The Office actress Lucy Davis says she has 'incurable' cancer
summary: Davis, who played receptionist Dawn in the UK sitcom, says the cancer has spread and it's "too late for chemo".
full_text:
The Office actress Lucy Davis says she has 'incurable' cancer
- Published
Lucy Davis, who played Dawn Tinsley in the original UK version of The Office, has revealed she has "incurable" breast cancer.
Davis, the daughter of comedian Jasper Carrott, starred as the office receptionist in the groundbreaking sitcom, which ran from 2001 to 2003.
A post from the 53-year-old actress on Instagram, external on Tuesday said: "I wanted to share something with you all that I've kept to myself for a while but for various reasons would like to share now.
"A year-and-a-half ago I was diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer, which has metastasized to my bones. Specifically to my spine, right hip and my ribs. The cancer is incurable, and too late for chemo."
She added: "The initial lump that I felt, wasn't a 'lump' as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny. I almost didn't bother getting it checked. So I guess I'm saying don't ignore anything – get everything checked out.
"As of now, I'm trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can. I always like to find the teachable moments in anything negative that happens. And cancer has not disappointed in that regard; there's a lot I have learned from it, and I'm grateful for that."
She continued: "I'm not scared of whatever comes next. I'm at peace with it. I'll see my [late dog] Gracie sooner than expected, and for me, leaving my physical body just means going home. Any and all grieving is for my family; it's far harder for them than for me."
'Cancer asks a lot from us'
Birmingham-born Davis played receptionist Dawn, who was the love interest of Tim Canterbury, played by Martin Freeman in Ricky Gervais's TV comedy classic.
After The Office, Davis went on to feature as Dianne in 2004 comedy-horror film Shaun of the Dead and Etta Candy in 2017's Wonder Woman, as well as Hilda Spellman in Netflix series The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina.
More recently, she played Eva in the Disney Channel's action comedy series The Villains of Valley View.
In her Instagram post - which was accompanied by a video of her reading a poem while ringing a bell in hospital - she went on to say she intended to keep up her work supporting animal rights, which is "so important to me".
She went on: "I still would like to keep working. I'm perfectly able to do so, and acting is one of the biggest joys in my life.
"For those of you on a similar journey to mine, I do wish you well. Cancer asks a lot from us, physically and mentally. And we all get to do it however we choose."

title: Russia releases former US Marine reported in poor health
summary: Robert Gilman, who was arrested in 2022 for kicking a police officer while drunk, had reportedly been in a catatonic-like state.
full_text:
Russia releases former US Marine reported in poor health
- Published
Russia has released a former US Marine who was jailed in 2022 and was reportedly in extremely poor health.
Robert Gilman, from Massachusetts, was freed "from detention for humanitarian reasons" and flying on a US plane to Washington, DC, on Tuesday, according to Kirill Dmitriev, special envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey posted on social media that Gilman had been "essentially catatonic" and battling a "severe case of pneumonia" before he was released.
Gilman was 28 when he was arrested for kicking a police officer while drunk aboard a train to Moscow.
"Approximately 50 days ago, Robert was diagnosed with a dissociative stupor - a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat," Markey said, adding that the details of Gilman's current condition were unknown.
Reuters reported that multiple doctors were tending to Gilman as he returned to the US and that a US official said "he seems to be in good shape".
His family is awaiting his arrival at a military hospital in Texas, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.
"I am so grateful to President Trump for saving my brother's life," Lexie Hudson, his sister said in a statement. "There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action."

title: Three ways to watch safely without glasses
summary: With some shops running out of stock, it may be too late to buy eclipse glasses - but you can still safely watch the spectacle using some household items.
full_text:
Three ways to watch the solar eclipse safely without glasses
- Published
With some online orders not able to arrive until the end of the week and shops running out of stock, it may be too late to buy eclipse glasses in time for Wednesday.
But you can still safely watch the spectacle using some household items.
People in the UK will see a partial eclipse - rather than the total eclipse that will be seen in parts of Spain, Greenland and Iceland - but it is the country's most significant eclipse since 1999.
Experts say enthusiasts should not to look directly at the Sun without specialist glasses.
And you shouldn't be tempted to try using sunglasses or dark goggles instead.
They often don't give enough UV protection when looking directly at the Sun and you could end up seriously damaging your eyesight, according to The Royal Astronomical Society.
Here are some viewing methods to try instead.
Pinhole projector - card, paper and pen
The astronomy group suggests creating a pinhole projector, which can be done by making a hole in a piece of card. You can use the tip of a ballpoint pen to push through the centre of it.
Holding the card in one hand and a blank piece of paper in the other, face away from the Sun.
Then line the card and paper up so that an image of the Sun becomes visible on the paper.
This pinhole projector will show you the shadow being cast on the Sun replicated in miniature.
- Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low 
  - Published29 minutes ago
Colander - find one in the kitchen
Instead of straining vegetables and pasta, you can use a colander to achieve a similar effect to that of the pinhole projector.
Eye specialist David Jones, consultant ophthalmologist at the Royal Cornwall Hospital Trust, says this is his favourite way of witnessing an eclipse.
"If you hold the colander to the Sun and you look away from the Sun, protecting your eyes, you can make not just one picture of the Sun but a hundred all at once."
Demonstrating the technique in a video on social media, he clutches a blank piece of paper behind the colander he is holding up.
It creates a kaleidoscope of images showing the Sun and the shadow cast on it during the eclipse.
Pinhole viewer - cardboard box, foil, paper
An empty cereal box is ideal for making a pinhole viewer. It works similarly to the projector but should provide a clearer image.
This is because the cardboard box blocks out the surrounding sunshine and allows in only light from the direction of the eclipse.
Cut out a piece of paper that fits the bottom of the box. Open the top of the box and tape the cutout to the bottom. This will be the screen on which you see the eclipse.
Close the box and tape it shut. On one half of the top of it, cut out a small square so you can see the paper at the bottom with one eye.
On the other half, cut out another small square to match. Cut out a piece of foil that is large enough to cover this square.
Tape it down over the square and use a pin or needle to poke a hole in the middle of the foil.
Standing with your back to the Sun, use one eye to look through the open square.
Once you've lined up the hole in the foil with the Sun, you should see an image of it on the screen at the bottom. This is where you'll see the eclipse too.
Can I not use my phone?
You might be tempted to video the eclipse using your mobile phone but Nasa advises against this., external
"To take images when the Sun is partially eclipsed, you'll need to use a special solar filter to protect your camera, just as you'll need a pair of solar viewing glasses (also called eclipse glasses) to protect your eyes."
They also say sensors in your phone could be damaged if pointed directly at the Sun.
"This is especially true if you're using any sort of magnifying lens attachment on the phone."
When the partial eclipse becomes visible in the UK and mainland Europe on Wednesday, it will be in the evening so it will take place low in the sky.
For a better view, the Royal Astronomical Society advises you try standing somewhere more elevated than the area around you "with a clear view of the western horizon".
Whatever you do, don't look directly at the Sun.

title: Weather forecast - where will the best view be?
summary: Look to the skies on Wednesday because one of the most spectacular solar eclipses for decades is coming the UK's way with likely optimum viewing conditions for many.
full_text:
Solar eclipse 2026 weather forecast – where and when will the best view be?
- Published
One of the most spectacular solar eclipses the UK has seen for decades is taking place on Wednesday 12 August.
From around 18:00 BST, the Moon will begin moving across the face of the Sun, creating a partial solar eclipse across the UK.
At its peak, around 90% of the Sun will be covered from London. In Cornwall, as much as 95% of the Sun could be obscured.
Depending on where you are in the UK, it will peak between 19:02 and 19:16 BST.
The UK is stuck in the middle of two different weather systems.
High pressure lies across much of continental Europe with low pressure and weather fronts out towards the north of the Atlantic.
This means contrasting fortunes.
High pressure is expected to bring generally dry and settled conditions across much of the UK, with a hot and sunny day forecast for most.
That means clear skies should give many a good view of the eclipse.
However, across some parts of north Wales, northern England and especially Scotland and Northern Ireland, areas of cloud could push their way through between 18:00 and 19:00 BST.
Across some parts of western Scotland and in towards the north and west of Northern Ireland, we see cloud bring some outbreaks of rain.
There may be some cloud for those watching in Iceland, the best of any gaps in the north, with rain in the south.
For Spain and Portugal the view is looking near perfect with clear skies.
The Sun will be very low in the western sky during the eclipse so ideally find somewhere with a clear, unobstructed view towards the west - somewhere high up and away from trees and buildings.
It is the closest thing to a total eclipse the UK will see for quite some time - and definitely one worth watching.

title: Burnham faces unpopularity test over prisons dilemma
summary: The early release conundrum has given the new PM his first taste of tricky political decision-making.
full_text:
Burnham faces unpopularity test over prisons dilemma
- Published
In his first few weeks in Downing Street, Andy Burnham could hardly have been clearer that his aim as prime minister is to make people feel better.
His supporters inside the Labour Party characterise him as a leader with the political nous to prioritise policies that will make a difference, and the communication ability to sell those messages to the masses.
His critics, including Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, have branded him a "people pleaser" who doesn't want to take difficult decisions.
The conundrum over how to manage the early release of prisoners is an acute example of the tricky political decision-making that inevitably comes with power.
Andy Burnham could have chosen to modify the early release scheme, which he inherited from the Starmer government, according to the length of offenders' sentences.
That would have seen some rapists and child sex offenders released, and inevitably lead to emotive stories from victims whose abusers were being set free.
Instead, the fledgling PM focused on the type of crime, ensuring those mentioned above would stay behind bars.
But that caused a political storm of its own, as it emerged that two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper would still be eligible for early release next year.
That quickly became the first big test for an administration that prides itself on its ability to communicate.
And after mounting pressure from the public, media and members of PC Harper's family, there does now appear to have been a shift.
'A hash'
Burnham said this morning he had "not accepted that it is impossible to do more" to prevent dangerous criminals being released early – and said he's asked the justice secretary to fast-track a plan for freeing up prison places.
He insisted that didn't constitute a change, saying he had been "pushing on this issue" since his first day in office.
But his latest view was not the impression created by the government in recent days.
On Monday lunchtime, Downing Street heavily suggested it could do no more.
Over the weekend, the Ministry of Justice said that exempting more prisoners from early release risked "prisons reaching capacity and collapsing".
And last week, Burnham himself wrote in the Telegraph that he'd "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do". Justice Secretary Alex Norris even apologised to the families of victims, including PC Andrew Harper.
PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam told BBC Breakfast the handling of the situation had been a "hash".
Sparse details
Downing Street will hope the events of the last week will be remembered as a PM who has forced the system to do what he wanted.
But they'll fear that the lasting impression could instead be of a misstep that's left victims' families in anguish.
Details of the government's plan to free up prison spaces are still sparse.
The government has been clear that it believes an exemption for manslaughter convictions is an all or nothing approach – and could therefore require a large amount of prison capacity.
Ministers are exploring how to speed up deportations of foreign criminals, the use of female prison spaces for male offenders, and indefinite sentences handed out in past decades.
None of those ideas sound easy, and there'll be questions over whether they will create enough space on the prison estate.
Even if success comes on that front, the PM's statement included an acknowledgement that the difficulties surrounding this policy are not over.
"Even with all these changes, there will be concerns from many victims about who will still be released early for other offences," Burnham said.
When those concerns arise in the coming months, a prime minister who wants to make people feel better may find himself under pressure again.
