title: ‘The Worst I’ve Ever Seen’: Cargo Thefts Have Turned Violent in Pursuit of AI Hardware
summary: Experts allege that two recent incidents in California show the extreme lengths that criminal organizations are willing to go to to steal servers and other gear meant for data centers.
full_text:
During the 25 years Gerardo Pachuca has spent investigating thieves who steal cargo from semitrucks, he says he’s never seen behavior this brazen. The consultant and former Los Angeles sheriff’s detective claims that two times in recent months, robbers stole pricey hardware destined for AI data centers using a confrontational new tactic. It’s left the freight industry on edge.
The incidents involved two different shipments of high-value technology traveling from Silicon Valley to Southern California, according to Pachuca, who says he learned about the thefts from law enforcement authorities. Each truck was tailed by private security professionals driving unmarked escort vehicles, which were supposed to ensure the goods made it to their destinations safely. But hours into one journey, another driver rear-ended the escort in a hit-and-run, forcing it to stop. In the other case, the escort stopped after another car nudged it into a tailspin, a ploy commonly known as a PIT maneuver, and then fled.
Everyone familiar with the “accidents” believes the escorts were deliberately immobilized, according to Pachuca. Once the semitrucks lost their escorts, the drivers proceeded without halting—but not to their planned destinations. They were never heard from again, Pachua says, and millions of dollars in data center gear remains unaccounted for.
WIRED attempted to independently confirm Pachuca's accounts with five state and local law enforcement agencies, but could not because he shared limited information to avoid jeopardizing what he describes as ongoing investigations. But two other people in the cargo industry provided corroborating information.
J.J. Coughlin, chairman of the Southwest Transportation Security Council, a nonprofit intelligence-sharing group, says one of the affected escort companies notified him as soon as its vehicle was attacked while it was guarding “high-value technology.” Danny Ramon, director of intelligence and response at the freight-monitoring software developer Overhaul, says he learned about the rear-ending incident from law enforcement sources days after it happened. He describes the situation as a “coordinated assault” affecting a shipment of “AI hardware.”
Pachuca, Coughlin, and Ramon all say that no one was hurt in the attacks—they assume the truck drivers were in on the scheme, an increasingly common issue—and the perpetrators have yet to be caught. They are all concerned that the isolated cases could turn into an alarming trend—a violent spin on freight crime, now enabled by cyber-based scams and hacks, and targeting the very equipment powering the bleeding edge of the internet.
“It’s the worst I’ve seen,” Pachuca says of cargo theft nationwide. “The methods they are using, the value they are getting, the frequency these crimes are occurring.”
Escort companies are a final line of defense and are increasingly in demand. Michael Duffy, CEO of Solutions Group International, says his escort business used to be busy primarily ahead of the holiday shopping season, but it has now picked up year-round, with companies moving liquid cooling parts, servers, and computer chips emerging as his biggest clients. “Now that the values have shot through the roof, we’re getting called all the time,” Duffy says. He estimates his company has protected 13,000 shipments over the past four years, without a single loss.
High-value cargo and their escort vehicles have been targeted in Mexico and other countries for years. The suspected attacks in the US are now prompting escort operators to find ways to beef up their security, and some are encouraging personnel to call 911 at the first sign of suspicion. “We’ve been trying to come up with a game plan,” says Rachel Fruchtenicht of Shadow Freight Security.
AI Heists
Cargo theft has been on the rise since the start of the Covid pandemic, when more consumers turned to ecommerce and delivery for their daily needs. More recently, the booming AI data center industry has created a new target for would-be thieves: Total spending on their construction in just the first half of this year surpassed the total for all of 2025. While the overall number of thefts reported last quarter fell 26 percent year over year, the value of the goods taken more than doubled as criminals are increasingly targeting expensive cargo, according to new data released this month by Verisk CargoNet, an analytics and risk assessment firm.
Some of the most commonly stolen goods include metals—especially copper—and enterprise-grade computer and networking equipment, according to Verisk CargoNet. These shipments are typically transported according to standard procedures, creating “a significant mismatch between their financial value and their ordinary transportation and security profile,” Verisk CargoNet said in an announcement accompanying the new data.
In April, for example, thieves allegedly made off with 34,560 optical transceiver cables and 96 network switch modules—parts used in data centers—that were supposed to be traveling from Olive Branch, Mississippi, to Richardson, Texas, according to a notice issued by private investigators to freight industry partners seen by WIRED.
In some cases, law enforcement has succeeded in recovering the lost goods. In May, authorities in Southern California announced the seizure of $4 million worth of allegedly stolen cargo, including data center cooling equipment developed by the company Deepcool AI. One person was arrested in connection with the case. Deepcool AI did not respond to a request for comment.
In June, California Highway Patrol received a tip from a prospective buyer who believed a deal was “too good to be true,” sergeant Omar Morales tells WIRED. He said CHP went on to recover more than $2.2 million in merchandise allegedly stolen in three separate incidents, including eight pallets of “server switches” manufactured by Celestica for Meta valued at $550,000 in total. Meta declined to comment. Celestica did not respond to requests for comment. Morales says the investigation is ongoing.
The same day as the Meta recovery, authorities in the Chicago area discovered a reportedly stolen trailer filled with about $1 million in equipment bound for data centers.
Hacking, Now Ramming
For the most part, today’s cargo heists are relatively simple—they don’t involve snipping locks, breaking down truck doors, or PIT maneuvers. Instead, thieves take advantage of the fragmented and sometimes impersonal nature of the freight industry, in which hundreds of thousands of independent truck owner-operators can sign up to transport shipments posted online.
Criminals sometimes hack into a truck operator's email address using social engineering or phishing, allowing them to essentially take over their business and sign up to transport loads using its legitimate motor vehicle registrations. GPS trackers on stolen trucks can be spoofed or deactivated, leaving no trace.
In another version of the scam, freight industry experts say, legitimate business owners illegally sell off their motor carrier numbers—the unique identifiers assigned to trucking companies by federal regulators—allowing fraudsters to operate as a real business with a long-standing permit, phone number, and email address.
Both of the recent thefts that targeted escort vehicles involved recently sold motor carrier numbers, Pachuca says. Morales says the Meta data center switches seized in California were stolen using a similar technique. To acquire their loot, the thieves posed as a real trucking company, including falsifying the legitimate motor carrier’s documents.
“These are very sophisticated, very organized criminal organizations,” says Ben Wilkens, director of cybersecurity at the National Motor Freight Traffic Association, a trade organization.
A new federal system, called MOTUS, is designed to crack down on some of these impersonations and scams by making it easier for trucking companies to manage their federal registrations, and for customers

title: You’re Thinking About Online Trends All Wrong
summary: From pessimism around dating to AI reshaping culture, cyber-ethnographer Ruby J. Thelot tells WIRED why people are putting too much stock into things that go viral.
full_text:
For the last decade on social media, Ruby Thelot has asked himself the same questions when he encounters viral content online: Is this an ad? Is this account real? Is this an actual trend or just a fluke?
While trends like “6-7” and “looksmaxxing” have recently broken containment, not every new term or subcultural phenomenon has real mainstream staying power. Remember, in years past, when tech bros tried to make NFTs a thing? Or that period when audio chat apps like Clubhouse were pitched as the future of social media but quickly flamed out? (A prediction WIRED was not immune to.)
Thelot, a cyber-ethnographer and media theory researcher at NYU, says overestimating trends happens because the internet has become “balkanized,” with each of us on our own “digital island,” where most seemingly viral phenomena are really just the result of force-fed consumption. This is where virality primarily exists today: between provinces, not among the masses.
Thelot’s book In Defense of Being-On-Line comes out this fall. WIRED recently spoke with him about why virality can be an outdated metric for understanding trends, the myth of dating burnout, and what the popularity behind prediction markets actually signals.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
JASON PARHAM: When determining if a trend is real, is the problem now that we mistake short-term engagement for long-term adoption?
RUBY THELOT: The problem with our attempt to understand culture is that what was once a good proxy, namely virality, has become a target in and of its own. Goodhart’s law [coined by British economist Charles Goodhart] tells us that when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. So people are architecting content and media in order to simply get to the goal of having a lot of views without thinking about the actual inherent value of the thing. And that inherent value is what actually gives it cultural staying power. Because we are so far into Goodhart’s law in terms of culture, you can engineer virality without it ever trickling down to culture.
Dating burnout has gotten a lot of attention over the last few years, which has pushed dating apps to rebrand around AI. In May, Bumble announced that it was killing its swipe feature to lure users back. But you say the narrative around burnout is a mirage.
Heteropessimism has been reported since 2019, and is about the general malaise that straight women have when dating straight men. What was interesting to me about this is that, of course, there is an existing group of people who feel this way.
A friend recently wrote a New York Times essay, “There’s Nothing Wrong With Wanting Men,” which was more of a hetero-optimist piece, and she needed to do that because there was a feeling of malaise. We took a look at posts on social media. I looked at Instagram and TikTok, around 1,000 videos that had over 1 million views. We wanted to know: What is the percentage of things that are actually negative?
What did the data tell you?
It hovered around 25 percent. And I wanted to compare—is there one platform that is more negative than the other? I’m trying to identify the different digital islands and see if there is an area where this specific comment is getting sent where it’s specifically more negative, like X has a trickier algorithm where things are a bit more negative. So I do think heteropessimism is a little overblown by culture writers, and I say that as someone who writes for magazines.
One beloved industry right now is prediction markets. On Kalshi and Polymarket, droves of young people are betting on everything from Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl halftime performance to the wildfires in Oregon. What does its widespread adoption signal?
I spent some time studying groups of young men who were trading meme coins in 2020 to 2024. This was a similar kind of activity; it is mostly gambling. What I discovered was that oftentimes the activity of gambling was not an individual activity. It tended to be in these group chats, lovingly called “the trenches,” in which you and your boys exchanged information and traded together. And not only that, you lose together.
When I think about the male loneliness epidemic, this was a rather twisted but interesting novel form of male bonding. With prediction markets, I think about them not merely as financial instruments, but also as a tool for participation. Consumers no longer want to just purely consume, they want to participate in culture.
So they buy into culture as a way of participating?
But I don't even think that the financial award is what is driving people to gamble. If you're spending eight hours on the screen, the question is not “How do I make money with this?” It is “How do I get closer to it?” The bet, for the most part, does not matter. Because we live in a highly financialized world, what matters is the closeness to the media, and you get close through the act of wagering or betting.
AI is reshaping culture at light speed. Which prediction about it do you think people will laugh at in 10 years?
I don’t think AI is going to end the world. And the reason is that I don't think intelligence is that important.
In what sense?
Most of our issues in the world are not bottlenecked by intelligence, but by the promise of cooperation, coordination, and essentially alignment of large groups of people toward a common shared goal. That's the first part. The second thing is, when you start to quantify specific things, once again, the metric becomes the goal in and of itself.
The belief that intelligence is the most powerful thing comes from the assumption that there's a group of people on this planet who are the most intelligent. Sir Francis Galton, the father of eugenics, also believed this. With AI, they are just projecting what they value about themselves onto the superintelligence. It’s philosophically unsound and actually quite dangerous.
Why dangerous?
In that process, you're foreclosing a whole slew of untapped values—emotional intelligence, bodily intelligence, artistic intelligence. This is a concept the French philosopher Gilbert Simondon talks about. With each new advancement, certain things are left behind. And I think we might be leaving behind a whole set of highly human, alternative intelligences that are not measured or quantified by our current systems.

title: 8 Great Deals From Patagonia’s Past-Season Sale
summary: Summer’s not over yet; pick up some new gear for that last Labor Day trip. Save up to 40 percent on some of our favorite Patagonia items at the company’s past-season sale.
full_text:
Patagonia’s annual past-season sale is underway, with deals up to 40 percent off regular price.
Patagonia is a perennial favorite here at WIRED. Founded by dirtbag climber extraordinaire Yvon Chouinard, the company has been reliably churning out durable outdoor clothing and gear that's topped many of our outdoor guides for years.
Below, we’ve gathered all the best deals on our favorites. You’ll find everything from base layers to duffel bags. Some of the discounts vary based on size and color.
Be sure to check out our other outdoor and clothing guides, including the Best Merino Wool, Best Base Layers, and Best Backpacking Tents.
Deals on Rain Jackets, Fleece, and Base Layers
The Torrentshell is Patagonia's basic, no-nonsense, three-layer rain shell made from a recycled fabric with a PFC-free DWR finish. This jacket is 95 percent as good and less than half the price of the Arc'teryx Beta SL everyone seems to love. It's got a two-way adjustable hood, and cuffs have Velcro to give a nice, tight seal against the rain. The only catch here is that the sale colors and sizes are extremely limited.
This is a good deal on one of the most packable synthetic puffer jackets we've tested. If you're avoiding down but want a light puffer for three-season backpacking or just around-town wear, this is the jacket to get.
Patagonia's R1 Fleece jackets are among the most iconic pieces of hiking gear out there. I see at least two people in these every time I spend a day on the trail. The grid fleece means it breathes well, helping to keep you dry when you're active on cool days. It's one of the most versatile mid-layers you can own. I like this, the pullover version, because it saves on weight, but the full-zip jacket is also on sale.
Our favorite synthetic base layer, Patagonia's Capilene long underwear is super soft and stretchy. Capilene is spun from 100 percent recycled polyester (not the same as polypropylene, which is something totally different). These are smooth on the outside and have a subtly embossed diamond grid pattern on the inside, which Patagonia says creates little pockets that trap heat and help wick moisture.
The Houdini is an extremely useful jacket that I don't love but definitely use frequently. Its usefulness lies in the fact that it packs down to about the size of a tennis ball, it's light, and it'll stop the wind and shed a light rain, all of which have earned it a permanent spot in my day-hiking kit. What I don't like is that it rustles, it's not very breathable, and I feel like I'm wearing a plastic bag when I use it.
Regular readers will know I'm a fan of Fjällräven's wool Canada shirt; think of this as Patagonia's version of that. This is 100 percent cotton, not wool, which makes the outside softer (it's brushed flannel), with a recycled polyester insulation layer to up the warmth. The color and patterns are decidedly lumberjack, so be prepared to split some wood when you're wearing this one.
Deals on Patagonia Packs and Gear
This is one of our favorite options in our guide to the best duffel bags. It's made from 100 percent recycled polyester with a TPU film and laminate. Our testers have been using the 40-liter version for 15 years, and the laminate hasn't peeled. The gear-swallowing 100-liter model is also on sale for $157 ($68 off).
I'll confess I have only one real use for a minimalist fanny pack like this: I wear one when backpacking so I can get to frequently used items like snacks without taking off my pack. The Black Hole fanny pack is just big enough to hold everything and small enough not to get in the way of my pack's hip belt. It uses 100 percent recycled, ultralight ripstop nylon that's been treated with a durable water-repellent (DWR) finish, and it packs down into a small stash pocket when you don't need it.

title: A Candidate Named ‘Count Binface’ Is the Most Normal Part of This Pivotal UK Election
summary: Clacton's parliamentary race has it all: Nigel Farage, a man dressed as a trash can, a Union Jack bikini, white nationalist conspiracy theories, and 34 candidates on the ballot.
full_text:
A man wearing a trash can on his head dances on the beach, silver cape glinting in the sun as he spins beneath a wheel-topped pier, singing “England needs a new hope” from under an enormous helmet. The scene is Clacton-on-Sea, the centre of one of the east of England’s poorest constituencies and home to around 92,000 people and now the focus of international attention over what locals and observers have dubbed a political circus. The video is part of an extremely online campaign by Count Binface, who is running to represent the Essex town in Parliament. In an ignoble first in British electoral history, he is one of 34 candidates on the ballot.
One of Britain’s most high-profile and perennial candidates, Binface has stood in six previous elections across England over the past decade (UK politicians do not have to live in a constituency in order to represent it in parliament). This Thursday, he faces Clacton incumbent Nigel Farage—leader of the right-wing anti-immigration party Reform UK and a friend of Donald Trump—in a by-election triggered by the latter’s resignation amidst allegations that he and his party accepted and failed to declare financial support, including a £5 million gift from a Thailand-based cryptocurrency tycoon. Reform did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment.
Farage maintains he has done nothing wrong and wants to recontest his seat to let voters judge his actions. Major parties, including governing Labour and the opposition Conservatives, refused to field a candidate in the contest, branding it a “gimmick” and a “circus.” When then chancellor of the exchequer Rachel Reeves accepted Farage’s resignation, she said: “If he wants to spend the summer arguing with a bin, I won't stop him.”
In the vacuum, campaigners have rushed to use a high-profile vote to push their own issues, from psychosexual theory to Bible messaging to white-nationalist conspiracy theories. There are also a number of novelty candidates, three from satirical party Monster Raving Loony Party alone, Nick the Incredible Flying Brick, Baron Von Thunderclap, and Howling Laud Hope, who plans to shrink hospital waiting lists by reducing the font size.
The 34-candidate list is unprecedented; the 3-foot-long ballot papers are reportedly bigger than the tables used to count them on and have proved difficult for organizers to fit into envelopes for postal votes. The parties are fighting frenziedly for voters’ attention. Rosie Morrell of the Everyone Is God party–whose policies include creating a “stable world economy” and “to map and fully comprehend the complete spectrum of human psychology and sexuality”–offers to take off her Union Jack dress so I can snap a photo of her in her matching bikini. That’s what other press have been asking for as her partner contests the by-election, she says, pink feathers dangling from her ears.
In national coverage, Count Binface has broken through. A common figure in British politics, he most recently ran against Prime Minister Andy Burnham in June and has contested several other general and London mayoral elections before. Inside the trash can is comedian and writer Jon Harvey, who has worked on satirical television shows including Last Week Tonight With John Oliver, weekly British news quiz Have I Got News for You, and iconic BBC comedy The Thick of It. With Farage’s popularity collapsing across the country, Britons nationally want a victory for Binface–who pledges to nationalize singer Adele, cap ice cream prices, and hold a referendum on whether Pluto should regain its planet status.
“We did have a giggle, and get that it’s someone just trying to make light of it,” Jaywick resident Angelina Port, who is not a Reform voter, recalls about first reading about Binface in the national press. “But we do have issues that need to be resolved,” she says, standing on the front steps of her bungalow, which has been raised on bricks to avoid flooding. It’s a common feature in the neighborhood, which was built as a summer holiday resort but ended up permanently inhabited due to bomb damage and a housing shortage in London caused by the Second World War. Ten of her neighbors have signs saying “I’m voting Reform,” staked outside. The breakfast and burger van she runs with her partner is parked in her drive.
It’s the first Tuesday of August, 82 degrees Fahrenheit (28 Celsius) by midmorning and bin day in Clacton. Garbage trucks heave down quiet cul-de-sacs and flies are buzzing as canvassers armed with leaflets for the Rejoin EU Party’s John Stevens trudge sun-baked tarmac. They are targeting former Conservative voters in the affluent neighbourhood of Holland-on-Sea. Houses with glass fronts, large balconies, and gated, manicured front drives overlook the turquoise sea lapping a sandy beach–where last month a small boat of migrants landed after crossing the English channel from continental Europe.
Once a Conservative member for European Parliament, Stevens is positioning himself as a vote against Farage and his political baby, Brexit. In recent years, national attitudes toward EU membership have shifted, with Brexit being blamed for an annual multibillion-pound hit to the British economy as growth stagnates and living costs climb.
Stevens wants to see if local attitudes have changed, believing that if even those living in Brexit heartlands—around 70 percent of Clacton voted for Brexit in 2016—believe it was a bad idea, it will send a message to Westminster. “The one policy that Farage has been advocating all his political life is widely regarded as a disaster—and that’s how you attack him,” says Stevens, who quit the Conservative party over its increasing Euroscepticism. “You don’t attack him through his money or his morals, because those simply don’t hit.”
Some houses they skip: Those with signs reading “I’m voting Reform” and showing a pointing, smirking Farage staked in the ground. Stevens has learnt from knocking on 2,500 doors so far that staunch Farage fans aren’t concerned by the £5 million. “Everybody knows that Farage is going to win this, because he’s got the place nailed down,” Stevens says.
His view is affirmed when he stops local retiree and Reform voter Jeff Brown, on his sea-view walk. Farage needs the money for security, says Brown, and who wouldn’t accept a £5 million gift? “I don’t think he should have done what he did, resigning and standing again,” he adds, but nevertheless believes Farage has been a good MP in the past couple of years and has voted for him again. Having voted for Brexit, Brown started supporting Farage two years ago when he burst back onto the political scene on Clacton Pier, impressed by the politician’s charisma and speech. Brown already held anti-immigration feelings, saying he had been “pushed” out of London by an influx of immigrants.
It’s a feeling not just Farage is trying to take advantage of. Kai Stephens, 22, is standing for the far-right British Democrats, targeting ex-Londoners living in Jaywick to push his theory that white populations in Western countries are being replaced by nonwhite immigrants. Farage was once a personal hero for 12-year-old Stephens in the run-up to the Brexit referendum and Trump’s first presidency. But since Stephens fell in with Nazi sympathizers and fascist organizations through YouTube and X, he feels that Reform’s immigration policy is too weak. As well as activists from his party, Stephens says he is being assisted in his campaign by people from Restore Britain–which did not submit a candidate for this election and instead has been appealing to Reform to coalesce. Restore did not respond to requests for comment.
Though Farage is polling on top, Irene, 81, thinks he is “ridiculous,” hasn’t done anything in his two years as MP, and finds his closeness with US president Donald Trump “frightening.” “I feel that we've been neglected, really,” she says, frustrated by the focus on Farage. “Somebody's got to stand up against him.” Wheeling her emptied trash can back from th

title: FlightAware Withdraws Its Kalshi Suit a Day After Filing, Leaving the Data Question Unanswered
summary:
The flight tracker dismissed its case without prejudice on Tuesday, a day after demanding a restraining order, and Kalshi's cancellation markets no longer carry the FlightAware name.

The post FlightAware Withdraws Its Kalshi Suit a Day After Filing, Leaving the Data Question Unanswered appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
FlightAware filed a notice of voluntary dismissal on Tuesday in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, ending the case it had brought against Kalshi the previous day. The filing dismisses the action against all four defendants, Kalshi Inc., KalshiEX LLC, Kalshi Klear Inc. and Kalshi Klear LLC, and it is without prejudice under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i), which leaves the flight tracker free to refile.
The complaint it walked away from was not a modest one. FlightAware had demanded a jury, a temporary restraining order, and preliminary and permanent injunctions, and pleaded six counts including breach of contract and federal trademark infringement. It alleged Kalshi settled flight cancellation contracts on data pulled through a free Personal AeroAPI account opened on July 14, 2022, under terms barring use in furtherance of any business, and that on July 14, 2026 Kalshi self-certified the contracts with the CFTC while naming FlightAware the “Primary Source Agency.” FlightAware said it learned of the markets only when reporters called, cancelled the account the next day and sent a cease-and-desist letter.
This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.
Subscribe here to get these updates in your email for free
Kalshi has rewritten disputed statements on its website since FlightAware’s initial filing. Contracts that previously said outcomes were verified from FlightAware now reference the “Primary Source Agency,” with the trademark removed and a note that the markets have not been endorsed by that agency or its affiliates, though the link still points to FlightAware’s site.
Corporate lawyer Ariel Givner wrote on X that a plaintiff abandoning a case this quickly after demanding a restraining order usually signals a private arrangement.
The retreat leaves Kalshi’s harder problems intact. New York is seeking at least $36 billion over alleged unlicensed gambling, a suit that prompted the CFTC to invoke emergency powers on Tuesday and order the exchange to keep trading. Washington and Michigan courts have restricted its sports contracts, while a federal judge blocked Minnesota’s ban last month.

title: CFTC Invokes Emergency Powers to Keep Kalshi Trading Even if New York Wins a Restraining Order
summary:
The federal derivatives regulator told Kalshi to keep its exchange open regardless of what a New York court orders, escalating a jurisdictional fight over prediction markets.

The post CFTC Invokes Emergency Powers to Keep Kalshi Trading Even if New York Wins a Restraining Order appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered Kalshi on Tuesday to continue operating its exchange in line with its normal practices and the Commodity Exchange Act’s core principles, using the emergency authority in Section 8a(9) of the act. The order responds to a notice Kalshi filed on August 1 warning of “an imminent market emergency” if New York obtained a temporary restraining order against it.
Attorney General Letitia James filed New York’s complaint on July 31 in state court in Manhattan, and the case has since been removed to federal court. The state’s proposed order would stop Kalshi from offering contracts tied to sports, culture, elections and other events within or from New York, which the CFTC reads as a nationwide shutdown because Kalshi’s principal place of business sits there. New York is also seeking disgorgement plus a penalty of three times profits, and at least $36 billion in compensatory damages pending an accounting, against a company its own petition values at $22 billion. Kalshi has been a CFTC-designated contract market since November 3, 2020.
This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.
Subscribe here to get these updates in your email for free
The commission’s reasoning leans on price discovery. It argues that if a single state can dissolve a market, every event contract carries a legal risk premium, that traders would shift toward exchanges headquartered outside New York, and that a forced liquidation of open positions would ripple into other assets, citing contracts on Federal Reserve rate moves, bitcoin’s year-end price, drought conditions and shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
Selig said New York “has no business” regulating interstate financial markets and that Congress did not design derivatives regulation around state gaming laws. The agency has sued nine states, including Arizona, Illinois and New York, and filed amicus briefs in two federal appeals circuits and the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts. In July it ordered Kalshi to honor trades a Michigan court told it to cancel, and in May it sued Minnesota over an outright ban.

title: 祖克柏的 3 億美元豪華遊艇沒回應「海上求救無線電」，42 年老船繞過它救人
summary:
8 月 3 日晚上，阿拉斯加東南部一艘 21 英尺小艇燃料耗盡，船上有兩名女性、一個小孩和一隻狗。海岸防衛隊代 […]

〈祖克柏的 3 億美元豪華遊艇沒回應「海上求救無線電」，42 年老船繞過它救人〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
8 月 3 日晚上，阿拉斯加東南部一艘 21 英尺小艇燃料耗盡，船上有兩名女性、一個小孩和一隻狗。海岸防衛隊代發協助請求時，距離最近的是祖克柏那艘造價 3 億美元的超級遊艇 Launchpad，它沒有回應。最後開過去救援的是 1984 年完工的老船。
（前情提要：祖克柏萬字公開信〈未來屬於每一個人〉全文：不存在仁慈的 AGI）
（背景補充：我在貝佐斯私人派對上學到的富豪心態：「同理心是弱點、沒有失敗、都不重要」）
重點摘要
- 8 月 3 日晚 9 點 32 分小艇求助，25 分鐘後海岸防衛隊判定非遇險並代發協助廣播
- 船舶追蹤顯示 3 億美元的 Launchpad 距離較近卻未回應，1984 年完工的老船繞過它去拖人
- Launchpad 配置 49 名船員，發言人稱當時船員使用的是另一個無線電頻道
阿拉斯加時間 8 月 3 日晚上 9 點 32 分，彼得斯堡與朱諾之間的海面上，一艘 21 英尺長的 Hewescraft 小艇燒完了燃料油。船上有兩個女性、一個小孩，還有一隻狗。她們拿起無線電，用那個所有船隻都被要求監聽的緊急頻率，呼叫美國海岸防衛隊。
小艇失去動力，接下來漂去哪裡由海流決定。離她們最近的那艘船，是全世界最大的私人遊艇之一，祖克柏的船。
祖克柏的船「閃邊停」
海岸防衛隊接到呼叫後花了大約 25 分鐘評估狀況。晚上 9 點 56 分左右，它做出判定，小艇並不處於遇險狀態，於是代替她們發出一則海事協助請求廣播，呼叫附近船隻幫忙。
多家媒體調閱的船舶追蹤資料顯示，當時距離小艇最近的是 Launchpad，一艘 387 英尺、造價 3 億美元的 Feadship 超級遊艇，登記船主是 Meta 執行長祖克柏。
接下來發生的事被記錄在航跡圖上。Launchpad 在 Farragut Bay 灣口慢慢停了下來，然後就停在那裡。另一艘船從它旁邊繞過去，超過它，繼續往小艇的位置開。
那艘救援的船叫 Wilderness Legacy，192 英尺，1984 年完工，是一艘仿造二十世紀初沿岸蒸汽船的復刻船，UnCruise Adventures 的探險小郵輪，載客上限 90 人。跟祖克柏的船比起來只是一艘小船。
Wilderness Legacy 把小艇拖進 Farragut Bay 的遮蔽水域，替它加了油。隔天，船長收到消息，那三個人平安回到彼得斯堡。
船長廣播完，整艘船開始噓
如果不是船上有乘客把這件事貼到網路上，這會是一則沒人知道的新聞。
8 月 5 日，Wilderness Legacy 的乘客 Michael Love 在 Bluesky 上寫下他昨晚聽到的事。船長在全船廣播裡說明了救援經過，包括海岸防衛隊先呼叫了距離更近的祖克柏遊艇，而對方一直沒有回應。
我們的船昨晚救了一艘擱淺的船，顯然是在海岸防衛隊呼叫了祖克柏的遊艇之後，那艘船距離更近，而他們都沒有回應。
乘客還補充，船長宣布這件事的時候，全船「幾乎一致地發出噓聲」。他覺得這本來對祖克柏是個機會，替有需要的人做點有用的事，順便還能換到一些正面宣傳。
結果出手救援的船載的是一般旅客，他們原本是付錢來看鯨魚和冰川。
49 名船員沒有人監聽緊急頻道
祖克柏 Launchpad 不是一艘小船，它 118 公尺長，2024 年由荷蘭 Feadship 交付，馬紹爾群島籍，可載 26 名賓客，配置 49 名船員。這艘船原名 Feadship 1010，2022 年完工時因為原始買主的身分交不出去，兩年後才掛上新名字交到祖克柏手上。
它還有一艘支援船隻。2025 年 9 月，祖克柏買下 80 公尺長的支援船 Wingman，價格約 1 億美元，滿編再帶 40 名船員，船上有直升機坪、健身房、三溫暖，前甲板還有一座籃球場。
祖克柏的發言人 Brian Baker 向《Forbes》回應了這件事，說法有三點。
- 第一，事發時祖克柏和家人不在船上
- 第二，如同海岸防衛隊指出的，那艘船並沒有處於遇險狀態
- 第三，等船員查看到海岸防衛隊的聯絡時，救援行動已經在進行中，因為他們當時操作的是另一個無線電頻道
配置 49 名船員的船，那天晚上沒有一個人在聽所有船隻都被要求監聽的那個無線電頻率。
同天祖克柏發萬字信
這件事真正的反差不在海上發生的事，而是在時間軸上，8 月 10 日，祖克柏發表了一封萬字公開信，標題叫〈未來屬於每一個人〉。信裡寫著，未來的富足可以由每個人共享，把力量交到人們手中、讓他們追求自己的抱負，是人類取得最多進步的方式。
延伸閱讀：祖克柏萬字公開信〈未來屬於每一個人〉全文：不存在仁慈的 AGI
同天，他的遊艇因為沒有回應阿拉斯加海面上的求助訊號，登上全球新聞。
常見問題
祖克柏的遊艇沒有救人違法嗎？
沒有。美國法典第 46 編第 2304 條的救助義務只在有人「面臨喪生危險」時觸發，海岸防衛隊當晚判定小艇並未遇險，發出的是協助請求廣播而非遇險求救，法律義務因此沒有成立。
最後是誰救了那艘小艇？
UnCruise Adventures 旗下的探險小郵輪 Wilderness Legacy，1984 年完工、192 英尺長。它繞過停在灣口的 Launchpad，把小艇拖進 Farragut Bay 並協助加油，三人隔天平安返回彼得斯堡。

title: 打電動也能進塔台！美國航空總署招募玩家當空管員，2,000 人已入職
summary:
美國聯邦航空總署鎖定電玩玩家招募航空管制員，已聘用超過 2,000 人、達成 94% 年度目標，另有 2,00 […]

〈打電動也能進塔台！美國航空總署招募玩家當空管員，2,000 人已入職〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國聯邦航空總署鎖定電玩玩家招募航空管制員，已聘用超過 2,000 人、達成 94% 年度目標，另有 2,000 多人正在候補。
（前情提要：AI 裁員潮成社會火藥桶！矽谷獲利創新高卻裁近 15 萬人，貧富差距直逼佔領華爾街）
（背景補充：黃仁勳：AI 時代讀什麼科系不重要，說故事、創造力、判斷力才是真正護城河）
聯邦政府把「打電動」寫進了國安等級職缺的招募條件，而且真的招到人了？美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）近日證實，透過鎖定電玩玩家的招募計畫，已聘用超過 2,000 人接受航空管制員訓練，達成 2026 年度招募目標的 94%。
交通部長 Sean Duffy 在 X 貼文中形容這項計畫是「game changer」。對一個長年被列為缺工重災區的職業來說，這是少見會被官員拿出來炫耀的數字。
🚨 GAME CHANGER
In April, we launched a NEW CAMPAIGN to recruit video gamers as air traffic controllers — and supercharged the entire hiring process to get the BEST & BRIGHTEST in faster. The results are HISTORIC ✈️
✅ 94% of hiring goal met — fastest time ever to reach target… pic.twitter.com/gN3OGmEIBB
— Secretary Sean Duffy (@SecDuffy) August 9, 2026
打電動的技能，恰好是塔臺要的技能
Duffy 今年 4 月啟動這項計畫時就承認，交通部得把招募觸角伸到傳統管道以外。
他在本週於紐澤西紐華克自由國際機場接受 CBS News 資深交通線記者 Kris Van Cleave 專訪時表示，玩家在遊戲裡做的事，某種程度上就是塔臺在做的事，快速判斷、保持專注、同時處理多條資訊流。
目前僅約 25% 的管制員持有傳統大學學歷，前管制員也指出，電玩需要的技能組合與管制員每天引導超過 8 萬架次航班的實際工作高度重疊。
數字攤開看
美國交通部數據顯示，這項招募活動於 2026 年 4 月上線後，FAA 在年度招募視窗開啟的 24 小時內就收到超過 12,000 份申請，創下紀錄。
除了已入職的 2,000 多人，Duffy 補充，另有超過 2,000 名候選人正在招募流程中排隊等待。
FAA 官方招募頁面列出的門檻並不寬鬆：須具備美國公民身分、年齡須低於 31 歲，並透過 FAA 的職前測驗；測驗成績會在一週內通知考生（學院階段的淘汰率業界估算在 2 至 3 成之間，通過後還要在派駐機場完成認證，全程約 2 到 3 年）。
薪水多少
美國勞工統計局（BLS）2024 年度數據顯示，航空管制員的年薪中位數為 144,580 美元，是目前可取得的最新官方數字。
但實際薪資落差極大：據業界人士估算，資歷較淺、任職於小型機場的管制員平均年薪僅約 6 萬美元，離中位數有兩倍以上差距。
缺工程度的溫度計
美國政府問責署（GAO）去年 12 月發布的報告已警告，管制員人力短缺可能導致航班延誤或取消頻率上升。去年底的政府關門風波，更讓部分現職管制員直接被嚇跑，依法被列為「必要人員」的他們，當時被迫在無薪狀態下持續值勤。
14.4 萬美元的年薪中位數，某種程度上是「人類還贏 AI 一截」的定價。但這波招募能不能真正補上缺口，還得看兩年後訓練學院的畢業率，而不是看申請表上填了幾份。

full_text:
Bitget Wallet 啟動全球推廣大使計畫，無申請門檻，提供交易與支付雙軌返佣，最高達 60%。平台數據顯示支付規模首度超越交易，累計穩定幣交易額突破 1,770 億美元。該計畫旨在將創作者納入 Everyday Finance 分發網絡，加速鏈上支付普及。

（背景補充：Bitget Wallet 研究》過去 10 年，你為何沒變成有錢人？）
（本文為廣編稿，由 Bitget Wallet 撰文、提供，不代表動區立場，亦非投資建議、購買或出售建議。詳見文末責任警示。）
Bitget Wallet 宣布正式啟動全球推廣大使計畫（Global Affiliate Program），即日起開放報名。凡已完成 Bitget Wallet 帳戶註冊、擁有活躍社群帳號或具備社群影響力的用戶均可申請，無申請門檻。
雙軌獎勵機制
此次計畫設有交易與支付兩條獨立獎勵軌道，兩者可同步疊加累積：
- 交易返佣：涵蓋代幣 Swap 及永續合約交易，推薦用戶每完成一筆交易，推廣者即按該交易幣種獲得對應比例的分成，返佣比例最高可達 60%，且無最低交易量門檻，適合受眾以加密新手為主的內容創作者。
- 支付返佣：覆蓋加密卡消費與掃碼支付兩大場景。推薦新用戶成功開卡並完成首刷，即可獲得一次性固定獎勵；此後該用戶每一筆消費均計入持續分成，無上限累積。
兩套獎勵機制可同步運行，創作者與社群運營者可同時從交易與消費兩個維度獲取收益。
支付規模首次超越交易，規模背書分佣邏輯
Bitget Wallet 數據顯示，2026 年上半年平台加密卡消費規模三倍成長，支付規模史上首次超越交易規模，累計穩定幣交易總額突破 1,770 億美元。當鏈上支付逐漸成為日常使用場景，推廣者的長期分成潛力也隨鏈上消費規模同步提升。
此次計畫將創作者與社群運營者正式納入 Everyday Finance 分發網路，加速鏈上支付在日常消費場景的普及。
如何參與
已完成 Bitget Wallet 帳戶註冊的用戶，可造訪官網或透過應用程式內的推廣中心提交申請，獲核准後即可取得專屬推廣連結，開始追蹤推薦轉換。
常見問題
沒有很多粉絲可以申請嗎？
可以。只要你有自己的社交媒體帳號或社群，並且願意分享 Bitget Wallet，皆可申請。
交易返佣需要完成任務嗎？
活動期間沒有交易量考核，符合活動規則即可享受對應返佣比例。
Card 獎勵可以提現嗎？
獎勵發放方式和具體規則以官方活動頁面及 App 公告為準。
活動說明

title: 知名交易員 Doctor Profit：比特幣 60 天只漲 0.18%，築底訊號第四次出現
summary:
比特幣 8 月 12 日報 63,890 美元，24 小時下跌 0.39%，過去 60 天累計漲幅只有 0.1 […]

〈知名交易員 Doctor Profit：比特幣 60 天只漲 0.18%，築底訊號第四次出現〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣 8 月 12 日報 63,890 美元，24 小時下跌 0.39%，過去 60 天累計漲幅只有 0.18%。瑞士交易員 Doctor Profit 指出，Glassnode 已實現價格分齡圖出現 2015 年以來第四次交叉，持有 3 到 6 個月的籌碼成本跌破持有 1 到 2 年的成本，歷史上這個位置對應的是熊市築底期的起點，不是反轉當天。
（前情提要：交易員 Doctor Profit 平掉比特幣空單改買現貨，最賺的是跌 64.8% 的 MSTR 空單）
（背景補充：貝格先生分析》BTC 長期、短期持有者成本逆轉訊號，數據上怎麼推算）
重點摘要
- 比特幣 8 月 12 日報 63,890 美元，過去 7 天跌 0.26%、30 天漲 1.16%、60 天漲 0.18%，兩個月幾乎零波動。
- Doctor Profit 指 Glassnode 已實現價格分齡圖出現 2015 年以來第四次交叉，3 到 6 個月籌碼成本跌破 1 到 2 年籌碼成本，且現價低於兩者。
- 下方結構性支撐在 200 週均線約 61,000 美元與全市場已實現價格 53,300 美元；同期 30 年期美債殖利率 5.25%，聯準會 7 月會議三張反對票主張的方向是升息。
比特幣在台北時間 8 月 12 日下午報 63,890 美元，24 小時區間落在 63,200 至 64,414 美元，跌幅 0.39%。真正該看的不是這根日線。過去 7 天跌 0.26%，30 天漲 1.16%，60 天漲 0.18%。兩個月下來，這個市場等於沒動。
$BTC: Historic Indicator flashing bottom was in or is very close
Realized Price by Age shows the average price at which different groups of Bitcoin last moved on-chain, giving us an estimate of their cost basis. The pink line represents Bitcoin held for 3–6 months, while the… pic.twitter.com/o8vR1X2hgO
— Doctor Profit 🇨🇭 (@DrProfitCrypto) August 11, 2026
粉線下穿藍線，11 年來第四次
瑞士交易員 Doctor Profit 近日把焦點放在 Glassnode 的「已實現價格分齡」圖表上。這張圖依照每一枚比特幣最後一次在鏈上移動的時間分組，算出各組的平均取得成本。粉紅線代表持有 3 到 6 個月的籌碼，藍線代表持有 1 到 2 年的籌碼。
他的觀察是，2015 年、2019 年、2022 年這三次熊市，底部形成階段的起點都是同一個動作，粉線下穿藍線。這代表較新的買家在虧損中投降賣出，籌碼從短線手上轉移到更長期的持有者手中。這個交叉正在第四次出現，而且比特幣現在的價格低於這兩組人的平均成本。
他自己也承認，這個訊號從來沒有帶來立即反轉。
歷史上這並沒有產生立即的反轉，比特幣在市場築底的過程中繼續橫盤了好幾個月，這段時間可以理解為積累區間。
他定義的是一個區間的開始，不是一根 K 棒的轉折。對照三次前例，2015 年 1 月的週期低點在 152 美元附近，2018 年 12 月是 3,122 美元，2022 年 11 月是 15,476 美元，而底部之後的積累期，2018 年那次拖了大約 14 個月，2022 年那次也走了 10 個月才真正轉向。
另一條成本線還沒交叉
這裡有個容易混淆的地方。市場上更常被引用的是短期與長期持有者已實現價格的交叉，那組指標用 155 天當分界，跟 Doctor Profit 引用的分齡區間不是同一條線。
以 8 月 10 日的數據，短期持有者已實現價格在 67,111.32 美元，長期持有者在 49,697.19 美元，兩者相差 17,414 美元，還沒有碰在一起。動區 7 月 15 日引述的推算，當時差距是 21,063 美元。26 天縮掉 3,649 美元，日均收斂約 140 美元，照這個速度還要 4 個月左右才會交叉。
同一個市場，兩條成本線給出兩份時間表。細分齡的那條已經翻過去，粗分的那條還在路上。這也解釋了為什麼「底部到了」跟「底部還沒到」可以同時成立，差別只在用哪組籌碼定義「新入場的人」。
宏觀那邊還沒鬆手
鏈上籌碼在換手，資金成本卻沒有配合。8 月 10 日 30 年期美債殖利率報 5.25%，比動區 7 月 30 日記錄的 5.201% 又往上推了一階，續處 2007 年以來的高檔區。10 年期在 4.72%，2 年期 4.25%。聯邦資金有效利率 3.63%，對應目標區間 3.50% 至 3.75%。
更關鍵的是 7 月的聯準會會議。決議以 9 比 3 維持利率不變，而三張反對票主張的方向是立即升息，不是降息。期貨市場對 9 月 16 日會議的升息押注一度升到六到七成。這是風險資產最不想看到的組合，長天期殖利率創高、政策路徑偏鷹、無風險收益率還壓在 4% 以上。
Doctor Profit 的多頭理由不在宏觀，在事件。他點名 10 月貝萊德代幣化平台上線與監管法案可能過關，認為那才是資金重新進場的催化劑，並判斷比特幣跌破 50,000 美元的機率低。
常見問題
已實現價格分齡交叉代表什麼？
它比較的是不同持有期間籌碼的平均取得成本。當持有 3 到 6 個月的成本跌破持有 1 到 2 年的成本，代表新進買家認賠出場、籌碼流向長期持有者。2015、2019、2022 三次熊市的築底期都由這個動作揭開序幕。
Doctor Profit 目前買在什麼價位？
他 7 月 18 日平掉建於 12 萬美元附近的空單，改在 64,000 美元附近建立現貨部位，並在 54,000 至 64,000 美元區間以每次 5% 的倉位分批進場，BTC 與 ETH 配置比例為四比一。實際上比特幣 8 月未跌破 62,800 美元，成交多落在區間上緣。

title: 熊本再震規模 4.9！台積電日本廠沒停機：廠區只測到震度 3
summary:
日本熊本縣今日（8/12）下午 1 點 05 分再傳規模 4.9 地震，最大震度 4，據 ウェザーニュース 與 […]

〈熊本再震規模 4.9！台積電日本廠沒停機：廠區只測到震度 3〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
日本熊本縣今日（8/12）下午 1 點 05 分再傳規模 4.9 地震，最大震度 4，據 ウェザーニュース 與 日本氣象廳 資料，台積電子公司 JASM 所在的菊陽町這次只測到震度 3，廠區未傳出停機。熊本一廠在 7 月 28 日規模 7.1 主震後曾停機校正設備，台積電已於 8 月 3 日宣布生產回到震前水準，前後約 6 天。
（前情提要：日本熊本規模 7.1 強震，台積電正在確認熊本廠災情狀況）
（背景補充：熊本處高風險地震帶，台積電為何要選擇落腳此處？）
重點摘要
- 熊本 8 月 12 日下午 1 點 05 分再震規模 4.9，最大震度 4，無海嘯風險
- JASM 所在菊陽町僅測得震度 3，未達 7 月 28 日主震當天的震度 5
- 台積電熊本一廠 8 月 3 日宣布生產回到震前水準，實際停機約 6 天
日本熊本縣今日（8/12）下午 1 點 05 分再度發生地震，震央位於熊本縣天草・蘆北地方，規模 4.9、深度約 10 公里。八代市、宇城市、上天草市、天草市、蘆北町，以及長崎縣諫早市、雲仙市測得最大震度 4，氣象廳確認沒有海嘯風險。台積電子公司 JASM（日本先進半導體製造）所在的菊陽町，這次只測到震度 3。
一廠 8 月 3 日恢復
台積電日本法人 8 月 3 日透過官方 X 帳號宣布，熊本廠已恢復正常生產體制，「生產已回復至地震發生前水準」。從 7 月 28 日停機算起，實際只停了約 6 天，比市場原估的兩週快上不少。台積電同時捐出 2.5 億日圓賑災，並在內部啟動員工募款；仍在興建的二廠受影響更小，工地 7 月 29 日就恢復施工。
生產設備校正花了很多時間，半導體機台對振動極度敏感，建築本體沒事不代表能開機，製程參數得重新確認過一輪，產線才敢投料。
餘震還沒停
熊本的地震活動並沒有結束。氣象廳 8 月 12 日更新指出，地震發生數雖然反覆增減、大方向上緩慢下降，活動仍處於活躍狀態。主震後最大的一次餘震落在 8 月 1 日晚間 9 點 47 分，規模 4.7、最大震度 5 弱，8 月 9 日、8 月 11 日到今天，熊本一帶都還記錄到有感地震。
JASM 一廠 2024 年 12 月投產，生產 28/22 奈米與 16/12 奈米成熟製程，規劃月產能 5.5 萬片 12 吋晶圓。設備校正再遇地震就得從頭再來，這是這座廠接下來得持續面臨的變數。
常見問題
熊本地震對台積電 JASM 熊本廠有什麼影響？
7 月 28 日規模 7.1 主震時 JASM 廠區測得震度 5，一廠停機校正設備約 6 天，台積電 8 月 3 日宣布生產已回到震前水準。8 月 12 日這場規模 4.9 地震，廠區僅測得震度 3，未傳出停機。
台積電熊本一廠生產哪些製程？
JASM 一廠 2024 年 12 月投產，生產 28/22 奈米與 16/12 奈米成熟製程，規劃月產能 5.5 萬片 12 吋晶圓，目前仍在產能爬坡階段，尚未達到規劃上限。二廠則還在興建中。

title: Manus 2.0 已開發完成，等待完全脫離 Meta 即發佈
summary:
《晚點 LatePost》報導，Manus 2.0 已經開發完成，但團隊按住沒有發布，要等與 Meta 的收購 […]

〈Manus 2.0 已開發完成，等待完全脫離 Meta 即發佈〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
《晚點 LatePost》報導，Manus 2.0 已經開發完成，但團隊按住沒有發布，要等與 Meta 的收購交易徹底結束後才上線，產品目前仍停在 1.6 版。1.6 是 2025 年 12 月 15 日發的，兩週後 Meta 就宣布收購，大版本因此凍了將近八個月。幾個月的交易風波沒有拆散團隊，Manus 現在有 150 多人，期間沒有一個人離職，創辦人肖弘給團隊和投資人寫信說「This is my third trip」。據 《晚點 LatePost》 報導，由動區動趨整理報導。
（前情提要：Manus 脫離 Meta 恢復獨立營運，誰贏了，誰輸了？）
（背景補充：Manus 告別 Meta 重獲自由！宣布恢復獨立營運，急籲用戶完成資料備份）
重點摘要
- Manus 2.0 已開發完成但未發布，要等 Meta 收購案徹底解除後才上線
- 產品停在 2025 年 12 月 15 日發布的 1.6 版，大版本凍結將近八個月
- 團隊 150 多人期間零離職，肖弘信中稱新 Manus 的起點是 ARR 超過 3 億美元的產品
做完的東西鎖著不釋出，這是 Manus 這幾個月的日常。官網上的版本號至今掛在 1.6，但據《晚點 LatePost》，代號 2.0 的下一個大版本其實早就完工。遲遲不上線的理由跟技術無關，團隊在等與 Meta 收購案的脫籍手續全部結束。
1.6 版是 2025 年 12 月 15 日推出的，帶來旗艦級的 Manus 1.6 Max、首次支援行動應用開發，以及互動式圖像創作介面 Design View。兩週後的 12 月 29 日，Meta 宣布以超過 20 億美元收購 Manus，肖弘出任 Meta 副總裁。從那天算到現在，Manus 的大版本原地不動將近八個月。
做完的版本卡在法律程序上
時間線倒回今年 4 月 27 日，中國國家發展和改革委員會的外資安全審查機制辦公室認定這筆交易帶有無法透過附加條件消除的國安風險，直接禁止投資，要求雙方終止收購安排、恢復交易前狀態。這是中國《外商投資安全審查辦法》實施以來，第一起被公開喊停的 AI 領域外資併購案。
一路走到 8 月 11 日，Manus 官網把「Manus is now part of Meta」換成即將恢復獨立營運的公告，用戶資料則預定在 8 月 23 到 24 日從 Meta 系統刪除。2.0 之所以按住不發，等的就是這幾道手續辦完。
大版本鎖住的時候，團隊把力氣花在小版本上。這段期間 Manus 推出桌面應用，也上線了先規劃再執行的 Plan Mode，兩者都是在追趕 Claude 和 Codex，並且維持每週 1 到 2 個功能更新的節奏。團隊早期就自建 Evaluation 評測團隊，把開發做成閉環迴圈，這也是它能在沒有自家模型的情況下把 agent 產品做起來的底子。
150 多名員工無人離職
被收購方在交易破局後被同業掃樓挖角，是這幾年 AI 圈的常態。Manus 的情況剛好相反，幾個月的風波下來，團隊維持 150 多人，期間無人離職。
重新獨立的消息公布那晚，肖弘寫了封信給團隊和投資人，用一句話替這家公司定調，「This is my third trip」。在他們自己的敘事裡，這不是一間被退貨的公司，而是一間帶著 150 人、一整組沒散掉的合夥人，以及一個年化營收 3 億美元的產品重新開張的新創。
常見問題
Manus 2.0 為什麼開發完成卻不發布？
團隊要等與 Meta 的收購交易徹底解除後再上線。中國發改委 4 月 27 日禁止該筆交易，拆解程序延續到 8 月，用戶資料預定 8 月 23 到 24 日從 Meta 系統刪除。
Manus 目前是什麼版本？
仍停留在 2025 年 12 月 15 日發布的 1.6 版，主要功能包括 Manus 1.6 Max、行動應用開發與 Design View。期間只有桌面應用、Plan Mode 這類小版本更新。

title: 韓國散戶新規定：買槓桿 ETF 須先完成 5 天共 5 小時模擬交易
summary:
韓國金融委員會 8 月 12 日通過韓國交易所業務規定修訂案，8 月 19 日起 ETF、ETN 的證券商偏離 […]

〈韓國散戶新規定：買槓桿 ETF 須先完成 5 天共 5 小時模擬交易〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
韓國金融委員會 8 月 12 日通過韓國交易所業務規定修訂案，8 月 19 日起 ETF、ETN 的證券商偏離率管理義務，由國內 3%、海外 6% 收緊到 2% 與 5%。首次買進單一股票槓桿與反向產品的散戶，還得先完成 5 個交易日、合計 5 小時以上的模擬交易。這類產品的單日成交額，已經從 7 月 30 日的 12 兆 4,000 億韓元掉到 8 月 11 日的 7,000 億。據 이투데이 與韓聯社報導，由動區動趨整理報導。
（前情提要：韓國「單一標的槓桿 ETF」遭重拳監管，三星、SK 海力士交易量雪崩 90%）
（背景補充：韓國財政部緊急出手「嚴管單股槓桿 ETF」！散戶保證金門檻暴增至 3 千萬）
重點摘要
- 韓國 8 月 19 日起收緊 ETF、ETN 偏離率管理標準，國內由 3% 降到 2%、海外由 6% 降到 5%
- 首投單一股票槓桿產品的散戶須完成 5 個交易日、合計 5 小時模擬交易，認證 8 月 24 日才發得出來
- 這類產品成交額從 7 月 30 日的 12 兆 4,000 億韓元萎縮到 8 月 11 日的 7,000 億，只剩 5.6%
韓國金融委員會（FSC）8 月 12 日召開第 1 次臨時例會，通過韓國交易所（KRX）有價證券市場業務規定修訂案。這次一口氣動兩件事，一是把所有 ETF、ETN 的證券商偏離率管理義務往下壓，二是把模擬交易義務擴大到韓國與海外上市的單一股票槓桿、反向產品，兩項都從 8 月 19 日生效。
新規還沒上路，市場自己先冷掉了。單一股票槓桿與反向產品的成交額在 7 月 30 日還有 12 兆 4,000 億韓元（約 87.6 億美元），到 8 月 11 日只剩 7,000 億韓元（約 4.9 億美元），是 7 月底的 5.6% 水準。8 月 4 日到 10 日之間還出現 1 兆 4,000 億韓元規模的輪動賣出。
轉折點是 7 月 31 日，基本保證金從 1,000 萬韓元跳到 3,000 萬韓元現金（約 2.1 萬美元），而且股票、債券這類代用證券一律不算數。當天 16 檔單一股票槓桿與反向 ETF 成交 3 兆 543 億韓元，比前一日少了 75.5%。真正把量打到剩十幾分之一的，不是掛牌當天那一刀，是後面兩週投資人一路撤出的累積結果。
偏離率兩道門檻下調
偏離率講的是 ETF、ETN 的市價跟淨值（NAV）之間的落差，數字愈大，代表投資人買到的價格離資產真實價值愈遠。修訂後，以收盤價計算的證券商管理義務範圍，從國內產品 3%、海外產品 6%，分別收緊到 2% 和 5%，偏離率是負數時直接取絕對值計算。
負責把價格拉回淨值附近的是流動性供給者（LP），也就是證券商。KRX 接下來要修施行細則，對故意、重大過失或反覆違反管理義務的證券商，限制它承接新標的的流動性供給業務。另外，偏離率反覆超過管理義務兩倍的 ETF，指定為投資注意標的的流程也從三階段縮短到兩階段。罰則從開罰單改成斷生意，對證券商來說是完全不同量級的壓力。
8 月 19 日不是可以買的日子
8 月 19 日起，首次投資國內外單一股票槓桿與反向 ETF、ETN 的個人一般投資人，除了 3,000 萬韓元現金基本保證金和 3 小時事前教育，還得在 KRX 的模擬交易系統把課修完，條件有三項。
- 總共至少 5 個交易日
- 每個交易日連線交易 1 小時以上
- 合計不少於 5 小時
不過真正卡住買盤的不是這 5 小時。模擬交易服務 8 月 19 日才開放，修完的認證要到 8 月 24 日才發得出來，證券商端登錄再抓 1 到 2 個營業日。也就是說，8 月 19 日才想進場的新投資人，最快也得等到 8 月底才按得下買進鍵。這道門檻擋掉的與其說是無知，不如說是衝動。
FSC 要投資人親自體驗的是「負複利效應」，白話講就是槓桿產品的淨值會被來回震盪磨掉，標的原地盤整、投資人照樣虧錢。FSC 的說法是，要讓投資人先摸過這個結構與風險，再自己判斷要不要投。
擋不住 4 成交易量的外資
5 月 27 日到 7 月 28 日，16 檔單一股票槓桿 ETF 累計成交 497.9 兆韓元（約 3,518 億美元），其中外國投資人吃下 202.4 兆韓元，佔 40.6%。而這次模擬交易義務的對象只有個人一般投資人，專業投資人、法人與外國人全部排除在外，5 月 27 日到 8 月 17 日之間有交易紀錄的人也直接豁免。
換句話說，靠高頻與演算法反覆做超短線的那 4 成交易量，連門檻都沒碰到。韓國金融監督院（FSS）也承認初期保護措施只針對個人投資人，正在研究參考衍生品市場既有制度、用交易成本來壓抑過度下單。
常見問題
什麼是 ETF 偏離率？
偏離率是 ETF 或 ETN 的市價與淨值（NAV）之間的落差比率，落差愈大代表買到的價格離資產真實價值愈遠。韓國 8 月 19 日起把證券商管理義務由國內 3%、海外 6% 收緊到 2% 與 5%。
韓國單一股票槓桿 ETF 的模擬交易要做多久？
至少 5 個交易日，每個交易日連線交易 1 小時以上，合計不少於 5 小時。服務 8 月 19 日開放，修完的認證 8 月 24 日起才發放，證券商端登錄還要 1 到 2 個營業日。

title: 富達以太幣 ETF 擬引入「質押」功能，加碼祭出每季配息
summary:
看準投資人對穩定收益的需求，美國資產管理巨擘富達（Fidelity）正準備為旗下規模近 9 億美元的以太幣現貨 ETF 導入「質押」機制，並加碼推出每季現金配息，勢必將掀起一波搶客大戰。

〈富達以太幣 ETF 擬引入「質押」功能，加碼祭出每季配息〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
看準投資人對穩定收益的需求，美國資產管理巨擘富達（Fidelity）正準備為旗下規模近 9 億美元的以太幣現貨 ETF 導入「質押」機制，並加碼推出每季現金配息，勢必將掀起一波搶客大戰。
根據最新提交的註冊聲明修正案，目前資產淨值達 8.98 億美元的「富達以太幣基金（代號：FETH）」，未來在正常市場情況下，最高可將 100% 的以太幣全數投入質押。
不過，富達並未設定最低質押比例，為了因應投資人贖回、支應基金開銷及維持必要的流動性，富達仍會保留一定比例的未質押以太幣在手。
促成華爾街巨頭大動作轉向的東風，來自美國國稅局（IRS）於 2025 年 11 月發布的「避風港（Safe Harbor）」稅務指引。該新規允許符合條件的加密貨幣信託進行資產質押，且不會因此喪失「授予人信託（Grantor-Trust，一種可避免雙重課稅的信託結構）」的稅務待遇。
如今，富達將跟進灰度（Grayscale）與 21Shares 的腳步，直接為旗下以太幣 ETF 添加質押功能；而同業勁敵貝萊德（BlackRock）則是採取不同策略，選擇另行推出另一檔以太幣質押 ETF 。
投資人最關心的收益分配方面，富達規劃將 85% 的質押獎勵保留給基金，剩餘的 15% 則用於支付給基金發行人、託管機構，以及節點營運商。目前名列這檔基金合作夥伴的節點營運商，包含了 Blockdaemon 、 Figment 與 Galaxy 等業內知名機構。
至於質押帶來的淨收益將如何處置？富達指出，這些收益將優先用於支應基金日常營運開銷，結餘部分才會轉換為每季發放的現金紅利。
依據國稅局相關法規，這類基金每季至少必須進行一次質押收益分配。此外，富達也在文件中補充說明，為了籌措配息所需的現金，基金在必要時會選擇出售部分持有的以太幣。

title: 比特幣 BIP-110 分叉失敗收場！推手 Luke Dashjr 遭拔除 BIP 編輯職務
summary:
由資深比特幣開發者  Luke Dashjr  主導推動的 BIP-110 軟分叉提案，在礦工支持度僅約 2.6%、遠低於 55% 門檻下迅速失敗，分叉鏈甚至只挖出 2 個區塊就陷入停擺。如今提案失敗後，Luke Dashjr 更遭免除「比特幣改進提案（BIP）」編輯職務，讓這場圍繞比特幣治理與區塊空間用途的爭議進一步升級。

〈比特幣 BIP-110 分叉失敗收場！推手 Luke Dashjr 遭拔除 BIP 編輯職務〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
由資深比特幣開發者 Luke Dashjr 主導推動的 BIP-110 軟分叉提案，在礦工支持度僅約 2.6% 、遠低於 55% 門檻下迅速失敗，分叉鏈甚至只挖出 2 個區塊就陷入停擺。如今提案失敗後，Luke Dashjr 更遭免除「比特幣改進提案（BIP）」編輯職務，讓這場圍繞比特幣治理與區塊空間用途的爭議進一步升級。
BIP-110 的核心訴求是建立一條新的分叉鏈，旨在限制比特幣網路被用於儲存圖片、文字等「非金融資料」，主要針對 Ordinals 協議興起後大量出現的銘文（Inscriptions）交易。
然而，提案在進入由礦工與節點營運商表態支持的「訊號傳遞期（Signaling Period）」後，幾乎乎立即失去動能。支持礦工僅約占 2.6%，遠低於方案設定的 55% 門檻，最終分叉鏈僅挖出 2 個區塊就停止運行，比特幣主鏈則維持正常運行。
就在 BIP-110 宣告失敗後，Luke Dashjr 的 BIP 編輯職務也遭到撤除。他被指控在推動 BIP-110 期間曾濫用編輯權力，包括在提案尚未被充分討論前，就擅自為提案指定 BIP 編號，且未遵循正規程序就將更新內容合併至程式碼庫。
比特幣開發者 Mark Erhardt 在提出撤職動議時指出：「自從 2024 年 4 月加入編輯團隊以來，Luke Dashjr 幾乎沒有參與過 BIP 編輯的日常維護工作：這段期間，他留下的編輯評論占比甚至不到總數的 1%，而這次的提案合併，竟是他自 2024 年 5 月以來的首次合併操作。」
面對排山倒海的抨擊，Luke Dashjr 在社群平台 X 上痛批，剝奪他的編輯職務是「濫權」。早在撤職動議剛提出之際，他就曾嚴正駁斥，強調這些指控全數是子虛烏有。
Luke Dashjr 還宣布，他將暫時卸下特幣挖礦池 Ocean 的董事長兼技術長職務，並將重心轉向比特幣及開源專案。
BIP-110 的爭議，源自該如何使用比特幣區塊空間的長期路線之爭。自 2023 年 Ordinals 協議上線以來，圖片、文字及其他資料開始大量寫入比特幣區塊，衍生出銘文、 BRC-20 等應用。
支持 BIP-110 的一方認為，這些非金融資料占用有限的區塊空間，推高交易成本，也讓比特幣偏離點對點電子現金及價值儲存等核心用途；反對者則主張，只要交易符合共識規則並支付手續費，節點與礦工就不應依照交易內容是否「有用」來進行審查。
BIP-110 試圖透過新的分叉限制這類交易，但最終獲得的礦工支持率卻遠不足以推動方案實施。如今，隨著 Luke Dashjr 遭撤職，爭議也從「比特幣是否應限制銘文」進一步延伸至開源治理的程序正當性，以及開發者在 BIP 流程中究竟擁有多大權限。

title: 1 美元就能建倉、 24 小時炒美股！Crypto.com 推出「代幣化股票」衍生品
summary:
加密貨幣交易所加速跨入傳統金融市場。Crypto.com 周三宣布，推出追蹤約  1,500 檔美股、ETF 的代幣化衍生品，而且只需 1 美元即可建倉，並支援 24 小時全天候交易。

〈1 美元就能建倉、 24 小時炒美股！Crypto.com 推出「代幣化股票」衍生品〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
加密貨幣交易所加速跨入傳統金融市場。 Crypto.com 周三宣布，推出追蹤約 1,500 檔美股、 ETF 的代幣化衍生品，讓符合資格的用戶能在平台上交易蘋果（Apple）、輝達（Nvidia）、特斯拉（Tesla）等熱門美股，以及 SPDR 黃金 ETF（GLD）、 iShares 白銀 ETF（SLV）等產品。
根據 Crypto.com 周三的聲明，歐洲經濟區（EEA）及其他獲准市場的合格用戶，現在可以透過平台直接參與傳統股市，而且只需 1 美元即可建倉，並支援 24 小時全天候交易。
合成曝險買賣靈活，底層資產交由美國券商託管
這些新產品是由 Foris Capital CY Limited 發行的衍生性商品，主要追蹤標的股票或 ETF 的價格表現。換言之，它們提供的是「合成曝險（Synthetic Exposure，指未實際持有資產，但透過衍生品獲得相同價格波動的投資方式）」：當蘋果股價上漲時，對應的代幣化產品也會同步走高，但持有者並不會因此成為蘋果的股東。
這意味著，買進這些代幣化衍生品的投資人，並不具備標的證券的合法所有權或受益權，自然也沒有投票權等股東權益。不過 Crypto.com 強調，投資人仍有機會獲得等同於現金股利的價格調整補償。至於支撐這些衍生品的底層資產，則統一交由美國合格券商 Alpaca 負責託管。
這項新業務的推展，歸功於 Crypto.com 在 2025 年 5 月成功收購 Foris Capital，讓該交易所順利取得《歐盟金融工具市場規則》（MiFID）牌照，獲准在歐洲發行受監管的金融產品。
根據數據平台 CoinGecko 統計，Crypto.com 目前為全球第 11 大加密貨幣交易所。
代幣化狂潮席捲，2030 年上看 5.5 兆美元
Crypto.com 這次新品上線，正值代幣化資產市場高速成長之際。根據 RWA.xyz 數據，代幣化股票總市值已達約 24.9 億美元，過去一年狂飆近 600% 。花旗集團（Citi）更樂觀預估，到了 2030 年，代幣化證券市場規模將膨脹至 5.5 兆美元，其中「代幣化股票」就將占據 2.6 兆美元。
放眼望去，Kraken 、 Bybit 、 Bitget 以及美國知名網路券商 Robinhood 等交易平台，都已搶先為美國以外的投資人推出代幣化股票產品。與此同時，美國證券集中保管結算公司（DTCC）已著手測試代幣化證券的底層基礎設施；就連那斯達克（Nasdaq）與紐約證券交易所（NYSE），也紛紛揭露了自家的資產代幣化藍圖。
不過，市場上的代幣化股票產品並非完全相同。 Crypto.com 這次推出的是合成型或衍生品模式，主要讓投資人追蹤股票價格表現，但不賦予股東身分；另一種則是發行方支持型（Issuer-Sponsored）模式，可將實際普通股上鏈，在完成代幣化的同時保留原有股票所有權及股東權利。
隨著代幣化證券一步步邁向金融主流，這兩種模式的優劣與適法性，也開始受監管機構及金融市場基礎設施業者高度關注。對交易所而言，如何把傳統股票的流動性帶上鏈只是第一步；如何同時處理證券所有權、投資人權利、託管與監管問題，才是真正決定代幣化技術能否被大規模採用的關鍵。

title: 美國電玩店驚見極稀有超級瑪利歐卡帶，8/14 起拍賣
summary: 美國威斯康辛州一家電玩店發現一批極其稀有的超級瑪利歐卡帶，14 日起拍賣。知名任天堂遊戲收藏家加諾斯指出，這些 […]
full_text:
美國威斯康辛州一家電玩店發現一批極其稀有的超級瑪利歐卡帶，14 日起拍賣。知名任天堂遊戲收藏家加諾斯指出，這些卡帶的保存狀態幾近完美，價值可能達數萬美元。
美聯社報導，威斯康辛州沃基夏（Waukesha）電玩店OneStopWonders店主布勞恩（Kevin Braun）幾年前告訴加諾斯（Jason Ganos），他有一箱塵封多年的超級瑪利歐（Super Mario）卡帶。這個消息讓加諾斯大吃一驚。
加諾斯指出，他們竟發現97個極為罕見、保存狀態堪稱完美無瑕的〈超級瑪利歐兄弟／打鴨子〉（Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt）遊戲卡帶，這款熱門的任天堂電玩卡帶是1988年發行。經過初步研究，加諾斯發現這批卡帶不僅是新版遊戲，生產日期也是已知最晚。
大部分卡帶將從14日起線上拍賣，持續至9月9日。
布勞恩當初聯絡加諾斯，是想請他協助賣掉一些東西，包括常見的任天堂遊戲與寶可夢卡。布勞恩回憶，這箱卡帶是從某顧客手中買來，對方家人原本打算當成廢金屬處理，但又認為不值什麼錢。
這批〈超級瑪利歐兄弟／打鴨子〉卡帶為1993年製，然而任天堂早於1991年就停售這款組合包。布勞恩與加諾斯仍不清楚這些卡帶為何生產，但推測可能是保固更換品，或原本是要與某家大型零售商合作推出的組合包，但最後沒有成案。
加諾斯帶著這些卡帶飛去加州，讓電玩遊戲專家鑑定和評級，以評估它們的價值。加諾斯表示，過去從未有遊戲卡帶在「專業運動認證機構」（Professional Sports Authenticator）電玩遊戲評級取得滿分10分，然而他手上97個卡帶，有五個獲滿分。
極稀有又具獨特生產歷史的電玩卡帶，收藏市場價格有時可達到六位數甚至七位數美元。不過加諾斯說，這批卡帶的最終價值難以預估，從幾百、幾千到幾萬美元都有可能。
（編譯：洪培英；圖片來源：PSA / Jason Ganos）

title: When do A-level results come out and what time does Ucas update?
summary: Your full guide to A-level results day, including what to do if you are not happy with your grades.
full_text:
When do A-level results come out and what time does Ucas update?
- Published
Hundreds of thousands of A-level students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland are waiting for their results.
They will be released at 08:00 BST on Thursday 13 August.
Those who have applied to university should be able to see whether they have been successful then too, as the Ucas Hub updates at the same time.
Here is everything you need to know about results, appeals and resits.
What are the 2026 A-level grade boundaries?
Each exam is graded on a scale from A* to E.
Grade boundaries show the minimum number of marks you need for each grade.
They are decided by assessment specialists at each exam board every year and are only published on results day.
Some exam boards, like AQA, external, have their old grade boundaries for previous years' exams published on their website.
How can I appeal against A-level results?
If you do not think your grade is right, you should first talk to your school or college.
It will contact the exam board on your behalf and ask for your marks to be reviewed.
If you still think you have been unfairly graded after a review, you can ask your school or college to appeal., external
The exam board will consider whether a correction is needed.
If you are still not satisfied, you can request a review from the exams regulator Ofqual.
What if I don't get the A-level grades I need for university or college?
If you only just miss out on the grades you need to get on to a university or college course, the admissions office might accept you anyway or offer you a place on a different course.
You could also try applying for a different place through the clearing process - see more details below.
It may also be possible to resit some or all of your exams. Talk to your school or college if you want to explore this route.
Resits will take place in May or June 2027.
What is Ucas university clearing?
The Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) runs a clearing process matching students with university and college courses which still have spaces., external
Students can use it if they:
- Fail to achieve the grades for their conditional offer
- Fail to receive any offers they want to accept
- Decide after 30 June to apply for university
- Achieve better grades than expected and want to change universities
Clearing opened on 2 July and closes on 19 October.
Universities make an offer to a student to join a course based on qualifications and grades or the Ucas tariff points system., external
Each A-level grade is worth a certain number of Ucas points. For example, an A* is worth 56 points and a D is worth 24 points.
Many students decide not to go to university and start an apprenticeship or go straight into work.
Others take a gap year, external so they have more time to decide what to do next.
When is results day in Scotland?
Scotland has a different qualification system, external. Students take Highers instead of A-levels.
Results day in Scotland this year was on Tuesday 4 August.

title: These seaside apartments were a ghost city - then police say scammers moved in
summary: Malaysia's Forest City was pitched as "paradise" but last month police raided it over alleged scam operations.
full_text:
These seaside apartments were a ghost city - then police say scammers moved in
- Published
From a distance, Malaysia's Forest City looks 3D-printed: a bristle of identical white blocks clustered on an otherwise unremarkable coastline.
When it was unveiled by Chinese developers in 2016, the $100bn mega-project was pitched as "a dream paradise for all mankind": a special financial zone that could house some 700,000 residents. But a decade later, this 14-sq-km (3,400-acre) artificial island on Singapore's doorstep is thought to be inhabited by less than 1% of that.
Rows of eerily vacant skyscrapers loom over quiet streets. Inside empty apartments, benchtops and windows are filmed with dust.
"In 2016 they described it here like the golden city; very, very beautiful," says Jason Deng, a 56-year-old investor who was among the first to buy in Forest City, paying "a lot of money" for five properties.
"If I had known it was not so good I would not have bought so many apartments," he says now. "I thought it would be much, much better."
As it turns out, this is only a golden city for some people – and they're not the ones developers had hoped to attract.
In mid-July, Malaysian police raided two alleged scam operations spread across 32 premises in Forest City, arresting 335 people and seizing assets worth about one million ringgit (£181,810; $245,000), including 313 computers, 1,557 mobile phones, 17 laptops and 10 modems.
From these two call centre hubs – one occupying 27 apartments across five storeys of a residential tower, the other spread between five bungalows – cryptocurrency syndicates ran investment and love scams targeting victims abroad, according to police.
Those arrested include 309 Chinese nationals, 19 Indonesians, three Malaysians and four Myanmar nationals. Johor police chief Ab Rahaman Arsad said authorities were working with Interpol to track down the mastermind behind the operations.
The BBC reached out to Forest City and Johor police for comment, but did not receive a response.
Experts and locals tell the BBC this is likely to be the tip of the iceberg – and a symptom of a global scam industry that is spreading, evolving, and professionalising.
"The reality is that many of these organisations now resemble multinational corporations more than a traditional organised crime network or gang," says John Wojcik, an analyst at TRM Labs, which investigates crypto-facilitated crime. "They have dedicated recruitment teams, IT departments, money-laundering specialists and infrastructure."
Authorities and experts agree that the Forest City operations were probably staffed by criminals who had been driven out of Cambodia, a global nerve centre for transnational scams.
Over the past five years, this criminal sector has ballooned into a multi-billion-dollar industry, built on the forced labour of brutalised trafficking victims who work under threat of torture and abuse.
Since late last year, the Cambodian government has stepped up efforts to stamp out these operations. Authorities recently estimated that 300,000 people had left the country within a few months as raids on industrial-scale compounds intensified.
But these Malaysian offshoots do not appear to have been scam "compounds" in the traditional sense.
Compared to more infamous walled complexes in places like Sihanoukville or the Myanmar borderlands, the alleged scam hubs in Forest City appear almost white collar, reportedly staffed by local residents and sitting wall-to-wall with the homes of unsuspecting neighbours.
Kevin, a tenant who also works in property sales for Forest City, believes scammers are still operating in "condominiums or serviced apartments" in the complex. He asked for his name to be changed for fear of repercussions.
"We know what they're doing," he says. "This is actually a very common issue in Johor city and Kuala Lumpur, but especially in Forest City. Forest City is very special."
Part of what makes Forest City "special", according to Kevin, Wojcik and others, is the very thing that has gained it so much notoriety: its reputation as a semi-abandoned "ghost city".
"When we speak to clients or customers, the company teaches us to say 'we already have 23,000 residents living in this area'," says Kevin – but the reality, he quietly adds, is there are "less than 5,000".
"That's the reason" scammers have chosen Forest City to set up shop, he suggests.
"They have their own privacy... Nobody comes here."
There are several factors which precipitated what many see as the downfall of Forest City.
Spearheaded by Country Garden, one of China's largest property developers, and Danga 88, a private company controlled by Malaysian Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar, the project was initially dreamed up as an eco-friendly metropolis for well-heeled Chinese clients. Featuring a high-end hotel, golf course and water park, the resort-style city's seafront offices and apartments were expected to be in high demand.
But the combined weight of the Covid pandemic, China's spiralling property slump and constricted borrowing limits for its citizens have sunk those sky-high ambitions, and all but ground the project to a standstill.
The lights are still on, but almost no-one is home.
And that appears to have made the complex a honeypot for scammers.
"Forest City reflects the conditions organised crime have been targeting for years - a flagship location marketed as a prestigious, luxury, master-planned smart city that never came close to fulfilling that vision," Wojcik says.
"Developments like this offer precisely what these syndicates look for: modern infrastructure, large numbers of vacant properties, and international connectivity all wrapped around the veneer of legitimate economic activity to ensure that the criminal nature of what goes on inside remains unnoticed."
With this in mind, the glittering facade of Forest City echoes a more infamous metropolis 1,800 kilometres (1,120 miles) to the north: Shwe Kokko, the so-called resort city on Myanmar's Thai border, which is one of the world's most notorious scam hubs.
Built by the private Chinese conglomerate Yatai, Shwe Kokko markets itself as a safe holiday destination for Chinese tourists and a haven for the super-rich. But behind its tree-lined streets and luxury villas is a nexus of fraud, money-laundering and human trafficking.
For all its headwinds, and despite the fact that only 15 to 20% of the originally proposed project has been completed, Forest City similarly still markets itself as an up-and-coming hotbed for property investment, tech innovation and tax-free business ventures.
Such entrepreneurial packaging serves as a Trojan horse for scammers wanting to set up shop without drawing unwanted attention – and allows them to perpetrate their fraud more effectively.
Wojcik explains that "when scam syndicates can embed themselves behind seemingly legitimate businesses in ordinary commercial developments, they not only become more difficult to detect and disrupt, they become capable of exerting serious amounts of power and influence through the massive profits they generate".
This power and influence in turn allows scammers to professionalise in other ways.
Though human trafficking still largely fuels much of the scam industry's labour force, there is now a noticeable trend of syndicate operators recruiting and retaining experienced scammers with higher pay and better working conditions.
Meanwhile, in the same Telegram groups where scam jobs are being advertised, career scammers are also now posting detailed resumes, outlining their experience in fraudulent activities and emphasising their eagerness to work.
"It's a sign the industry is maturing into a more professionalised criminal enterprise," Wojcik explains, "while coercion and exploitation still remain widespread".
The Forest City raids highlight a transnational scam industry that is shifting in size and shape. But this is far from the first time such operations have been detected in Malaysia.

title: Gavin & Stacey star Melanie Walters completes Strictly line-up
summary: Walters, who played Gwen in the BBC sitcom, is the 15th and final celebrity to be announced for Strictly.
full_text:
Gavin & Stacey star Melanie Walters completes Strictly line-up
- Published
Gavin & Stacey star Melanie Walters has become the 15th and final celebrity to be announced for the line-up of Strictly Come Dancing 2026.
Walters has played mild-mannered, omelette-obsessed Gwen West in the BBC comedy since 2007, including the finale broadcast at Christmas in 2024.
In a statement, Walters said: "Performing in pantomime for the last 15 years, my Strictly 'fix' has always been watching in a dressing room rather than my front room.
"This year I am completely thrilled and happy to swap my fairy wand for sequinned dance shoes."
She added: "I just hope I don't follow Cinderella and leave one on the Ballroom stairs. I cannot wait to take part in this absolutely iconic show, it's so exciting. See you in September!"
Walters is also known for roles in Coronation Street, Beyond Paradise, Doc Martin, Being Human, Death Valley and Hollyoaks.
Her film credits include High Tide and Save the Cinema, while she has also appeared in stage productions such as Blood Brothers, Twelfth Night and Educating Rita.
All 15 celebrity contestants have now been confirmed for Strictly Come Dancing - see the full line-up below:
John Nellis
Football content creator John Nellis has more than 20 million followers across social media.
He has amassed billions of views for his videos featuring global soccer stars such as Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi.
The former air traffic controller said he was "a little nervous" because he has never danced before, but is hoping to be "much better at family parties by the end of it".
Tabby Stoecker
Team GB skeleton racer Tabby Stoecker won gold at the 2026 Winter Olympic Games, and is also a World Cup race winner, a double World Championship medallist and a European Championship medallist.
She only made her international debut in the sport five years ago.
When her participation was announced, Stoecker said she was "over the moon" to be joining this year's Strictly cast.
"I've had the wildest year of my life so far," she continued, "so to be rounding it off with a childhood dream of dancing in the Strictly ballroom is surreal and I can't wait to get stuck in!"
Lawrence Robb
Emmerdale actor Lawrence Robb has played Mackenzie 'Mack' Boyd in the ITV soap since 2020.
His other credits include appearing opposite Billie Piper in I Hate Suzie and in stage productions such as Legally Blonde The Musical.
In a statement, the actor joked: "I don't know who's more excited about this, me or my mother.
"I can't quite believe that I am going to be getting my dancing shoes on this September on one of my favourite shows of all time."
He added: "It's a dream come true, and I can't wait to bring my all to ballroom. Wish me luck, and any advice is very welcome - trust me I'll need it!"
Graeme Hall
Known as the Dogfather, Graeme Hall has appeared on Channel 5's Dog's Behaving (Very) Badly since the show's launch in 2017.
The presenter and dog trainer has also fronted The Dog Hospital and contributed to BBC radio programmes, ITV's This Morning, and wrote a regular column for the Times.
"I can't believe I am joining the cast of Strictly for 2026," Hall said. "I have always loved dancing, so to have the opportunity to learn from the best in the business is a dream come true.
"I have watched the show for years, so to be a part of it feels like a very exciting challenge, albeit more than a bit nerve-wracking! I can't wait to get started. Bring it on!"
Hall has also written books including The Ultimate Kid's Guide to Dogs and previously made a cameo appearance in the hit drama All Creatures Great and Small.
Shaun Wright-Phillips
Other celebrities to be confirmed for Strictly this year include former England and Manchester City winger Shaun Wright-Phillips.
The football pundit, who is the son of Arsenal legend Ian Wright, had 36 caps for England and also played for clubs including Chelsea and Queens Park Rangers.
His fancy footwork may have dazzled on the pitch but Wright-Phillips said this latest challenge "is definitely outside my comfort zone".
"Dancing is in my blood - but mainly at family events!" he said. "I'm super excited to get started and really looking forward to the challenge!"
While ex-footballers have had mixed fortunes on previous Strictly series, former soccer star Karen Carney flipped the script last year by winning the coveted glitterball.
Bethany Anthony
Antonia has portrayed dragon-rider Lady Baela Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel since 2022. She is currently starring as Eurydice in the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown in London's West End.
Her acting career began when she was 14 when she appeared in a short film adaptation of The Tempest, before being cast as a guest role in the BBC's Doctors.
The singer and actress has also appeared in series including Nolly, Stay Close, Stath Lets Flats, and Doctor Who.
Antonia said: "I can't quite believe that I will be heading to the Strictly ballroom this September! I have grown up watching Strictly, and I am so excited to take the challenge on and (hopefully!) learn a new skill. See you on the dancefloor!"
Jaime Winstone
Jaime Winstone launched her acting career in 2004 and her film credits include Bullet Boy, Tomb Raider and Wild Bill, as well stage productions such as 2:22 A Ghost Story.
The actress, who also won acclaim for her portrayal of Barbara Windsor in the BBC biopic Babs, said she was "so excited" to be joining the dance competition.
The actress said in a statement she was "no stranger to a dance floor", but added that ballroom is "a whole new world for me".
"I love a challenge though," she continued, "so can't wait to enter my showgirl era and get super sparkly!"
Winstone has also appeared in TV series such as Poirot, Dead Set, Torvill & Dean, Mad Dogs, Count Abdulla and Four Lives.
After playing Windsor in Babs, Winstone stepped into the late actress's famous role of Peggy Mitchell in EastEnders, appearing in flashback specials, most recently in the soap's 40th anniversary last year.
Dame Sarah Storey
Known as Great Britain's most successful Paralympian of all time, Dame Sarah Storey has secured 19 gold medals across the nine Paralympic Games she competed in.
The swimmer and cyclist said embarking on the challenge is "hugely exciting" and she "can't wait to get started".
"I have always loved watching Strictly and my daughter Louisa is a very talented dancer, so to be able to learn from the best and hopefully understand even more about her world, is incredibly motivating!" she said.
The former athlete won four golds at London 2012. She started her career as a swimmer and later switched to cycling, winning 30 Paralympic medals in total.
Will Best
Best is known for hosting Big Brother with AJ Odudu on ITV since 2023, and as host of the Hits Radio Breakfast Show alongside Fleur East and James Barr.
He said it was "an absolute dream" to be taking to the BBC One contest's dance floor in September, "albeit a pretty terrifying one".
Best added: "I've been lucky to do lots of live telly before, but absolutely nothing like this. And I cannot wait!
"I have no idea if I can actually dance, but bring on the sequins, bring on the quicksteps, bring on the dance floor! I'm going to try to enjoy every minute of it."
Cach Mercer
Mercer was part of the winning couple on ITV dating show Love Island last year, and also works as a model and DJ, and is an ambassador for a young people's mental health charity.
"I have grown up watching the show with my family and am so excited to now be part of the cast," he said.
Mercer also showcases his Afrobeat, hip-hop and street dance moves on his social media accounts.
"Dancing is a huge passion of mine and I can't wait to learn ballroom and do the foxtrot for the first time!" he added.
Delta Goodrem
Delta Goodrem is also part of this year's celebrity list, with the Australian singer and actress becoming the third celebrity to be announced for the upcoming series.

title: Wisconsin result halts winning streak for Democratic Party's left wing
summary: Centrist David Crowley is projected to have beaten democratic socialist Francesca Hong, breaking a recent nationwide trend.
full_text:
Wisconsin result halts winning streak for Democratic Party's left wing
- Published
David Crowley is projected to have won a primary election to become the Democrat's candidate for Wisconsin governor, in a surprise result that halts a winning streak for the party's left wing.
With almost all votes counted in the Midwestern state, Crowley, the more centrist candidate, has secured a narrow victory over Francesca Hong, according to a projection made early on Wednesday by the BBC's partner, CBS News.
Anti-establishment Democrats had previously recorded wins across the US that had rattled the party leadership in Washington. Many pundits expected Hong to continue that trend.
Crowley will now face off in November against Tom Tiffany, who easily won the equivalent Republican contest.
Crowley, the chief executive officer of the state's Milwaukee County, posted on X to say it was time to "get to work".
He reiterated that his missions were "making life more affordable, strengthening our schools, creating good-paying jobs, and making sure opportunity reaches every corner of our state".
Tiffany, meanwhile, currently serves as a US congressman and has the backing of US President Donald Trump.
He has also emphasised affordability issues, running on a platform that includes lowering taxes, supporting farmers and improving healthcare.
The state's political matchups are expected to be closely fought during November's midterm elections, which have also wider implications for the control of the US Congress.
The Hong-Crowley contest was just one of several that were held across the state and neighbouring Minnesota across Tuesday.
Meanwhile, in South Carolina, Darline Graham Nordone advanced to a run-off vote later this month in a special Republican primary for the US Senate which was held following the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham.
She will face off against Democrat Annie Andrews to fill the vacant seat.
Crowley's late surge in Wisconsin was all the more unexpected to many observers, given that he briefly dropped his bid last month in order to support a rival.
He later re-entered the race with the backing of Tony Evers, the state's current governor.
Hong, a Wisconsin state assemblywoman, a single mother and a former chef, was believed by many observers to be the frontrunner as she entered election day in what proved to be a crowded Democratic primary.
She aimed to become the first democratic socialist to govern the state. However, some of her historical comments raised questions about whether she could have beaten her Republican opponent.
Hong faced particular scrutiny for remarks about police funding and the US Thanksgiving holiday - some of which she later walked back.
Prominent left-wing politicians Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders and New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who both often endorse insurgent candidates such as Hong, notably stayed out of this race.
AP News reported that Hong had conceded the race to Crowley, and that her campaign manager had said Hong was "proud of the race we ran".
Hong's defeat brings to an end a series of wins for left-wing candidates in Democratic primaries.
Some of the successful candidates been endorsed by, or affiliated with, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) organisation.
They have gained traction with voters not just by running against Republican policies, but by challenging the Democratic status quo in Washington set by the party's current leaders.
They have also found traction by demanding the US end or curtail funding to Israel, due to its ongoing military operation in Gaza.
Last week, for example, Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic primary for Michigan's US Senate seat, beating Congresswoman Haley Stevens.
And in June, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani endorsed a trio of progressive Democrats in the regions' US House races, all of whom won their primaries.
Mamdani's picks unseated two sitting lawmakers and beating the hand-picked successor of a retiring congresswoman.
Additional reporting by Kayla Epstein and Sareen Habeshian

title: Pogba suffers new injury setback with Monaco future now in doubt
summary: Former France and Manchester United star Paul Pogba suffers latest injury setback, sparking rumours about Monaco future.
full_text:
Pogba suffers new injury setback with Monaco future now in doubt
Former France and Manchester United star Paul Pogba suffers latest injury setback, sparking rumours about his future with Monaco.
Paul Pogba’s future with Monaco could be in doubt after he suffered another injury setback.
The former Manchester United and Juventus midfielder suffered a new injury to his left thigh on Tuesday during the first day of Monaco’s training camp in England.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo marries long-term partner in Portugal
- list 2 of 4Poland says Women’s World Cup plan on course despite UEFA boycott of FIFA
- list 3 of 4Bangladesh and India battle to save cricket series after political turmoil
- list 4 of 4Palestinian club football to restart in September after Gaza war suspension
The 2018 French World Cup winner suffered the injury as the Ligue 1 club trained at the English national football centre at St George’s Park after beating Liverpool in a friendly on Sunday.
The 33-year-old midfielder was only returning to group training after a long spell of right-knee problems.
Pogba has played only one half of football for Monaco in this preseason.
According to several sources close to the matter, the new injury shows Pogba is some way off the level of fitness required to begin the French league season.
There has been widespread speculation that Monaco have begun talks with Pogba’s representatives about buying the player out of the remainder of his contract, which is set to expire at the end of the new season.
After serving 18 months of a four-year ban for doping, Pogba played just six Ligue 1 matches for Monaco last season, totalling 115 minutes on the pitch.
Pogba started his career with United in the English Premier League before the manager at the time, Sir Alex Ferguson, released the midfielder on a free transfer in 2012 after a dispute with the player’s agent.
Juventus stepped in for the then 19-year-old, and he won four consecutive Serie A titles with them and reached the Champions League final before re-joining United in 2016 for a world record transfer fee at the time of $120.2m.
He returned to Juventus on another free transfer in 2022 before his release in 2024, during his ban. Monaco stepped in to hand the Seine-et-Marne-born player his first taste of senior football in his home country in 2025.
Pogba’s last appearance for France came in 2022, in a 5-0 victory over South Africa in an international friendly. It was the last of his 91 caps, during which he scored 11 goals for the team.
His World Cup-winning moment came with France when they defeated Croatia 4-2 in the final of the Russia 2018 tournament, with Pogba scoring his side’s third goal.

title: Rybakina defeats Osaka, advances to Canadian Open semifinals to play Gauff
summary: Elena Rybakina stages a huge comeback to beat Naomi Osaka and will now play Coco Gauff for a place in the final.
full_text:
Rybakina defeats Osaka, advances to Canadian Open semifinals to play Gauff
Elena Rybakina stages a huge comeback to beat Naomi Osaka and will now play Coco Gauff for a place in the final.
Second-seeded Elena Rybakina fought back from a set and a break down to prevail 4-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 in her Canadian Open quarterfinal against Naomi Osaka in Toronto on Tuesday.
Rybakina, the 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 Australian Open champion, will meet fourth-seeded Coco Gauff for a place in the final after the American’s opponent, Belinda Bencic, withdrew due to a hip injury.
